ProgramName: Master of Advanced Architectural Design
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Master of Advanced Architectural Design (MAAD) program, applicants must hold a professional degree in architecture (Bachelor of Architecture or Master of Architecture) from an accredited program in the U.S. or an international equivalent. Required application materials include a digital portfolio of design work, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, three letters of recommendation, transcripts, and a curriculum vitae (CV) or resume. A minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 is required.
Concentration: Digital Design and Manufacturing; Health and Built Environment; History, Theory and Society; Informal Urbanism; Sustainable Design; Urban Design
Description: The Master of Advanced Architectural Design (MAAD) is a post-professional degree program for students who already hold a professional Bachelor of Architecture (BArch) or Master of Architecture (MArch) degree. The program provides the opportunity for students to pursue specialized research and design in a variety of areas. This two-semester program is intended for individuals who want to develop a specific design or research interest through further study. Successful applicants will have an interest in a particular area of architectural research or design and will have articulated a clear focus for their work. The program is specifically designed to allow students to take advantage of the faculty’s expertise in a wide range of fields.
Accredidation: The Master of Advanced Architectural Design (MAAD) is a post-professional degree and is not accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB).

ProgramName: Master of Advanced Study in Engineering
Requirements: Minimum requirements for admission to graduate study at UC Berkeley: A bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution; A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. In addition to the University’s requirements, applicants must provide: 3 letters of recommendation, Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Resume, Official Transcripts, and Evidence of English language proficiency.
Concentration: Aerospace Engineering, Integrated Circuit Design
Description: The Master of Advanced Study (MAS) is a professional master’s degree program for students who have already completed an undergraduate degree in engineering or a related field, and who are looking to advance their careers. These programs provide a deep technical foundation in a specific area of engineering, while also developing leadership and management skills.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in African American Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Ph.D. program in African American Studies, applicants must submit an online application and provide the following materials: an application fee ($135 for US citizens/permanent residents; $155 for all others), Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Curriculum Vitae (CV), a Writing Sample (must be double-spaced and no more than 30 pages), three letters of recommendation, and transcripts from each college or university attended. International applicants must also demonstrate English Language Proficiency via the TOEFL or IELTS. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required.
Description: The doctoral program is designed to provide students with the research and teaching skills to examine the experiences of people of African descent and the social and cultural forces that shape those experiences. It is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the African Diaspora in its historical and contemporary dimensions. Students are expected to master a body of knowledge in African American and African Diaspora Studies and to develop a disciplinary or multi-disciplinary concentration. The program consists of coursework, a qualifying examination, and a dissertation.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), and Graduate Student Researchers (GSR)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in African American Studies
Requirements: The Department of African American Studies at UC Berkeley offers a program of study leading to the Ph.D. degree (a terminal Master of Arts is not offered). Application requirements include a statement of purpose, personal statement, three letters of recommendation, a current resume or curriculum vitae, a writing sample (one, maximum of 25 pages), and transcripts. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 is required. The GRE General Test is not required.
Description: The Department of African American Studies offers a program of graduate study leading to the MA and PhD degrees. Our graduate program is based on a multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary approach to the study of the history, culture, and society of Black people in the United States, the Caribbean, and the African diaspora. We invite applications from students who have already earned the BA or an equivalent degree. We also welcome applications from students who have already completed the MA in African American Studies or related fields for admission to the PhD program. Students should indicate on the application whether they are applying for the MA or the PhD. Students admitted for the MA may apply for the PhD program at the end of their second year. All students in the MA/PhD program are required to demonstrate competence in a language other than English.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructor (GSI) positions, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) positions

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Agricultural and Resource Economics
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0 is required. Application requirements include the submission of GRE General Test scores, three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and a current resume or curriculum vitae. International applicants whose native language is not English must also fulfill the English Language Proficiency requirement via the TOEFL or IELTS exam.
Description: The Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ARE) offers a program of academic study leading to the PhD degree. The PhD program is designed to prepare students for careers in research, teaching, and government service. It provides a strong foundation in economic theory and quantitative methods and encourages students to apply these tools to problems in agricultural, environmental, and resource economics, and international development. Students are encouraged to develop their own research interests early in the program and to work closely with faculty members on research projects.

ProgramName: Master of Analytics
Requirements: To be eligible for the Master of Analytics, applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution with a minimum GPA of 3.0. Required prerequisites include Linear Algebra, Calculus, Probability and Statistics, and Computer Programming (Python is preferred). The application requires a Resume or CV, Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, official transcripts, and three letters of recommendation. GRE/GMAT scores are not required. International applicants must meet English language proficiency requirements (TOEFL or IELTS).
Concentration: Analytics
Description: The Master of Analytics program at UC Berkeley is designed for individuals who want to lead the way in using data to make better decisions. The program provides students with a strong foundation in the mathematical and computational tools of analytics, as well as the practical skills needed to apply these tools to real-world problems. The program is offered by the Department of Industrial Engineering & Operations Research (IEOR) and is designed for students with a strong quantitative background who are looking to pursue careers as data scientists, analysts, or consultants in industry, government, or non-profit sectors.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Ancient History and Mediterranean Archaeology
Requirements: The Graduate Group in Ancient History and Mediterranean Archaeology (AHMA) at the University of California, Berkeley offers an interdisciplinary program leading to the PhD degree. It is composed of 30 faculty members from eight different Berkeley departments: Anthropology, Classics, History, History of Art, Near Eastern Studies, Italian Studies, Rhetoric and Philosophy. Applicants are expected to have a strong foundation in at least one of the fields of study represented in the Graduate Group and to have begun the study of the necessary ancient and modern languages. A minimum GPA of 3.0 is required for admission to the University of California, Berkeley.
Description: Ancient History and Mediterranean Archaeology (AHMA) is an interdepartmental program that offers a course of study leading to the PhD degree. The group is composed of more than thirty faculty members from the following departments: Anthropology, Art History, Classics, History, Middle Eastern Languages and Cultures, and Philosophy. The program provides students with a broad background in the history and archaeology of the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern worlds, and offers specialized training in various disciplines and sub-fields.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Anthropology
Requirements: The minimum graduate admission requirements are: (1) A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; (2) A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and (3) Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. In addition to the University’s minimum requirements, the department requires: Three letters of recommendation, Personal Statement, Statement of Purpose, Current CV, and a Writing sample (1 required, 2 maximum).
Concentration: Archaeology, Biological Anthropology, Sociocultural Anthropology, Medical Anthropology (joint with UCSF)
Description: The Department of Anthropology offers a doctoral program in the standard subfields of the discipline—archaeology, biological anthropology, and sociocultural anthropology. In addition, there is a joint program with the University of California, San Francisco, in medical anthropology. Students in the Berkeley program have the opportunity to participate in a variety of interdisciplinary concentrations as well as in the programs of several centers and institutes.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Applied Mathematics
Requirements: Applicants for the doctoral program should have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A strong background in mathematics is necessary. We normally require at least 15 semester units of upper-division mathematics, including at least one year of analysis (e.g., MATH 104 and MATH 105) and one semester of linear algebra (e.g., MATH 110).
Description: Applied Mathematics at Berkeley has a long history. Since its beginnings, the Applied Mathematics program has focused on the creation and analysis of mathematical modeling for the physical and biological sciences and for engineering. Today the program encompasses a wide range of research in numerical analysis, scientific computing, partial differential equations, and many others. The PhD in Applied Mathematics is a program of the Department of Mathematics. Many of the requirements for the Applied Mathematics PhD program are the same as those for the Mathematics PhD program. However, the programs also have several significant differences. For example, students in Applied Mathematics must take at least two graduate courses in some field of application (such as physics, engineering, or biology).
ScholarshipAmount: Full funding (tuition and stipend) is typically provided for PhD students
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), and Research Assistantships (GSR)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Applied Science and Technology
Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution and have a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0. Required application materials include unofficial transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and a resume/CV. The GRE General Test is not required and will not be considered for this program.
Concentration: Applied Physics, Biophysics, Chemistry and Chemical Biology, Mathematical Sciences, and Nanotechnology
Description: The Applied Science & Technology (AS&T) Graduate Group offers an interdisciplinary program of study and research leading to the doctor of philosophy degree. The program is designed for students with strong backgrounds in physical science, mathematics and engineering who want to pursue research in areas that span multiple disciplines. AS&T research areas include: applied physics; biophysics; chemistry and chemical biology; mathematical sciences; and nanotechnology.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Research Assistantships, and Teaching Assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Architecture
Requirements: The minimum graduate admission requirements are: (1) A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; (2) A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and (3) Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. Application materials include three letters of recommendation, a portfolio of design work, and a Personal History Statement.
Concentration: Building Science, Technology and Sustainability; History, Theory and Society; Design Theories, Methods and Practices; Architecture of Life and Living
Description: The Master of Architecture program is a professional degree accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB). The program is intended for students who plan to practice architecture and who have already earned a four-year non-professional bachelor's degree in architecture or a bachelor's degree in a field other than architecture. Students who have completed a professional Bachelor of Architecture degree from an NAAB-accredited (or equivalent) program are not eligible for the M.Arch degree.
Accredidation: Accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB)
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Master of Science in Architecture
Requirements: Admission requirements for the Master of Science (MS) in Architecture include a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, a Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV), three letters of recommendation, and official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. Additionally, a writing sample is required for all MS applicants, while a portfolio is considered optional. The GRE is not required for admission. Applicants must have a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0.
Concentration: Building Science, Technology and Sustainability; History, Theory and Society
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) in Architecture is a non-professional degree for those who wish to pursue advanced research in a specific area of architectural inquiry. This program is intended for students who already hold a professional degree in architecture (Bachelor of Architecture or Master of Architecture) or a related field, and who wish to develop a specialized focus. The M.S. degree does not lead to licensure as an architect. Research in the MS and PhD programs is generally organized into two areas of study: Building Science, Technology and Sustainability (BSTS) and History, Theory and Society (HTS).
ScholarshipType: Departmental fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSIs), and Readerships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Architecture
Requirements: To apply for the Ph.D. in Architecture, applicants must submit the UC Berkeley Graduate Division online application, which includes an application fee, official transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, a personal history statement, and a resume or curriculum vitae. A writing sample is specifically required for Ph.D. applicants. The GRE is not required for this program.
Concentration: Building Science, Technology and Sustainability; History, Theory and Society
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Architecture is a research-oriented degree appropriate for those who wish to pursue a career in teaching and scholarship in architecture and its related areas, or in roles in government or professional consultation which require depth in specialization and experience in research. This degree is intended to provide a student with a foundation of theoretical and methodological knowledge, and an opportunity to engage in advanced research in a specialized area of study.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructor (GSI) positions, and Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) positions

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Art Practice
Requirements: Applicants must hold a Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must have completed a minimum of 18 semester units of upper division studio art courses. The Graduate Division requires a minimum grade point average of 3.0. Applicants are expected to have a broad knowledge of art history and be prepared to participate in a demanding program of work and study. A portfolio of work is a major part of the application.
Description: The MFA program in the Department of Art Practice at UC Berkeley is a two-year, small, and intensive program. Each year, roughly six to seven students are admitted into the program. MFA students are provided with individual studios at the Richmond Field Station and are expected to develop their work across multiple disciplines. Our world-renowned faculty work closely with students throughout their time in the program. The UC Berkeley MFA program culminates in a museum exhibition at the Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive (BAMPFA). MFA students are provided with large, individual studios at the Richmond Field Station (RFS), a 15-minute shuttle ride from the main campus. These studios provide students with the space and privacy to develop their work over the course of the two-year program. This exhibition is a highlight of the program and provides students with the opportunity to show their work in a professional museum setting.
ScholarshipType: Departmental MFA Fellowships, Regents’ Fellowship, Chancellor’s Fellowship, Foreign Language Area Studies (FLAS) Fellowships, UC Berkeley Berkeley Center for New Media (BCNM) fellowships

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Asian Studies
Requirements: The Group in Asian Studies welcomes applications for the M.A. degree from students with strong backgrounds in an Asian language and in the social sciences or humanities. Requirements for admission include: A Bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A GPA of 3.0 or better (on a 4.0 scale) in the last two years of undergraduate study. Demonstrated proficiency in an Asian language (usually at least two years of college-level study or equivalent). Three letters of recommendation. Statement of Purpose. Personal History Statement. CV. Writing Sample. TOEFL or IELTS scores for international applicants.
Concentration: East Asian Studies, South Asian Studies, Southeast Asian Studies
Description: The Group in Asian Studies (GAS) offers a multi-disciplinary MA program that is designed for students who want to develop a broad knowledge of Asia and who may wish to pursue a career in the private or public sector, or to prepare for further graduate study. The program provides students with the opportunity to take courses in many different departments and to work with faculty from across the university.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships (FLAS, Graduate Division, Departmental)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Asian Studies
Requirements: The PhD program in South & Southeast Asian Studies is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the languages, literatures, and cultures of South and Southeast Asia. The program is flexible and allows students to pursue a variety of research interests, including linguistics, literature, religion, philosophy, and history. Minimum requirements for admission include a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum GPA of 3.0.
Department: College of Letters & Science / Department of South & Southeast Asian Studies
Concentration: South Asian Studies, Southeast Asian Studies
Description: The Department of South & Southeast Asian Studies offers programs of graduate study and research leading to the Master of Arts and Doctor of Philosophy degrees. The PhD program is designed to provide students with a high degree of specialized training in a particular field of South or Southeast Asian studies. Students are expected to become proficient in at least one of the major languages of the area and to acquire a thorough understanding of the history, culture, and literature of the region.
ScholarshipAmount: Full funding (stipend, tuition, and health insurance)
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Multi-year funding packages, fellowships, and teaching assistantships)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Astronomy
Requirements: The minimum graduate admission requirements are: A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. Background in physics and mathematics is required.
Description: The goal of the graduate program in astronomy is to provide students with a broad knowledge of modern observational and theoretical astrophysics, as well as an opportunity to perform research at the forefront of the field. The department's research activities include the study of the solar system, stars, and the interstellar medium; the formation and evolution of galaxies; the large-scale structure of the universe; and the big bang.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Research Assistantships, Teaching Assistantships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Astrophysics
Requirements: The Department of Astronomy offers a program of graduate study leading to the degree of Doctor of Philosophy in Astrophysics. The program is designed to provide students with a broad knowledge of modern astrophysics and the techniques of astronomical research. Admission requirements include the Graduate Division Application, Transcript(s), Letters of Recommendation (3), Statement of Purpose, and Personal History Statement.
Description: The Department of Astronomy offers a graduate program leading to the PhD degree in astrophysics. The primary objective of the graduate program is to train students for a career in research and teaching. This is accomplished through a series of core courses and an early introduction to research. Students are expected to start on a research project during their first year of study, often with one of the observational or theoretical projects currently being pursued by members of the faculty. Members of the faculty are also involved in several interdisciplinary organizations, including the Center for Particle Astrophysics, the Space Sciences Laboratory, and the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR), Graduate Student Instructor (GSI)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Bioengineering
Description: The Department of Bioengineering at the University of California, Berkeley, and the Department of Bioengineering and Therapeutic Sciences at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF), offer a joint graduate program in bioengineering. The program provides students with a solid foundation in the engineering and biological sciences and offers opportunities for research in a wide range of areas. The program offers a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) and a Master of Science (MS) in Bioengineering. The MS degree is typically earned by students who are already enrolled in the PhD program.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Bioengineering
Requirements: The PhD in Bioengineering is a joint program offered by UC Berkeley and UC San Francisco (UCSF). Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 is required. Required application materials include a Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, three letters of recommendation, and transcripts. The GRE General Test is not required for this program.
Description: The bioengineering graduate program is a joint program between the UC Berkeley and UC San Francisco (UCSF) campuses. Students in the program take classes at both campuses and may have research advisors at either campus. This unique program gives students the opportunity to learn from and conduct research with world-class faculty from two of the world’s leading universities in the fields of engineering, the biological sciences, and healthcare.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) positions

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Biostatistics
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution with a satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B). For the MA in Biostatistics, prerequisites include multivariable calculus (equivalent to Berkeley's Math 53) and linear algebra (equivalent to Berkeley's Math 54). Students are expected to have a strong background in mathematics.
Description: The MA and PhD in biostatistics are offered by the Interdepartmental Group in Biostatistics. This program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the development and application of statistical methods in the biological and health sciences. The MA degree is designed for students who are interested in careers as biostatisticians in public health, the pharmaceutical industry, or other health-related fields. The program also provides a strong foundation for students who wish to pursue a PhD in biostatistics or a related field.
Accredidation: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Biostatistics
Requirements: The PhD in Biostatistics is offered by the Interdepartmental Graduate Group in Biostatistics. It is intended for students with a background in mathematics and/or statistics who have a strong interest in biological and health sciences. Admission to the PhD program is based on a review of the applicant’s academic record, letters of recommendation, and personal statements. Applicants must have a strong background in mathematics and/or statistics.
Description: The Graduate Group in Biostatistics offers programs of study leading to the MA and PhD degrees. These programs are designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the development and application of statistical and computational methods for the study of biological and health sciences. Students are trained to collaborate with researchers in a variety of fields and to contribute to the advancement of knowledge in public health and medicine.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Research Assistantships (GSR), Teaching Assistantships (GSI)

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration
Requirements: Admission to the Full-time MBA Program is based on a combination of academic achievement, professional experience, and leadership potential. The GMAT or GRE is required for all applicants. Applicants must have a bachelor's degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution. Professional experience is not required but is strongly recommended.
Description: The Haas School of Business offers the Master of Business Administration (MBA) degree. The program is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of the fundamentals of business, while also allowing them to tailor their education to their specific interests and career goals. The curriculum is built on a foundation of 12 required courses that provide a comprehensive look at business basics. Students can then choose from a wide range of elective courses to customize their education.
Accredidation: The Haas School of Business is accredited by AACSB International (Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Business Administration
Requirements: The PhD Program application process is online. Required materials include a current resume or curriculum vitae, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, three letters of recommendation, official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, valid GMAT or GRE scores, and TOEFL or IELTS scores for international applicants. A nonrefundable application fee is also required.
Concentration: Accounting, Business and Public Policy, Finance, Marketing, Management of Organizations (Micro and Macro), Real Estate, Operations and Information Technology Management, and Strategy
Description: The Berkeley PhD Program in Business Administration offers students the opportunity to learn from and work with some of the world's leading scholars in their fields. The program's goal is to prepare students for careers in research and teaching at the world's top universities and research institutions. The PhD program is small and highly selective, with about 15-18 students entering each year. Because of the small size, students are able to work closely with faculty members in a collaborative and intellectually stimulating environment.
ScholarshipType: Fellowship, Research Assistantship, Teaching Assistantship

ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: The M.S. and Ph.D. programs in Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering are designed to develop each student’s ability to conduct independent creative research. While the Ph.D. is the department’s primary emphasis, the M.S. degree is also offered. Minimum requirements for admission include a bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; a satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field.
Description: The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering (CBE) offers a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Chemical Engineering and a Master of Science (MS) in Chemical Engineering. Students have the opportunity to move into new and exciting research areas in chemical engineering, including: biochemical engineering, synthetic biology and protein engineering; catalysis and reaction engineering; electrochemical engineering; polymers and soft materials; and environmental research. In addition, students can explore their interests in several cross-disciplinary programs: the Berkeley Sensors and Actuators Center, the Berkeley Stem Cell Center, the Energy Biosciences Institute, the Joint BioEnergy Institute, the Kavli Energy NanoSciences Institute, and the Synthetic Biology Engineering Research Center.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: A complete application includes: Three letters of recommendation, official transcripts, Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Current Resume/C.V., TOEFL/IELTS scores (if applicable).
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree in chemical engineering is primarily a research degree. The program is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of the fundamental principles of chemical engineering and to develop their ability to conduct original research. The doctoral program in chemical engineering is consistently ranked in the top few nationally by U.S. News & World Report and the National Research Council. Graduates are widely sought after for positions in academia, industry, and government laboratories.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Chemistry
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree in chemistry or a closely related field. Generally, it is required that applicants have a GPA of at least 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale). Evidence of English language proficiency for international applicants whose native language is not English. Three letters of recommendation are required.
Concentration: Analytical Chemistry, Chemical Biology, Inorganic Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Physical Chemistry
Description: The Department of Chemistry offers a graduate program leading to the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree. The program is designed to develop the student’s ability to conduct independent research and to provide them with a strong background in the fundamentals of chemistry. The research activities in the department cover a wide variety of fields, including analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry, as well as such diverse areas as chemical biology, nuclear chemistry, and chemical physics.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Research Assistantships, and Teaching Assistantships

ProgramName: Master of City Planning
Requirements: Admission to the MCP program is based on the following: An undergraduate degree from an accredited institution with a GPA of 3.0 or better; Three letters of recommendation; Statement of Purpose; Personal History Statement; Resume or curriculum vitae; and TOEFL/IELTS for international applicants. The GRE is not required for the Master of City Planning (MCP) program.
Concentration: Environmental Planning and Healthy Cities; Housing, Community, and Economic Development; Transportation Policy and Planning; Urban Design
Description: The Master of City Planning (MCP) at UC Berkeley is a two-year professional degree accredited by the Planning Accreditation Board. The curriculum is designed to give students a strong foundation in the history and theory of planning, as well as the technical skills needed for professional practice. Students choose from one of four concentrations: Environmental Planning and Healthy Cities; Housing, Community, and Economic Development; Transportation Policy and Planning; or Urban Design.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Planning Accreditation Board (PAB)
ScholarshipType: Departmental fellowships, need-based aid, and teaching or research assistantships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in City and Regional Planning
Requirements: The minimum graduate admission requirements are: (1) A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; (2) A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and (3) Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. Application materials for the Ph.D. in City and Regional Planning include three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, a current Resume/CV, and a writing sample. For international applicants from countries where the official language is not English, TOEFL or IELTS scores are required. The GRE is not required for this program.
Concentration: Environmental Planning and Policy; Housing, Community, and Economic Development; Land Use Planning; Transportation Policy and Planning; and Urban Design
Description: The PhD in City and Regional Planning provides training for careers in research, teaching, and advanced policy analysis. Our students focus on the study of urban and regional issues in both the US and international contexts. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the theory and history of planning, as well as in the quantitative and qualitative methods used in planning research.

ProgramName: Master of Engineering in Civil and Environmental Engineering
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale, is required. The GRE is not required for the application. As part of the online application, you will also be required to submit a Personal History Statement and three letters of recommendation.
Concentration: Energy, Civil Infrastructure and Climate; Engineering and Project Management; Environmental Engineering; GeoSystems (Geoengineering); Structural Engineering, Mechanics and Materials; Systems (Civil Systems); Transportation Engineering
Description: The Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) Department offers a Master of Science (MS), a Master of Engineering (MEng), and a PhD. The Master of Science program emphasizes graduate-level research or specialized professional practice. The Master of Engineering (MEng) is a professional degree that provides students with a foundation in engineering and the business, management, and leadership skills to enter the workforce as an engineering leader. The PhD program is designed for students interested in research and teaching.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Master of Science in Civil and Environmental Engineering
Requirements: A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. Applicants must also provide three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and evidence of English language proficiency if their native language is not English.
Concentration: Energy, Civil Infrastructure and Climate; Engineering and Project Management; Environmental Engineering; GeoSystems (Geoengineering); Structural Engineering, Mechanics and Materials; Systems (Civil Systems); Transportation Engineering
Description: The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering offers several degree programs for graduate students. The Master of Science (MS) and the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programs are designed for students who want to specialize in a particular technical area within civil and environmental engineering. The MS program usually takes two or three semesters of study. Students can also choose a professional degree program, the Master of Engineering (MEng). The Civil and Environmental Engineering department’s research and teaching are at the forefront of providing the data, models, and decision-making tools to manage the complexities of modern engineering systems.
ScholarshipAmount: Up to $33,000/Year plus tuition and fees
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and Diversity-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Civil and Environmental Engineering
Requirements: Applicants must have at least a 3.0 or higher-level GPA from their undergraduate institution. Required application materials include unofficial transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, a personal history statement, a resume/curriculum vitae, and evidence of English language proficiency (for international applicants). A bachelor's degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution is required.
Concentration: Energy, Civil Infrastructure and Climate; Engineering and Project Management; Environmental Engineering; GeoSystems (Geoengineering); Structural Engineering, Mechanics and Materials; Systems (Civil Systems); Transportation Engineering
Description: The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) at UC Berkeley is a world-renowned leader in engineering education and research. We offer a wide range of graduate programs in several key areas of civil and environmental engineering. Our faculty and students work on cutting-edge research that addresses the most pressing challenges facing our society today, including climate change, urban sustainability, and resilient infrastructure. Berkeley’s CEE department is home to a vibrant and diverse community of students and faculty, and our graduates are highly sought after by employers in industry, government, and academia. Whether you’re interested in pursuing a career in research or practice, our programs will give you the skills and knowledge you need to succeed. The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree is awarded as a mark of the highest achievement in preparation for a career in research and teaching. PhD students are expected to complete a series of advanced courses and to perform original and significant research leading to a dissertation.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Classics
Requirements: To apply to the PhD program in Classics, applicants must submit an online application through the UC Berkeley Graduate Division. Requirements include a statement of purpose, a personal history statement, three letters of recommendation, official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, a writing sample of roughly 20-25 pages, and a curriculum vitae (CV). The GRE is not required for applications to the PhD in Classics.
Description: The PhD program in Classics is a five- to seven-year course of study leading to the degree of Doctor of Philosophy. The program is designed to provide students with a broad and deep knowledge of Greek and Latin language and literature, as well as the history and culture of the ancient world. Students will develop their research and teaching skills through coursework, exams, and the writing of a dissertation. The aim of the PhD program is to prepare students for careers in research and teaching at the university or college level, as well as for other professional paths that require high-level skills in analysis, communication, and research.
ScholarshipAmount: Full funding (covers tuition, fees, and stipend) for 5-6 years
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructor (GSI) positions, and Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) positions

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Comparative Literature
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution with a minimum grade point average of B (3.0). Required preparation includes study in three literatures, at least one of which must be an ancient language, and command of at least two foreign languages, with at least one of these usually being at an advanced level. Admission is based on the applicant's academic record, statement of purpose, personal statement, three letters of recommendation, and a writing sample. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required.
Description: The Department of Comparative Literature at Berkeley is a community of scholars and students dedicated to the study of literature and culture across national and linguistic boundaries. Our program is built on the belief that literary study is most productive when it involves the crossover between different languages, cultures, and disciplines.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based fellowships (University and Departmental), Teaching Assistantships (GSI), and Research Assistantships (GSR)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Science
Requirements: A minimum GPA of 3.0 is required. Applicants for the research-oriented degrees are usually required to have an undergraduate degree in a technical discipline. Admission to the MS and PhD programs is highly competitive. Applications are evaluated by a faculty committee that takes into account the applicant's academic record, research experience, and potential for success in a research-intensive environment. Required application materials include a Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Resume or Curriculum Vitae, and three letters of recommendation.
Description: The Master of Science (MS) is a research-oriented degree. It is intended for students who have a master’s level of maturity in their research and wish to pursue a PhD. It can also be a terminal degree for those who wish to pursue a career in research and development in industry.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Computer Science
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution with a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0. Required application materials include official transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and a Resume/CV. The GRE (Graduate Record Examination) is not required for the Computer Science PhD program and will not be considered in the review process.
Description: The PhD in Computer Science is a research-based program for students who have a prior BS or MS in a technical field (e.g., Computer Science, Math, etc.) and who wish to pursue a career in research and/or academia. The focus of the PhD program is on research. Our program is ranked as one of the top in the country and our faculty is world-renowned.

ProgramName: Master of Design
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale is required. International students from a country where the official language is not English must also fulfill the English Language Proficiency requirement.
Department: College of Engineering and College of Environmental Design
Description: The Master of Design (MDes) at UC Berkeley is a three-semester professional graduate program that prepares students to lead the design of emerging technologies for social and technical impact. Jointly offered by the College of Engineering and the College of Environmental Design, the MDes provides an interdisciplinary curriculum that bridges technical innovation with social consciousness and creative practice. The program is designed for students who are passionate about the potential of design to address complex challenges and who want to gain the skills and knowledge to lead the design of the next generation of products, services, and environments.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Master of Development Engineering
Requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution or recognized equivalent. Minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0. Resume or Curriculum Vitae. Three letters of recommendation. Statement of Purpose. Personal History Statement. Transcripts. English Language Proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS) if applicable. The GRE is not required.
Concentration: AI & Data Analytics; Digital Platforms; Energy, Climate & Sustainability; Health & Medical Technologies
Description: The Master of Development Engineering (MDevEng) is a professional graduate degree designed to prepare students for careers in the private and public sectors as they work to address the most pressing global challenges. Development Engineering (DevEng) is an emerging field that integrates engineering, social sciences, and design to address development challenges through the lens of human-centered design and social impact. The program provides students with a multidisciplinary education, emphasizing the development, implementation, and scaling of technological solutions in low-resource settings. Students will learn to analyze complex problems, design sustainable and impactful interventions, and evaluate their effectiveness. The three-semester curriculum includes core coursework in development engineering, specialized tracks, and a capstone project.

ProgramName: Master of Development Practice
Requirements: To be eligible for the Berkeley MDP, an applicant must have a Bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A typical applicant has at least two years of work experience in a field related to international development. The application requires a completed online graduate application, official transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a current resume/CV, a Statement of Purpose, and a Personal History Statement. International applicants must provide evidence of English language proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS scores). The GRE is not required.
Description: The Master of Development Practice (MDP) at UC Berkeley is a cross-disciplinary professional degree program that prepares students to address the world’s most pressing challenges. Drawing on the expertise of the Goldman School of Public Policy and faculty from across campus, the MDP provides students with the skills and knowledge needed to become leaders in sustainable development. The program combines rigorous academic training with practical, hands-on experience through a summer internship and a capstone project. Students learn to integrate insights from across the natural sciences, social sciences, and management to develop innovative solutions to complex problems.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Departmental Fellowships)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Earth and Planetary Science
Requirements: In addition to the University’s basic requirements for admission, the department requires three letters of recommendation and a statement of purpose. The GRE is not required. Completion of the PhD degree requires: 1) a minimum of four units of 200-level courses from four different EPS professors, 2) passing an oral qualifying examination, 3) the writing of a dissertation, and 4) a final public presentation of the research.
Description: Earth and Planetary Science (EPS) is a multidisciplinary field of study that focuses on the physics, chemistry, and biology of the Earth and other planets. EPS research at Berkeley involves faculty and students in the fields of atmospheric science, biogeochemistry, climate science, ecology, geochemistry, geodesy, geology, geomorphology, geophysics, glaciology, mineralogy, paleontology, planetary science, and seismology. EPS students and faculty use a wide range of tools, including laboratory experiments, field observations, remote sensing, and numerical modeling. Our department is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment where all students can thrive.
ScholarshipAmount: Full financial support (tuition, fees, and stipend) for five years
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR), Graduate Student Instructor (GSI)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in East Asian Languages and Cultures
Requirements: The Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures (EALC) offers a program of study in the languages and cultures of China, Japan, and Korea, leading to the PhD. Requirements for admission include a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution, a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale, and evidence of English Language Proficiency for international applicants. The GRE is not required for this program.
Department: Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures
Concentration: Chinese, Japanese, or Buddhist Studies
Description: The Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures (EALC) offers a program of graduate study leading to the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD). The primary goal of the PhD program is to prepare students for a career in research and teaching at the university level. Students specialize in one of three areas: Chinese, Japanese, or Buddhist Studies. The department also participates in several interdisciplinary doctoral programs, including the Designated Emphasis (DE) in Film Studies, Renaissance and Early Modern Studies, Folklore, and Women, Gender, and Sexuality.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), Research Assistantships (GSR)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Economics
Requirements: The Department of Economics requires that applicants have a basic knowledge of undergraduate economics: at least one course in intermediate microeconomics, one course in intermediate macroeconomics, and one course in econometrics. We also require a strong mathematical background: at least two years of calculus, one course in linear algebra, and one course in statistics. The minimum graduate admission requirements are: A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field.
Concentration: Behavioral Economics, Development Economics, Econometrics, Economic History, Economic Theory, Industrial Organization, International Economics, Labor Economics, Macroeconomics, Public Economics
Description: The PhD program at Berkeley is designed for students interested in pursuing advanced study and conducting original research in Economics. The primary objective of the graduate program is to educate students for careers in research and teaching. The program is designed to provide students with the tools and techniques of modern economic analysis, as well as to encourage them to develop their own research interests. The PhD program is a full-time, in-residence program, and is completed, on average, in 5 to 6 years. Students take core courses in their first year and then specialize in two fields of their choice during their second and third years. The remainder of the program is spent conducting original research and writing a dissertation.
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition and fees coverage plus a stipend ($41,000 for 2024-25)
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships, and Graduate Student Research positions)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Education
Requirements: The minimum graduate admission requirements are: (1) A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; (2) A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and (3) Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. Required application materials include an online application, application fee, transcripts, three letters of recommendation, statement of purpose, personal history statement, and a resume/CV.
Concentration: Critical Studies of Race, Class, and Gender; Cultural Studies of Sport in Education; Language, Literacy, and Culture; Learning Sciences and Human Development; Policy, Politics, and Leadership; Quantitative Methods and Evaluation; Social Research Methodologies
Description: The Berkeley School of Education offers a Master of Arts in Education for students who wish to pursue a research-focused degree. This program is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in the future or who are seeking a career in educational research, policy, or practice. The MA degree is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in educational theory, research methods, and a specialized area of study. The MA degree requires students to complete a minimum of 24 units of coursework and a capstone project (either a thesis or a comprehensive examination).
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), Graduate Student Researcherships (GSR), and Need-based grants

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Education
Requirements: In addition to the University’s requirements for admission, applicants to the Berkeley School of Education must fulfill the following: 1. A Statement of Purpose 2. A Personal History Statement 3. Three letters of recommendation 4. Official transcripts for all college-level work 5. A current resume or curriculum vitae 6. A writing sample. The GRE is not required for the PhD in Education.
Concentration: Critical Studies of Race, Class, and Gender; Cultural Studies of Sport in Education; Development in Language, Literacy and Culture; Learning Sciences and Human Development; Policy, Politics, and Leadership; Quantitative Methods and Evaluation; Social and Cultural Studies; Special Education (joint program with SF State)
Description: The Graduate School of Education offers a PhD and MA/PhD in Education with several areas of study. The doctoral program is designed to produce scholars who will conduct research and teach in universities and other research settings. The Master’s/Doctoral program is for students who do not already have a Master’s degree. Students are admitted to one of the following areas of study: Critical Studies of Race, Class, and Gender; Cultural Studies of Sport in Education; Development in Language, Literacy and Culture; Learning Sciences and Human Development; Policy, Politics, and Leadership; Quantitative Methods and Evaluation; Social and Cultural Studies; and Special Education (joint program with SF State).
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructor (GSI) positions, and Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) positions

ProgramName: Doctor of Education in Education
Requirements: Requirements for admission to the LEAD EdD program include: A Master's degree from an accredited institution; A grade point average of at least 3.0 (B) or better; Evidence of professional leadership in education or a related field; Professional writing sample; Current CV/Resume; Three letters of recommendation; Statement of Purpose; and a Personal History Statement. GRE scores are not required for this program.
Concentration: Leaders for Equity and Democracy
Description: The LEAD EdD program is designed for working educational leaders who are committed to disrupting systems of privilege and power to achieve more equitable outcomes for students. The program is a three-year, cohort-based, executive-style program that integrates theory, research, and practice to prepare leaders to transform educational organizations.

ProgramName: Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences
Requirements: The minimum graduate admission requirements are: (1) A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; (2) A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and (3) Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. Applicants must also provide three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and unofficial transcripts. The GRE is not required for the M.Eng. program.
Concentration: ['Data Science and Systems', 'Physical Electronics and Integrated Circuits', 'Robotics and Embedded Software', 'Signal Processing and Communications', 'Visual Computing and Computer Graphics']
Description: The Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) in Electrical Engineering & Computer Sciences is a professional program designed for students who plan to pursue a career in industry. The program's core curriculum consists of a capstone project and courses in leadership and technology management, which are supplemented by technical electives in the student's chosen area of concentration.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Master of Engineering Opportunity Grant)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences
Requirements: The minimum undergraduate grade point average (GPA) for admission is 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale. Applicants must submit a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, three letters of recommendation, and a current resume or curriculum vitae. The GRE is not required.
Description: The Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences (EECS) offers two graduate programs in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences: the Master of Integrated Circuits (offered only through the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences) and the Master of Science (MS) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD). The Master of Science (MS) is a research-oriented degree that can be earned as a terminal degree or as the first step toward the PhD. This program is available only to students who are currently enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley or who have been admitted to a PhD program at UC Berkeley. The PhD is a research-oriented degree intended for students who wish to pursue a career in research and teaching. The Master of Engineering (MEng) is a professional degree designed for students who want to enter the industry with a high level of technical expertise and a grounding in business and management.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences
Requirements: In addition to the University’s minimum requirements, applicants must also meet the specific requirements of the EECS Department. A minimum grade point average of 3.0 (B) or better is required. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for the PhD, MS/PhD, and MS program applications. International applicants from countries in which the official language is not English and who do not hold a bachelor's degree from a US institution must provide evidence of English language proficiency.
Concentration: Computer Science, Electrical Engineering
Description: The Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences (EECS) offers two graduate programs in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences: the Master of Science (MS) and the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD). The Master of Science (MS) is a research-oriented degree that can be earned in two semesters (Plan II, which requires a project) or three semesters (Plan I, which requires a thesis). The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) is intended for students who desire a career in research. The program requires a minimum of two years of study, a qualifying examination, and a dissertation. Research in the department is organized into several areas: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Biosystems & Computational Biology (BIO), Communications & Networking (COMNET), Computer Architecture & Engineering (ARC), Control, Intelligent Systems, and Robotics (CIR), Database Management Systems (DBMS), Design of Electronic Systems (DES), Education (EDUC), Energy (ENE), Graphics (GR), Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Integrated Circuits (INC), Micro/Nano Electro Mechanical Systems (MEMS), Operating Systems & Networking (OSNT), Programming Systems (PS), Scientific Computing (SCI), Security (SEC), Signal Processing (SP), Theory (THY).
AverageScholarshipAmount: Full funding (Tuition, fees, and monthly stipend)
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR), and Graduate Student Instructor (GSI)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Energy and Resources
Requirements: The Graduate Group in Energy and Resources (ERG) offers two programs of study and research: one leading to the MA and MS degrees in Energy and Resources, and the other to the PhD degree in Energy and Resources. The objective of the program is to teach students the range of knowledge and the types of analysis they will need to understand and help solve the world’s energy and resource problems. To that end, the ERG curriculum is designed to provide students with a fundamental understanding of the biological, physical, economic, and political-institutional dimensions of energy and resource issues.
Description: The Energy and Resources Group (ERG) is an interdisciplinary academic graduate unit at the University of California, Berkeley. ERG’s mission is to provide education and research for a sustainable environment and a just society. To this end, ERG provides the tools to help students and researchers develop the skills to bridge disciplines and the knowledge to work across the boundaries of traditional departments. ERG students are challenged to integrate the methods of the natural and social sciences into an approach that addresses the complex challenges facing the world. ERG focuses on issues such as global climate change, sustainable development, resource governance, renewable energy, and environmental justice. ERG graduates go on to work in academia, government, non-profit organizations, and the private sector.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based

ProgramName: Master of Science in Energy and Resources
Requirements: A bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. Evidence of academic excellence and potential for creative research. A minimum GPA of 3.0 is required. The GRE General Test is not required and will not be considered. International applicants must demonstrate English proficiency via the TOEFL or IELTS.
Description: The Energy and Resources Group (ERG) is a unique, interdisciplinary graduate program at the University of California, Berkeley. ERG provides an environment for research and teaching on the complex challenges facing our environment, our societies, and our energy and resource systems. The ERG Master’s program is a two-year program designed to provide students with a broad, interdisciplinary education in energy and resources. The program leads to either a Master of Arts (MA) or a Master of Science (MS) degree. The curriculum is intended to help students develop the analytical tools and the conceptual framework to address the complex issues of resource management, environmental impact, and sustainable development.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Energy and Resources
Requirements: In addition to the University’s minimum requirements, the Group requires that an applicant have a strong background in one of the relevant fields, such as physical, biological or social sciences, engineering or humanities. Applicants should have a minimum of two semesters of college-level calculus and at least one semester of upper-division natural science or engineering. The requirements for the Ph.D. consist of coursework, a preliminary examination, a qualifying examination, and a dissertation. Ph.D. applicants are usually expected to have already completed a master's degree or equivalent.
Description: The Energy and Resources Group (ERG) is an interdisciplinary academic unit of the University of California, Berkeley. ERG’s mission is to provide education and research for a sustainable environment and a just society. To this end, ERG offers two professional master’s degrees (MA and MS) and a doctoral degree (PhD). The ERG curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the technical, economic, social, and political aspects of energy and resource issues, as well as the tools to analyze and solve problems in these areas. ERG students and faculty come from a wide range of backgrounds, including the natural sciences, engineering, social sciences, and humanities.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), Graduate Student Researchers (GSR)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in English
Requirements: Each applicant must have a B.A. or its equivalent from an institution of acceptable standing. In addition, we require that applicants have done a substantial amount of work in English literature. It is also important that an applicant be able to demonstrate an ability to read at least one foreign language. Materials for the online application include: Letters of recommendation, GRE scores (General and Subject), Transcripts, Writing Sample, Statement of Purpose, and Personal Statement.
Description: Our PhD program provides students with a broad and deep foundation in English and American literature, as well as the specialized skills needed to carry out original research in a chosen area of study. Students work closely with faculty members who are leaders in their fields, and they benefit from the resources of a world-class research university. The program is designed to be completed in six years, and it includes coursework, a qualifying examination, and a dissertation. Graduate students in English at Berkeley are part of a vibrant intellectual community that includes over 100 PhD students and 50 faculty members.
ScholarshipType: Multi-year funding package (stipend, tuition, fees, and health insurance)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Environmental Health Sciences
Requirements: Applicants to the MS program must have: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Evidence of potential for doctoral study. A minimum of one year of prior research experience is strongly recommended. Preference is given to applicants with strong backgrounds in the biological or physical sciences. Previous coursework should include: 1 year of general chemistry, 1 year of biology, and at least 1 semester of organic chemistry.
Concentration: Global Health & Environment, Industrial Hygiene, Occupational and Environmental Health Nursing
Description: The Master of Science (MS) in Environmental Health Sciences provides students with a strong foundation in the principles and practices of environmental health. This degree program is designed for students with a background in the basic sciences who wish to pursue careers in research or professional practice. Students in the MS program will gain expertise in identifying and assessing environmental and occupational hazards, understanding the health effects of these hazards, and developing strategies to prevent or control exposure. The MS program typically takes two years to complete and requires a combination of coursework and research. Students will work closely with faculty mentors to develop a research project and complete a thesis.
Accredidation: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Environmental Health Sciences
Requirements: The program in Environmental Health Sciences (EHS) provides students with the knowledge and skills for research and leadership in the field of environmental health. Applicants are required to submit a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, a Resumé/Curriculum Vitae, three Letters of Recommendation, and Transcripts for all college-level work. Applicants must have an academic record of high quality and demonstrate commitment to the field of public health. A bachelor’s degree or its recognized equivalent from an accredited institution is required for admission. The GRE General Test is not required.
Description: The Environmental Health Sciences (EHS) program at UC Berkeley is concerned with the effects of environmental and occupational exposures on human health and with the assessment and control of these exposures. The Doctor of Philosophy degree (PhD) in Environmental Health Sciences is an academic research degree that is intended for students who have an interest in academic or research careers. The Division of Environmental Health Sciences (EHS) provides students with the skills required for research and practice in the prevention of injuries and illnesses caused by various exposures in the workplace and the environment. Students specialize in one of several areas within environmental health, though the integrated nature of the program ensures that all students obtain a thorough understanding of the field as a whole. Core areas of focus include: climate change and health; environmental and occupational epidemiology; and toxicology, environmental chemistry, and exposure assessment.
Accredidation: The School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Environmental Science, Policy, and Management
Requirements: Applicants must complete an online application and submit a Statement of Purpose (2-3 pages), a Personal History Statement, three letters of recommendation, unofficial transcripts from each institution attended, and a current CV or resume. A minimum GPA of 3.0 from the undergraduate institution is required. International applicants must also meet the Graduate Division’s English Language Proficiency requirement. The GRE is not required and will not be seen by the admissions committee.
Concentration: Ecosystem Sciences, Organisms & Environment, and Society & Environment
Description: The ESPM PhD program is one of the premier environmental research and education programs in the world. Our mission is to educate the next generation of scholars and leaders who will address the most pressing environmental challenges of our time. ESPM provides a diverse and interdisciplinary environment for graduate study, where students work across natural and social science disciplines to understand and manage the earth's environment.
ScholarshipAmount: Full funding (includes tuition, fees, and a stipend for living expenses)
ScholarshipType: Fellowship, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR), and Graduate Student Instructor (GSI)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Epidemiology
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution. A minimum grade-point average of 3.0 (B) is required. At least one college-level math or statistics course with a grade of B or better is required. The GRE is not required.
Description: The MS in Epidemiology provides students with a strong foundation in epidemiologic and biostatistical methods and their application to a wide range of public health problems. The program is designed for students who want to pursue a career in epidemiologic research or who intend to pursue a doctoral degree. Through a combination of coursework and a master’s thesis, students will learn to design, conduct, and analyze epidemiologic studies and to communicate their findings to scientific and professional audiences.
Accredidation: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, need-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Epidemiology
Requirements: Applicants must have a previous degree (BA, BS, MA, MS, MPH, MD, or equivalent) and an interest in and a demonstrated aptitude for quantitative methods and research. Successful applicants generally have a background in a related field (such as biology, math, statistics, or social sciences) and previous research or work experience in public health or a related area. While a prior master’s degree is not strictly required for the PhD program, most successful applicants do have one.
Description: Epidemiology is a department-wide program at the UC Berkeley School of Public Health. Our epidemiology graduate programs offer students a choice of three degrees: Master of Public Health (MPH), Master of Science (MS), and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD). Students in our program gain the skills to become highly-trained, independent researchers who can apply epidemiological methods to various public health issues. Our students work closely with faculty members in a variety of areas of public health, including infectious diseases, chronic diseases, maternal and child health, environmental health, and social epidemiology. Our students also have the opportunity to collaborate with faculty members in other departments at UC Berkeley and at other institutions. The PhD in epidemiology provides students with the skills to become independent researchers who can apply epidemiological methods to a wide range of public health issues, preparing them for careers in academia, research institutions, and government agencies.
Accredidation: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructor (GSI) positions, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) positions

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Ethnic Studies
Requirements: A bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 (B) is required for the application to be reviewed. Applicants must submit a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, three letters of recommendation, a writing sample (approx. 30 pages maximum), and a current resume or CV. The GRE is not required for the 2024-2025 application cycle.
Description: The Department of Ethnic Studies at the University of California, Berkeley, offers a PhD in Ethnic Studies. The program is internationally recognized for its leadership in the development of comparative ethnic studies. The PhD program provides an interdisciplinary and comparative framework for studying the historical, social, and cultural productions of power and social difference. The curriculum focuses on the histories, cultures, and politics of racial and ethnic groups in the United States and globally, with particular emphasis on African American, Asian American/Pacific Islander, Chicana/o/Latina/o, and Native American/Indigenous peoples.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), and Research Assistantships (GSR)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Film and Media
Requirements: The PhD in Film & Media is a 12-course program (plus two semesters of Graduate Student Instructor pedagogy courses). PhD students are expected to complete two years of coursework, followed by a Qualifying Exam in the third year and a doctoral dissertation thereafter. Applicants must hold a BA or equivalent from an accredited institution. An MA is not required to apply.
Description: The graduate program in Film & Media at UC Berkeley is designed for students who want to develop a deep understanding of film and media history, theory, and criticism. The program emphasizes the interdisciplinary nature of film and media studies, and students are encouraged to draw on the resources of the entire university. Film & Media at Berkeley is a leading center for the study of cinema and new media, with a world-renowned faculty and a vibrant graduate student community.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships, Graduate Student Researchers)

ProgramName: Master of Financial Engineering
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the MFE Program, you must have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. Applicants must demonstrate a strong quantitative background including coursework in Multivariate Calculus, Linear Algebra, Differential Equations, Numerical Analysis, and Statistics and Probability. Proficiency in computer programming, specifically Python and C++, is required prior to the start of the program. Applicants must also provide valid GRE or GMAT scores, a professional resume, and two letters of recommendation.
Description: The Berkeley Master of Financial Engineering program prepares you for a career in finance by combining advanced training in financial theory with the practical skills needed for the quantitative finance industry. Our curriculum is designed to provide you with a deep understanding of finance, economics, mathematics, and computer science. Since its inception in 2000, the Berkeley MFE has been a leader in the field, consistently ranking among the top programs in the world, providing students with the knowledge and skills they need to succeed in the fast-paced world of quantitative finance.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Folklore
Requirements: The basic requirements for admission to the Folklore M.A. program are: 1. A Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Science degree from an accredited institution. 2. An undergraduate Grade Point Average of 3.0 or higher. 3. Proficiency in at least one foreign language is required for the M.A. degree in Folklore. This requirement may be satisfied by the end of the first year of the program.
Description: The Folklore Graduate Program offers an M.A. degree. Folklore at Berkeley is interdisciplinary and students have the opportunity to design an individual program of study with the help of a faculty advisor. The Berkeley faculty includes many distinguished scholars from across the campus with a specific interest in folklore. Folklore is a multifaceted discipline that draws from many other fields, including anthropology, linguistics, literature, history, sociology, and psychology.
