Students interested in pursuing a graduate degree in folklore should have a strong background in one or more of these areas.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Foreign Language and Area Studies (FLAS) awards

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in French
Requirements: To apply for the Ph.D. program in French, applicants must submit the University’s Graduate Application. Required materials include: 1. Statement of Purpose: approximately 2 pages in English, describing preparation and motivation for graduate study. 2. Personal History Statement: in English. 3. Transcripts: Digital transcripts from each college or university attended. 4. Three letters of recommendation. 5. Writing Sample: 20-25 pages in length in French or English, demonstrating best scholarly work. The GRE is not required. Applicants must have a B.A. or M.A. in French or its equivalent from a university of recognized standing.
Description: The Department of French offers a Ph.D. in French. It does not offer a terminal Master’s degree. All students are admitted to the Ph.D. program, but have the option of receiving an M.A. en route to the Ph.D. Once admitted, students follow a program of study consisting of course work, a qualifying examination, and a dissertation. Students are expected to become proficient in the standard areas of French and Francophone literature and culture, while also pursuing their own particular research interests. They are also expected to develop a high level of proficiency in the French language. The department provides a rigorous training in the teaching of French at all levels, and students are given the opportunity to teach both language and literature courses.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructor (GSI) positions, and Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) positions

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Geography
Requirements: To apply to the graduate program, applicants must submit a complete application through the UC Berkeley Graduate Division online application system. A complete application includes: Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, Three letters of recommendation (submitted through the online application system), a Writing Sample (15–30 pages), and a Curriculum Vitae or Resume. International applicants must also submit TOEFL or IELTS scores. The Geography Department no longer requires the GRE.
Description: The graduate program is primarily a PhD program, although students may receive an MA degree in the course of their doctoral studies. (The department does not offer a terminal MA degree.) The Berkeley Geography graduate program is one of the most highly ranked in the country. Our faculty and students have a wide range of interests, and the program is designed to be flexible to allow students to pursue their own research agendas. Geography at Berkeley is a small, highly-ranked department that offers students a chance to work with a distinguished faculty. Our graduate students are a talented and diverse group, and they go on to careers in academia, government, and the private sector. Themes of the department include: Development & Political Ecology, Global Change and Ecosystems, Global Environmental Processes, Geomorphology, Urban Studies, Place, Race and Power, and GIS and Remote Sensing.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), and Graduate Student Research (GSR)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in German
Requirements: Applicants for the Ph.D. in German at UC Berkeley must submit an online application that includes a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, a Writing Sample (approximately 20-25 pages in German or English), three letters of recommendation, and a CV/Resume. Applicants must also provide transcripts from all institutions of higher education attended. The GRE (Graduate Record Examination) is not required for admission to this program.
Concentration: German Literature and Culture, Germanic Linguistics
Description: The Department of German at the University of California, Berkeley offers a program of graduate study leading to the Ph.D. Students may specialize in either German Literature and Culture or Germanic Linguistics. The program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive knowledge of the German language, its history, and its literature and culture from the earliest times to the present, while at the same time encouraging them to develop their own research interests within a broad range of theoretical and interdisciplinary perspectives. Students are prepared for careers in research and teaching at the college and university level.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Fellowships, Teaching/Research Assistantships)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Global Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Master of Arts in Global Studies, you will need to submit the following: Official Transcripts, Evidence of English Language Proficiency, Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, A current CV, Three letters of recommendation. Analytical Writing Sample (Optional), GRE scores (Optional).
Concentration: Global Development, Global Societies and Cultures, Global Governance
Description: The Master of Arts (MA) in Global Studies is a one-year, interdisciplinary program designed for students who want to develop a deeper understanding of the global processes that shape our world. The program is ideal for students who are looking for a rigorous academic experience that will prepare them for a variety of careers in the public, private, and non-profit sectors, or for further graduate study.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Health Policy
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution, a satisfactory scholastic average (usually a minimum GPA of 3.0), and enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in the chosen field. Required application materials include a Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, three letters of recommendation, transcripts, a current Resume/CV, and a Writing Sample. The GRE is not required for this program.
Concentration: health economics, health services and policy research, and organizational behavior
Description: The Doctoral Program in Health Policy at the University of California, Berkeley, provides students with the breadth and depth of knowledge and the specialized skills to perform high-quality, innovative research in health policy and health services. This multidisciplinary program, which leads to a PhD degree, is designed for students interested in pursuing careers in teaching and research in academic institutions, and in research and policy analysis in government and in the private sector.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Hispanic Languages and Literatures
Requirements: To apply for the Ph.D. in Hispanic Languages and Literatures, applicants must submit a Graduate Division online application, official transcripts from all institutions attended after high school, three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, a curriculum vitae (CV), and a writing sample of approximately 15-20 pages in Spanish or Portuguese. The GRE is not required for admission to this program.
Description: The Department of Spanish & Portuguese offers programs of study leading to the PhD in Hispanic Languages and Literatures. The program provides students with a high degree of professional preparation for a career in university teaching and research. It is designed to ensure that students have a broad knowledge of the literature and culture of the Hispanic and Lusophone worlds, as well as the critical and linguistic tools necessary for specialized research.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in History
Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution and have a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0. Required application materials include a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, a curriculum vitae (CV), three letters of recommendation, and a writing sample. The GRE is no longer required for admission to the PhD program in History.
Description: The Department of History offers a program of graduate study leading to the Ph.D. in History. The program is designed to provide students with the opportunity for advanced study in history, to train them in the methods of historical research, and to prepare them for careers in teaching and research. The department offers training in a wide range of geographical and thematic fields, from ancient history to the present day, and is committed to preparing its students for professional success both within and outside of academia.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in History of Art
Requirements: Application components: Statement of Purpose; Personal History Statement; Curriculum Vitae; Three letters of recommendation; A writing sample (e.g. a term paper, or a portion of a senior or master’s thesis) of 15 to 25 pages, but no more than 30 pages; Transcripts of all college or university work. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is no longer required for application to the Ph.D. program in History of Art.
Concentration: Critical Theory, Film Studies, Gender, Women and Sexuality, Medieval Studies, New Media, Renaissance and Early Modern Studies, Science and Technology Studies
Description: The Graduate Program in History of Art is designed to prepare students for careers in college and university teaching, museum work, and other positions of intellectual leadership in the visual arts. The program is specifically directed toward the PhD. We do not offer a separate Master’s degree, although students may earn an MA on the way to the PhD. The Department of History of Art at Berkeley provides its graduate students with diverse opportunities for intellectual growth, professional training, and financial support. These range from departmental and campus resources to external fellowships and internships.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSIs), Readerships, Graduate Student Researchships (GSRs)

ProgramName: Master of Engineering in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research
Requirements: Applicants must fulfill the following: A bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution; A minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; Three letters of recommendation; Statement of Purpose; Personal History Statement; Resume; Evidence of English language proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS) if the applicant’s degree is from a country where English is not the official language.
Concentration: Data Science and Systems Engineering, Financial Technology, Intellectual Property and Strategy, and Management Science and Engineering
Description: The Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) program is a professional program that combines advanced technical courses with leadership and management courses. The Berkeley Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) in Industrial Engineering & Operations Research is a full-time, one-year professional program that blends rigorous technical training with leadership and management coursework. It is designed for students who want to become engineering leaders in their field. The program allows students to customize their experience by choosing from a range of concentrations and electives, and provides opportunities to work on real-world projects with industry partners.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Fung Institute Excellence Fellowships)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research
Requirements: Applicants to the M.S. and Ph.D. programs must have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. A major in engineering, physical science, mathematics, or another field with a strong mathematical background is preferred. The department requires a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0 or higher for the last two years of undergraduate study. Required application materials include transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, a personal history statement, and a resume/CV.
Description: The Department of Industrial Engineering and Operations Research at UC Berkeley offers three graduate programs: the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), the Master of Science (MS), and the Master of Engineering (MEng). Our programs are consistently ranked among the top in the nation by U.S. News & World Report. Students come from all over the world to work with our award-winning faculty in one of the most exciting and productive departments in the country.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the IEOR graduate program, you must have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution or its equivalent. A minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 is required. Applicants are also expected to have a strong mathematical background, including calculus, linear algebra, and probability and statistics. The IEOR department welcomes applications from students with strong backgrounds in any area of engineering, mathematics, physics, or other quantitative sciences.
Description: The IEOR Department offers a Ph.D. in IEOR, where students participate in an advanced, research-oriented program of study. Students focus on a specific research area of their choice. UC Berkeley’s graduate programs are consistently ranked among the top in the nation. The goal of the Ph.D. program is to prepare students for careers in research and teaching at the university level, or for research and development positions in industry or government.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructor (GSI), Graduate Student Researcher (GSR)

ProgramName: Master of Information and Cybersecurity
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or its recognized equivalent from an accredited institution. A high level of technical aptitude and a basic proficiency in at least one programming language (such as Python, Java, or C++) are required for success in the program. Applicants are also required to submit three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, and a personal history statement.
Description: The Master of Information and Cybersecurity (MICS) is a multi-disciplinary professional degree program. Delivered online, MICS provides students with the proficiency in the technologies and practices of systems, software, and network security, as well as an understanding of the legal, policy, and ethical issues surrounding cybersecurity. Students will learn to develop and manage secure systems, analyze and respond to security threats, and understand the broader social and political implications of cybersecurity. The program is designed for working professionals with a background in computer science, information technology, or a related field.
Accredidation: The University of California, Berkeley is accredited by the Western Association of Schools and Colleges (WASC).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Master of Information and Data Science
Requirements: The Master of Information and Data Science (MIDS) program is an innovative part-time program that prepares data science professionals to solve real-world problems. Applicants must have a superior scholastic record, normally a 3.0 undergraduate GPA. Applicants should have a working knowledge of fundamental programming concepts and a basic understanding of data structures and algorithms, and they should have completed a college-level course in introductory statistics.
Description: The Master of Information and Data Science (MIDS) is a professional degree program designed to train data science leaders. Delivered online, the MIDS program features a multidisciplinary curriculum that includes computer science, statistics, social science, management, and law. Students learn to derive insights from complex and unstructured data, using the latest tools and analytical methods. Students explore the entire data science lifecycle, from data collection and processing to analysis and communication.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Master of Information Management and Systems
Requirements: Bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution. A minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale. 3 Letters of Recommendation. Statement of Purpose. Personal History Statement. Evidence of English Language Proficiency (for international applicants). High level of quantitative and analytical ability. Basic understanding of programming and data structures.
Description: The Master of Information Management and Systems (MIMS) program is a 48-unit, two-year professional degree program designed to train students for careers as information professionals. To prepare students for such careers, the MIMS program provides a solid foundation in the concepts and techniques of information management, as well as the ability to apply those concepts and techniques in a variety of settings. The program is interdisciplinary, drawing on faculty and courses from across the Berkeley campus, including computer science, law, business, and the social sciences.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Information Management and Systems
Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. To apply, you must submit the UC Berkeley Graduate Division online application. Required application materials include: UC Berkeley graduate application, Application fee, Current Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV), Three letters of recommendation, Statement of purpose, Personal history statement, Transcripts from all college-level institutions attended, TOEFL or IELTS scores (for international applicants from countries where the official language is not English), and a Writing sample.
Description: The Ph.D. in Information Management and Systems is a research-oriented degree program for students who wish to prepare for careers in research and teaching at the university level or for research and leadership positions in industry or government. The program is designed for students with diverse backgrounds — including the social sciences, humanities, and computer and physical sciences — who have a common interest in the study of information. PhD students work with faculty on original research and will develop a deep understanding of the social, technical, and policy issues that surround information.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based fellowships, Graduate Student Researchships (GSR), and Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Integrative Biology
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. Applicants should have a minimum GPA of 3.0. A complete application consists of the following: University Online Application, Three letters of recommendation, Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Resume/CV, Official transcripts (uploaded), TOEFL/IELTS scores (if applicable). The GRE General and Subject tests are no longer required for admission to the IB graduate program.
Description: Graduate study in the Department of Integrative Biology (IB) at the University of California, Berkeley, offers a program of study and research leading to the Doctor of Philosophy degree. The Department of Integrative Biology is one of the largest departments on the UC Berkeley campus. It focuses on the integration of structure and function in the evolution and ecology of organisms. Research in the department spans all levels of biological organization, from the molecular and organismal to the community and ecosystem levels. The department includes over 45 faculty members, over 100 graduate students, and approximately 100 postdoctoral fellows and visiting scholars. Areas of expertise include ecology, evolutionary biology, paleontology, physiology, functional morphology, biomechanics, and human biology.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), and Graduate Student Researchships (GSR)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Italian Studies
Requirements: The department admits students for the fall semester only. Applicants are required to have a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A background in Italian literature and culture is expected. Minimum requirements for admission include: 1. A bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. 2. A minimum grade point average of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale. 3. Sufficient undergraduate training to undertake graduate study in Italian. 4. Evidence of English language proficiency, if your native language is not English and you have not received a degree from a university in an English-speaking country.
Description: The Department of Italian Studies offers a program of study leading to the PhD in Italian Studies. The program is designed to provide students with a broad and rigorous training in Italian literature and culture from the medieval period to the present. The department’s faculty are specialists in a wide range of areas, including medieval and Renaissance studies, 18th- to 20th-century literature, film studies, and cultural studies.
ScholarshipType: Multi-year funding packages (including fellowships and Graduate Student Instructorships)

ProgramName: Master of Journalism
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution with a grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 (B). Required application materials include a statement of purpose, personal history statement, resume/CV, three letters of recommendation, and three samples of journalistic work. International applicants must also meet the Graduate Division's requirements for English language proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS). The GRE is not required for applicants to the MJ program.
Description: Our two-year Master of Journalism program is widely considered to be one of the best in the country. Our unique curriculum allows students to gain a foundation in the basics of reporting, writing and editing, while developing professional-level skills in multiple platforms: audio, documentary, multimedia, narrative writing, photography, and video journalism. Throughout the program, students can choose to work in any of these media or a combination of several, focusing on everything from investigative reporting to local news. This multiplatform approach gives our graduates an advantage in an increasingly digital and diverse professional world. It prepares them to be leaders in the field and provides them with the flexibility to thrive in any newsroom. Students in the MJ program spend two full years on campus. The first year is focused on learning foundational skills and creating high-quality work in specific media platforms. The second year is devoted to deep, original reporting on a master’s project or a documentary film. MJ students can also apply for a concurrent degree in another field. We currently offer three concurrent degrees: Journalism and Law (JD/MJ), Journalism and Asian Studies (MA/MJ), and Journalism and Public Health (MPH/MJ).
Accredidation: The UC Berkeley Graduate School of Journalism is accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications (ACEJMC).
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, merit-based, need-based

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Jurisprudence and Social Policy
Requirements: The Jurisprudence and Social Policy (JSP) program at UC Berkeley requires applicants to submit a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, three letters of recommendation, and a writing sample (preferably 10 to 20 pages). A Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume is also required. Standardized tests, such as the GRE, are not required for admission to this program. Applicants should have a background in social sciences or humanities.
Description: The Jurisprudence and Social Policy (JSP) Program is a unique PhD program that provides interdisciplinary study in law and legal institutions. At the Jurisprudence and Social Policy Program (JSP), we study law using the concepts and methods of the humanities and social sciences. As the first program of its kind in the United States, JSP has a long-standing commitment to cross-disciplinary scholarship. JSP is located in the Law School, but our faculty and students come from many disciplines, including history, political science, sociology, economics, philosophy and psychology. We emphasize the integration of law and legal institutions with the theories and methods of the social sciences and humanities. While some of our students pursue a JD alongside their PhD, JSP is a research-intensive program that does not require a law degree. Our mission is to produce scholars and leaders who can apply rigorous interdisciplinary research to the most pressing legal and social issues of our time.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Jurisprudence and Social Policy
Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. Application requirements include the University’s online Graduate Application, official transcripts from all institutions attended after high school, three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and a Writing Sample. The JSP Program no longer requires or accepts GRE scores as part of the application for admission.
Concentration: Economics, History, Philosophy, Political Science, and Sociology
Description: Jurisprudence and Social Policy (JSP) is a unique interdisciplinary graduate program at Berkeley Law. JSP was the first of its kind in the United States, offering a Ph.D. degree for the study of law from the perspective of various social science and humanities disciplines: economics, history, philosophy, political science, and sociology. The JSP program provides a setting for students to analyze legal ideas, institutions, and processes from an empirical and normative perspective. Students in the program develop the necessary expertise to become scholars in their chosen fields of study and to teach in law schools and departments of social science and humanities.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, teaching assistantships, and research assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Landscape Architecture
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Graduate Division at UC Berkeley, including a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum grade point average of 3.0 (B). Applicants to the MLA program will be required to submit transcripts from all higher education institutions attended, three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and a portfolio of creative work.
Description: The Master of Landscape Architecture (M.L.A.) degree is a professional degree, which is accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB). The program offers two tracks of study: a three-year program (M.L.A. I) for students who have an undergraduate degree in a field other than landscape architecture or architecture; and a two-year program (M.L.A. II) for students who have a prior professional degree in landscape architecture or architecture. The M.L.A. program prepares students for leadership in the profession of landscape architecture. It is an intensive course of study that provides students with the necessary skills to design at a variety of scales—from the site to the region—and to engage with the complex social, environmental, and aesthetic issues facing the built environment today. The program’s curriculum is grounded in a strong foundation of design, ecology, and technology, and it emphasizes the importance of research and critical thinking in the design process. The M.L.A. program in the Department of Landscape Architecture and Environmental Planning (LAEP) at the Berkeley campus is one of the oldest and most prestigious landscape architecture programs in the United States.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB)
ScholarshipType: Need-based and merit-based grants and fellowships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Landscape Architecture and Environmental Planning
Requirements: Applicants are expected to have completed a master's degree before entering the Ph.D. program. However, students with only a bachelor's degree may be admitted under exceptional circumstances. The Ph.D. program in Landscape Architecture and Environmental Planning is for students who wish to pursue research and teaching careers. The program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the theoretical and methodological aspects of the field, while also allowing them the flexibility to pursue their own research interests.
Description: The PhD program in Landscape Architecture and Environmental Planning (LAEP) is a research-oriented degree that emphasizes the development of specialized knowledge in various facets of the field. Students pursue individual research interests under the guidance of faculty experts, contributing to the academic and professional knowledge base of landscape architecture and environmental planning. Areas of research may include environmental history, social and cultural aspects of design, ecological design and planning, and urban design.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships (e.g., Berkeley Fellowship, Chancellor's Fellowship)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Latin
Requirements: Applicants for admission must have an undergraduate major in Latin or the equivalent. The minimum graduate admission requirements are: (1) A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; (2) A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and (3) Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. Three letters of recommendation are required.
Description: The Master of Arts (MA) in Latin is a terminal degree program designed to provide students with a broad and deep knowledge of Latin literature and language. The program is particularly suited for those who wish to teach Latin at the secondary school level or who wish to prepare for further graduate study in classics or related fields.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Latin American Studies
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Latin American Studies is a research-oriented program designed for students who wish to focus on a particular problem or theme related to Latin America while also gaining expertise in two different disciplines. Students work with a faculty committee that reflects their multidisciplinary interests. The program is intended to produce scholars who are well-grounded in a particular discipline, but who can also think and work across disciplinary boundaries. Each student’s program is unique, organized around a particular problem or theme and two disciplines.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructor/Researcher positions)

ProgramName: Master of Laws
Requirements: To be eligible for the LL.M. program, applicants must have a first degree in law (JD, LLB, or equivalent) from a law school outside the US or an ABA-accredited law school in the US. Applicants must submit an online application through LSAC, an application fee, official transcripts, at least two letters of recommendation, a personal statement, and a curriculum vitae (CV) or resume. Additionally, applicants whose first degree in law was not taught in English must provide a TOEFL or IELTS score.
Concentration: Environmental Law
Description: The Berkeley Law LL.M. Certificate in Environmental Law recognizes that students have successfully completed a course of study and have specialized in environmental and energy law. To earn the certificate, students must complete at least 12 units of coursework from the list below, including a 1-unit ‘foundational’ course (Environmental Law and Policy for LLMs) and a 1-unit ‘capstone’ experience (the LLM Environmental and Energy Law Research Seminar or a faculty-approved research paper).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Juridical Science
Requirements: The J.S.D. is Berkeley Law’s most advanced law degree. It is designed for those interested in academia and requires a high degree of independent research and writing. The program is limited to a small number of exceptional students who have already completed an LL.M. degree. All applicants must have already completed (or be in the final year of) an LL.M. degree at Berkeley Law or a similarly high-ranked law school in the U.S. or another common-law country. Application materials include: an Online LSAC application, application fee, Curriculum Vitae, Personal Statement (2-3 pages), Dissertation Proposal, Writing Sample (in English), Two Letters of Recommendation (three are preferred), Transcripts/Academic Records, and English Language Proficiency.
Description: The Doctor of Juridical Science (J.S.D.) is Berkeley Law’s most advanced law degree. It is designed for those who want to pursue a career in legal education and who want to engage in scholarly research and writing in a particular field of law. J.S.D. candidates are expected to produce a dissertation that will make a substantial and original contribution to legal scholarship.

ProgramName: Juris Doctor
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. All applicants are required to take the Law School Admission Test (LSAT) or the Graduate Record Exam (GRE). Application components include a personal statement, a current resume, and two letters of recommendation. Applicants must also register with the Law School Admission Council (LSAC) Credential Assembly Service (CAS).
Concentration: Business Law, Energy & Clean Technology Law, Environmental Law, Intellectual Property & Technology Law, International Law, and Public Interest & Social Justice Law
Description: Berkeley Law is one of the nation’s premier law schools. Its curriculum is one of the most comprehensive and innovative in the country, and its faculty is composed of many of the world’s leading scholars and practitioners. The law school offers several degree programs, including the Juris Doctor (J.D.), the Master of Laws (LL.M.), the Doctor of the Science of Law (J.S.D.), and the Ph.D. in Jurisprudence and Social Policy (JSP). The law school also offers several joint degree programs with other departments on campus. Berkeley Law students are high achievers with a commitment to making a difference. They are also incredibly diverse in terms of their backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives.
Accredidation: The School of Law is accredited by the Council of the Section of Legal Education and Admissions to the Bar of the American Bar Association.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Linguistics
Requirements: Applicants to the graduate program in linguistics must have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A previous degree in linguistics is not required, but applicants should have a clear idea of why they want to pursue graduate study in the field. Selection is based on the applicant's prior academic record, letters of recommendation, statement of purpose, and a sample of written work.
Description: The Department of Linguistics offers a graduate program leading to the Doctor of Philosophy degree. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the core areas of linguistics and to allow them to specialize in one or more areas of research. The department has a long-standing reputation for excellence in research and teaching, and our faculty and students are engaged in a wide range of linguistic research, including phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, historical linguistics, sociolinguistics, psycholinguistics, and cognitive linguistics.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Logic and the Methodology of Science
Requirements: To apply for the Doctor of Philosophy in Logic and the Methodology of Science, applicants must have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution with a minimum GPA of 3.0. Required application materials include three letters of recommendation, official transcripts from all institutions attended after high school, a statement of purpose, a personal history statement, a curriculum vitae, and a writing sample. The GRE General Test is not required for admission to this program.
Description: The Group in Logic and the Methodology of Science at the University of California, Berkeley, offers an interdisciplinary program of study leading to the degree of Doctor of Philosophy. The program is designed for students with a strong background in mathematics or philosophy who wish to pursue research in logic, the foundations of mathematics, or the philosophy of science.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), Graduate Student Researchers (GSR)

ProgramName: Master of Engineering in Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: The Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) program is designed for students who want to develop their technical expertise while also gaining business and leadership skills. This degree is intended for students who want to work in industry after graduation. Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution, a minimum GPA of 3.0, and a background in a physical science or engineering.
Concentration: Biomaterials, Chemical and Electrochemical Materials, Computational Materials, Electronic, Magnetic and Optical Materials, and Structural Materials
Description: The Department of Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Engineering (MEng), Master of Science (MS), and the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees. Materials science and engineering is a multidisciplinary field that applies the fundamental principles of physics, chemistry, and biology to design, characterize, and manufacture the materials that underpin our modern world. Graduate students in MSE have the opportunity to work with world-class faculty on cutting-edge research in areas such as biomaterials, chemical and electrochemical materials, computational materials, electronic, magnetic and optical materials, and structural materials. The Master of Engineering (MEng) is a professionally oriented program designed to develop business and leadership skills for students who want to become leaders in the technology industry.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: To be considered for admission, applicants must have a bachelor's degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale. Required application materials include: Evidence of English Language Proficiency, three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and a Resume/CV. The GRE is not required.
Concentration: Biomaterials; Chemical and Electrochemical Materials Science and Engineering; Computational Materials Science and Engineering; Electronic, Magnetic and Optical Materials; Structural Materials
Description: Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) is a multidisciplinary field that explores the relationship between the structure of materials at atomic or molecular scales and their macroscopic properties. Materials scientists and engineers work to understand and manipulate these relationships to design and develop new materials for a wide range of applications, including electronics, energy, medicine, and aerospace.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution. The Graduate Division requires a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) or better. The Department of Materials Science and Engineering requires that all applicants have a minimum 3.0 GPA. Evidence of English language proficiency, if your native language is not English, is also required. Required documents include: Statement of purpose, Personal history statement, three letters of recommendation, official transcripts, and a current CV. GRE: Not required.
Description: Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) is a discipline that investigates the relationship between the structure of materials at atomic or molecular scales and their macroscopic properties. Materials scientists and engineers at Berkeley and elsewhere are at the forefront of modern technology. Many of the most exciting areas of engineering involve the design and development of new materials for applications in the electronics, computing, energy, and healthcare industries. MSE is a highly interdisciplinary field, drawing upon the principles of physics, chemistry, and biology to understand and control the behavior of materials. Graduate students at Berkeley work with faculty and researchers across various departments and laboratories, including the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. Students in the graduate program learn the basic principles of materials science and engineering through a core curriculum and specialized courses in their research areas. They also gain research experience by working with world-class faculty in state-of-the-art facilities. The program provides students with the skills and knowledge needed to pursue careers in academia, industry, or government.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Mathematics
Requirements: Applicants are expected to have a solid background in mathematics. Most successful applicants have taken some or all of the following upper division courses: real and complex analysis, abstract algebra, linear algebra, topology and differential geometry. The following items must be submitted via the online application: 1. Statement of Purpose: Describe your aptitude and motivation for graduate study in your area of specialization, including your preparation for this field of study, your academic plans or research interests, and your future career goals. 2. Personal History Statement: Describe how your personal background informs your decision to pursue a graduate degree. 3. Three letters of recommendation: These should be submitted via the online application. 4. Transcripts: Upload copies of transcripts for all college-level coursework. 5. GRE Scores: The GRE General Test and the GRE Mathematics Subject Test are required. 6. TOEFL/IELTS scores: If you have completed at least one year of full-time academic course work with grades of B or better at a recognized U.S. institution, you do not need to take a standardized test. Instead, you must upload an unofficial transcript from the U.S. institution.
Description: The Ph.D. program is designed for students who wish to pursue a career in research and/or teaching. The centerpiece of the program is the doctoral dissertation, which must be a finished piece of original research. There are no course requirements; however, students are expected to complete two semesters of a proseminar and three semesters as a Graduate Student Instructor (GSI). The Ph.D. is awarded on the basis of a demonstration of significant achievement in math research and a high level of proficiency in the field. Specializations within the Department of Mathematics include almost all the major areas of contemporary research: algebra, analysis, geometry, topology, logic, number theory, and many others. We also offer an emphasis in applied mathematics.
ScholarshipType: Departmental fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSIs), and Graduate Student Researchers (GSRs)

ProgramName: Master of Engineering in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution and have a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0. Application requirements include undergraduate transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and a current resume or CV. For the Master of Engineering in Mechanical Engineering, the GRE is not required for the current application cycle. International applicants must also demonstrate English language proficiency through the TOEFL or IELTS exams.
Concentration: Advanced Energy Technology, Aerospace Engineering, Biomechanics, Control of Robotic and Autonomous Systems, Design, Fluids and Ocean, MEMS/Nano, Mechanics, Modeling and Simulation of Physical Systems, Product Design
Description: The Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) program is a professional degree designed for students who plan to enter industry and want to develop their technical skills and leadership potential. The program combines advanced technical coursework with a core leadership curriculum in business and management. Students choose from one of 10 concentrations and complete a capstone project that focuses on solving real-world challenges.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: The minimum graduate admission requirements are: (1) A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; (2) A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and (3) Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. Applicants must also provide three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and a current Resume/CV.
Concentration: Biomechanical Engineering, Controls, Design, Dynamics, Energy Science and Technology, Fluid Mechanics, Manufacturing, Materials and Mechanics, Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS), Nanoscale Science and Engineering, Ocean Engineering
Description: The Mechanical Engineering Department at Berkeley offers four graduate degrees: the Master of Engineering (M.Eng.), the Master of Science (M.S.), the Master of Science/Doctor of Philosophy (M.S./Ph.D.), and the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.). In the Mechanical Engineering department, we have a very clear mission: to provide our students with the best possible education, to conduct research that will benefit society, and to serve our profession and the community. Our graduate program is one of the best in the world, and our students have the opportunity to work with world-class faculty on cutting-edge research.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: To apply for the Doctor of Philosophy in Mechanical Engineering at UC Berkeley, applicants must have a Bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution with a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale. Required application materials include an online application, official transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, a personal history statement, and a current resume. For international applicants, evidence of English Language Proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS) is required. The General Record Examination (GRE) is not required for the current application cycle.
Concentration: Biomechanical Engineering, Controls, Design, Dynamics, Energy Science and Technology, Fluids, Manufacturing, Materials, Mechanics, Micro and Nano Systems, and Ocean Engineering
Description: The Ph.D. degree is intended for students who wish to pursue a career in research and/or teaching in an academic or industrial environment. It is awarded for original and significant research as well as for proficiency in the chosen area of study. This research is expected to be of such high quality that it could be published in a peer-reviewed journal.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructor positions, and Graduate Student Researcher positions)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Media Studies
Doctor of Philosophy in Medical Anthropology
Requirements: The Department of Anthropology admits students for the PhD degree only. Our program is for students who intend to pursue a career in research and teaching. We do not have a Master’s degree program. We also have a Joint Program in Medical Anthropology (PhD) with the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF). Applications for the Medical Anthropology program are only accepted in even-numbered years (e.g., 2024, 2026, etc.) to UC Berkeley and in odd-numbered years (e.g., 2023, 2025, etc.) to UC San Francisco. Basic requirements include the Online Graduate Application, Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Transcripts, Letters of Recommendation (3), Writing Sample, and Resume/Curriculum Vitae.
Description: The Joint Degree Program in Medical Anthropology is a Ph.D. program offered by the Department of Anthropology at UC Berkeley and the Department of Humanities and Social Sciences (formerly Anthropology, History and Social Medicine) at UCSF. The program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive background in social and cultural anthropology, and to prepare them for research and teaching in the field of medical anthropology.
ScholarshipType: multi-year funding package (includes tuition, health insurance, and a stipend); Berkeley Fellowship, Chancellor’s Fellowship, and COTA Fellowship

ProgramName: Master of Science in Metabolic Biology
Requirements: Online application to the Graduate Division; Transcript (official or unofficial) from each college or university attended; Graduate Record Exam (GRE): GRE scores are NOT required for the Metabolic Biology MS or PhD application; Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or International English Language Testing System (IELTS) (if applicable); Three Letters of Recommendation; Resume/CV; Statement of Purpose; Personal History Statement; Application Fee.
Description: The Metabolic Biology graduate program focuses on the study of the biochemical and molecular basis of metabolic processes and how these are integrated at the level of the whole organism. Our faculty research a broad range of topics, including the control of metabolism and the physiological consequences of metabolic dysregulation, such as obesity, diabetes, and cancer. Students in the program gain expertise in metabolic regulation, nutrition, and disease pathophysiology. The program offers both a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) and a Master of Science (M.S.) degree.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) positions, and Graduate Student Instructor (GSI) positions

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Metabolic Biology
Requirements: Graduate applicants are first reviewed by the faculty in the Graduate Program in Metabolic Biology. Students with a background in nutrition, biology, and/or chemistry are encouraged to apply. Prerequisites: 1 year general chemistry with lab, 1 year organic chemistry with lab, 1 semester biochemistry, 1 semester physiology, 1 semester molecular biology.
Description: The graduate program in Metabolic Biology (MB) offers a program of study and research leading to the PhD or MS degree. The MB program focuses on the study of how nutrients and metabolites regulate gene expression, signal transduction, and physiological processes. Research in the MB program spans a wide range of topics, including the regulation of lipid, carbohydrate, and protein metabolism; the molecular basis of metabolic diseases such as obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease; and the role of metabolism in aging and cancer. Students in the MB program will receive training in the latest techniques in biochemistry, molecular biology, cell biology, and physiology, and will have the opportunity to work with world-renowned faculty in a highly collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment. The goal of the program is to prepare students for careers in academia, industry, and government, where they can make significant contributions to the field of metabolic biology and the improvement of human health.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR), Graduate Student Instructor (GSI)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Microbiology
Requirements: Basic requirements for admission include: (1) A bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. (2) A minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale. (3) Background in the biological and physical sciences. GRE scores are NOT required for applicants to our graduate programs. International students must also demonstrate English proficiency through TOEFL or IELTS exams.
Description: The Graduate Program in Microbiology is a PhD program that involves 50+ faculty from diverse departments, including Plant & Microbial Biology; Molecular & Cell Biology; Public Health; Chemistry; Civil & Environmental Engineering; Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering; and Environmental Science, Policy & Management. Research is focused in four areas: Ecology and Evolution; Genetics and Development; Physiology and Biochemistry; and Host-Microbe Interactions.
ScholarshipType: Full support (Stipend, tuition, and fees covered)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Middle Eastern Studies
Requirements: Applicants must meet the minimum graduate admission requirements of the University of California, Berkeley. These include a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0. The program requires three letters of recommendation, official transcripts, a Statement of Purpose, and a Personal History Statement. Applicants must also provide a writing sample and a Resume/Curriculum Vitae. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission to this program.
Department: College of Letters & Science (Middle Eastern Studies Graduate Group)
Description: The Middle Eastern Studies program is designed for students who wish to pursue a multidisciplinary program of study and research on the Middle East. The program is intended to allow students to combine a social science or humanities discipline with the study of a particular region or period of the Middle East. Students are expected to attain a high level of proficiency in at least one Middle Eastern language.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Fellowships)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Molecular and Cell Biology
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0. A strong background in biology, chemistry, and mathematics is expected. The GRE General Test is no longer required and will not be considered for admission. Required application materials include a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, a Curriculum Vitae (CV), and three letters of recommendation.
Concentration: Biochemistry, Biophysics and Structural Biology; Cell Biology, Development and Physiology; Genetics, Genomics, Evolution, and Development; Immunology and Molecular Medicine; Neurobiology
Description: The Department of Molecular and Cell Biology (MCB) is one of the largest academic departments at UC Berkeley. In MCB, the study of biological processes focuses on the organization and function of organisms at the molecular and cellular level. MCB research and teaching are focused on the molecular and cellular basis of life, including biochemistry, biophysics, structural biology, cell biology, developmental biology, genetics, genomics, and neurobiology. The MCB Graduate Program is designed to prepare students for a career in research and teaching in molecular and cell biology. The program is organized into five divisions: Biochemistry, Biophysics and Structural Biology (BBS); Cell Biology, Development and Physiology (CDP); Genetics, Genomics, Evolution, and Development (GGED); Immunology and Molecular Medicine (IMM); and Neurobiology (NEU).

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Music
Requirements: The Penn State Graduate School requires: Complete Penn State Graduate School application, TOEFL or IELTS scores (if applicable), and official transcripts. The Master of Arts in Music (MA) specifically requires: GPA of 3.0 or higher, three letters of recommendation, a resume, Statement of Purpose, and writing sample (or samples).
Concentration: Composition, Ethnomusicology, and Musicology
Description: The Department of Music offers programs of study leading to the MA and PhD degrees in composition, ethnomusicology, and musicology. For each of these three areas of specialization, the MA is usually a prerequisite for the PhD; however, students who already hold an MA or its equivalent from another institution may be admitted directly to the PhD program. The MA/PhD program is intended for students who intend to work toward the PhD. The department does not offer a terminal MA.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Fellowships)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Music
Requirements: Admission to the PhD in Music at UC Berkeley requires a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution, or its equivalent, with a grade-point average (GPA) of at least 3.0. Applicants should have a background in music equivalent to the music major at UC Berkeley. Required application materials include official transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and a Curriculum Vitae (CV). For applicants in the scholarship tracks (Musicology and Ethnomusicology), recent writing samples are required. For applicants in the Composition track, three scores and recordings of their music are required. The GRE is not required for admission.
Concentration: Composition, Ethnomusicology, Musicology
Description: The Department of Music offers programs of study leading to the PhD degree in composition and the PhD degree in scholarship (history and literature of music or ethnomusicology). These programs are intended for students who intend to pursue careers in research and teaching at the college or university level, or in composition.
ScholarshipType: Fellowship, Teaching Assistantship, Research Assistantship

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Near Eastern Studies
Requirements: Applications are considered once a year for the fall semester only. Applicants for admission to the doctoral program should have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. Although a master's degree is not required, applicants with an MA in the field or a related one are given preference. Students should have a reading knowledge of at least one of the languages in their field of concentration (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, or Turkish; or ancient Near Eastern languages, such as Akkadian, Egyptian, or Sumerian). Additional requirements: Three letters of recommendation, Current CV, Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Writing sample (not to exceed 30 pages).
Concentration: Ancient Near Eastern Civilizations; Egyptology; Hebrew Bible/Old Testament; Islamic Studies; Jewish Studies; and Near Eastern Art and Archaeology
Description: The Department of Near Eastern Studies offers graduate programs in the languages, literatures, and civilizations of the Near East from ancient times to the present. The department offers a variety of programs leading to the Master of Arts and the Doctor of Philosophy. Students choose to specialize in one of several areas: Ancient Near Eastern Civilizations; Egyptology; Hebrew Bible/Old Testament; Islamic Studies; Jewish Studies; and Near Eastern Art and Archaeology.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Fellowships, Research Assistantships, Teaching Assistantships)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Neuroscience
Requirements: The minimum graduate admission requirements are: A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field.
Description: The Helen Wills Neuroscience Institute (HWNI) is the locus for campus-wide multidisciplinary neuroscience research at UC Berkeley. The institute is composed of over 70 faculty members from many departments including Molecular and Cell Biology, Psychology, Integrative Biology, Vision Science, Physics, Chemistry, Engineering, and Environmental Science Policy and Management. The Neuroscience Graduate Program offers a premier research and training environment for students who wish to pursue a PhD in Neuroscience. The research of the HWNI faculty spans the full breadth of modern neuroscience, from the molecules that allow neurons to communicate, to the circuits that allow us to see and hear, and the complex brain processes that underlie our behaviors, such as memory and decision making.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructor (GSI), and Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) positions

ProgramName: Master of Engineering in Nuclear Engineering
Requirements: In addition to the University’s basic requirements for admission, the department requires a basic background in physics and mathematics, including calculus and differential equations. An undergraduate degree in engineering, physics, or mathematics is recommended.
Concentration: Advanced Nuclear Reactors; Nuclear Materials and Manufacturing; Nuclear Waste Management; Medical Physics and Radiation Imaging
Description: The Master of Engineering (MEng) program is designed for students who want to become leaders in industry and want to focus on their career in an area of technical specialization. Students will take a combination of technical courses and leadership courses, and will complete a capstone project.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Nuclear Engineering
Requirements: The minimum requirement for admission to graduate study in the Department of Nuclear Engineering is a bachelor’s degree in engineering, physics, chemistry, or mathematics from an accredited institution. Applicants must have a grade point average of at least 3.0 (B) for the last two years of undergraduate study. The department also requires three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, and a Personal History Statement.
Description: The graduate programs in nuclear engineering are designed to provide a broad education in the fundamental science and technology of nuclear processes and their applications. The department offers several options for graduate study: the Master of Science (MS), the Master of Engineering (MEng), the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), and the Doctor of Engineering (DE). Students may choose to focus their studies in areas such as nuclear reactor theory and design, nuclear materials, fusion engineering, nuclear thermal hydraulics, nuclear waste management, and nuclear non-proliferation. The MS program is designed to provide a solid foundation for more advanced study or for a career in industry or research.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Nuclear Engineering
Requirements: A bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale. To apply, submit the UC Berkeley Graduate Division online application. Required documents include: official transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, and a personal history statement. Applicants for admission to the graduate program in Nuclear Engineering are expected to have completed an undergraduate program in physical science or engineering.
Description: The Department of Nuclear Engineering offers a wide range of graduate study and research in nuclear technology. In keeping with the department’s traditions, research and teaching are maintained at the highest level of scholarship. The primary areas of study and research are: applied nuclear physics; nuclear materials and chemistry; nuclear energy systems and safety analysis; and nuclear thermal hydraulics. Students can also participate in other interdisciplinary programs such as fusion research, nuclear security, bioengineering, and many more. The department also participates in the Graduate Group in Energy and Resources.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, research assistantships, and teaching assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Science in Nutritional Sciences and Toxicology
Requirements: The Department of Nutritional Sciences and Toxicology (NST) requires applicants to have had sufficient undergraduate preparation in chemistry (organic and physical) and biology (including molecular biology and biochemistry). Applicants are required to have a Bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum grade point average of B (3.0) or better.
Concentration: Metabolic Biology
Description: The Department of Nutritional Sciences and Toxicology (NST) offers the Master of Science (MS) and the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees. The Metabolic Biology (MB) graduate program provides a comprehensive understanding of the biochemical, molecular, and physiological aspects of metabolism. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in academia, industry, and government by providing them with the necessary knowledge and research skills. Students in the program have the opportunity to work with world-class faculty on cutting-edge research projects. Research in the department spans a wide range of topics, including nutrient-gene interactions, metabolic regulation, cell signaling, and the role of nutrients and phytochemicals in health and disease. Students gain a deep understanding of the physiological and molecular mechanisms by which nutrients and toxicants affect human health.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructor (GSI) positions, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) positions

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Nutritional Sciences and Toxicology
Requirements: Applicants for the Ph.D. in Nutritional Sciences and Toxicology must have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution with a minimum GPA of 3.0. Required prerequisite coursework includes General Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Physiology, Calculus, and Statistics. The application requires a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, a Resume/CV, and three letters of recommendation. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission to this program.
Concentration: Metabolic Biology, Toxicology
Description: The Graduate Program in Nutritional Sciences and Toxicology (NST) provides students with the opportunity to pursue research in a variety of areas, including metabolic biology, molecular and cellular nutrition, and toxicology. The department's mission is to educate students in the biochemical and molecular basis of nutrient function and metabolism, and the mechanisms of action of toxic substances. Research in the department spans a wide range of topics, including the study of metabolic diseases such as obesity and diabetes, the role of nutrients in gene expression, and the impact of environmental toxins on human health.

ProgramName: Doctor of Optometry
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the UC Berkeley School of Optometry, you must: Have a minimum overall 3.00 GPA (on a 4.00 scale) for all college coursework; Complete the required prerequisite courses; Take the OAT (Optometry Admission Test); Demonstrate your potential through a variety of experiences; Submit three letters of recommendation; Provide a personal statement; Complete the online application and pay the application fee.
Department: Herbert Wertheim School of Optometry & Vision Science
Description: The Herbert Wertheim School of Optometry & Vision Science at the University of California, Berkeley offers the Doctor of Optometry (OD) degree. Our four-year professional program (OD) leads to the Doctor of Optometry degree. Our curriculum is designed to provide you with the clinical and theoretical knowledge required for the practice of optometry. You will learn to diagnose, treat, and manage conditions and diseases of the eye and visual system. The program provides a rigorous, comprehensive curriculum that prepares students for a career in clinical practice, research, and academia. Our program combines classroom instruction, laboratory work, and extensive clinical experience.
Accredidation: The Doctor of Optometry (OD) degree program at the University of California, Berkeley, Herbert Wertheim School of Optometry & Vision Science is accredited by the Accreditation Council on Optometric Education (ACOE).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and Need-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Studies
Requirements: Admission to the Ph.D. program in Performance Studies is highly selective. Successful applicants have strong academic backgrounds and demonstrate an interest in the study of performance as a central site of social and cultural life. Students with undergraduate or Master’s degrees in any relevant field are encouraged to apply.
Description: The UC Berkeley PhD in Performance Studies is an interdisciplinary program that draws on a wide range of faculty and resources from across the campus. It is designed to provide students with a rigorous foundation in the history, theory, and practice of performance, with a particular focus on the ways in which performance intersects with social, political, and cultural issues. Students in the program have the opportunity to work with faculty from a variety of departments, including Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies; Music; Rhetoric; English; Anthropology; and Ethnic Studies, among others. The program prepares students for careers in academia, as well as for leadership roles in the arts and other fields.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Philosophy
Requirements: In addition to the University’s Academic Requirements, applicants must also meet the following program requirements: A writing sample (not to exceed 20 pages) is required. A statement of purpose and a personal statement are required. Three letters of recommendation are required. Current Resume or Curriculum Vitae. For fall 2025, the GRE is not required.
Description: The graduate program in philosophy is designed to lead to the degree of Doctor of Philosophy. The program provides a strong foundation in the history of philosophy and the main areas of contemporary philosophical inquiry, while allowing students to specialize in their areas of interest. The department offers courses and seminars in logic, ethics, social and political philosophy, metaphysics, epistemology, philosophy of mind, philosophy of language, philosophy of science, and the history of philosophy (including ancient, medieval, and modern).
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), and Graduate Student Researchers (GSR)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Physics
Requirements: The UC Berkeley Physics Department graduate program is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a Ph.D. The department does not offer a separate M.A. degree. The Ph.D. program is intended to prepare students for careers in research and teaching. The following list of items is required for the application: 1. Resume/CV, 2. Personal Statement, 3. Three Letters of Recommendation, 4. Transcripts, 5. Statement of Purpose, 6. The TOEFL or the IELTS (International Students only). We no longer require or accept GRE scores (General and Subject). These scores will not be considered if submitted.
Description: The Ph.D. program is designed to give students a thorough grounding in the fundamental principles of physics and to provide them with the opportunity to do original research in a variety of experimental and theoretical areas. During their first two years, students take a core of courses to prepare them for the Preliminary Examination and for research. These courses include: graduate-level classical mechanics, quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, and electricity and magnetism. In addition, students are encouraged to begin research as soon as possible. After passing the Preliminary Examination, students choose a research advisor and a research area.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), and Graduate Student Researchers (GSR)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Plant Biology
Requirements: Applicants should have a strong background in the biological, chemical, or physical sciences. A minimum 3.0 grade point average is required. Undergraduate preparation should include a minimum of one year each of biology, organic chemistry, and physics, and at least one semester of calculus. Required application materials include an online application, Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, transcripts, three letters of recommendation, and a current CV. The GRE General Test is not required and will not be considered for admission.
Description: The PhD program in Plant Biology at UC Berkeley provides training in modern plant biology, including genomics, proteomics, and molecular, cellular, and genetic analysis. The program’s goal is to provide students with a broad and solid foundation in the various areas of plant biology, as well as to develop their skills in independent research. Our graduate students are part of a tight-knit community that includes over 40 faculty members and approximately 100 students.
ScholarshipType: fellowship/research assistantship package

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Political Science
Requirements: The minimum graduate admission requirements are: (1) A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; (2) A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and (3) Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. The Department of Political Science requires a Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, 3 Letters of Recommendation, Official Transcripts, Resume/Curriculum Vitae, and a Writing Sample (one writing sample, no more than 30 pages). The GRE is not required.
Department: Department of Political Science, College of Letters and Science
Concentration: American Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations, Models and Politics, Political Theory, and Quantitative Methods
Description: The Department of Political Science offers a program of graduate study leading to the degree of Doctor of Philosophy. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching, and for other professional careers. It provides students with a broad knowledge of the field of political science and with the skills necessary to conduct original research.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Psychology
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0. Required application materials include a Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Curriculum Vitae (CV), three letters of recommendation, and transcripts. The GRE General Test and GRE Subject Test are no longer required for admission to this program.
Concentration: Clinical Science
Description: The Clinical Science Program at the University of California, Berkeley is a member of the Academy of Psychological Clinical Science, which is an alliance of leading, scientifically oriented, doctoral and internship training programs in clinical and health psychology in the United States and Canada. Clinical Science at Berkeley is also a charter member of the PCSAS (Psychological Clinical Science Accreditation System). Our program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue careers in research and teaching, and to provide clinical services in a variety of settings. The program is committed to a training model that integrates research and practice.
Accredidation: The Clinical Science Program at the University of California, Berkeley is accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA) and the Psychological Clinical Science Accreditation System (PCSAS).
ScholarshipType: Fellowship, Graduate Student Instructor (GSI), Graduate Student Researcher (GSR)

ProgramName: Master of Public Health
Requirements: The minimum graduate admission requirements are: (1) A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; (2) A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and (3) Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. The School of Public Health also requires three letters of recommendation and a current CV or resume. Specific concentrations within the MPH may have additional prerequisite coursework or work experience requirements.
Concentration: Biostatistics, Environmental Health Sciences, Epidemiology, Epidemiology/Biostatistics, Health and Social Behavior, Health Policy and Management, Infectious Diseases and Vaccinology, Interdisciplinary, Maternal, Child, and Adolescent Health, Public Health Nutrition
Description: The Master of Public Health (MPH) is the most common professional degree for those who wish to pursue a career in public health. The program provides a strong foundation in the core disciplines of public health while allowing students to specialize in their area of interest. The UC Berkeley School of Public Health aims to improve population health, especially for the most vulnerable, through high-quality research and education. We prepare tomorrow’s health leaders, perform transformative research, and bring together the power of local and global communities. The degree is offered in several areas of study and in a variety of formats, including two-year, 11-month, 4+1, and online tracks.
Accredidation: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and Need-based

ProgramName: Master of Science in Public Health
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution and a satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale. Required application materials include three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and a current CV or resume. Evidence of English language proficiency is required for international applicants. The GRE is not required for any graduate programs in Public Health.
Concentration: Biostatistics, Environmental Health Sciences, Epidemiology, Health Policy and Management
Description: The School of Public Health offers several programs of study leading to the following degrees: Master of Public Health (MPH), Master of Arts (MA), Master of Science (MS), Doctor of Public Health (DrPH), and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD). The Master of Public Health degree is a professional degree, designed to prepare students for a career in public health practice. The MA, MS, and PhD degrees are academic degrees, designed for students interested in a career in research or teaching. The DrPH degree is a professional degree, designed for students interested in a career in public health leadership and practice.
Accredidation: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and Need-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Public Health
Requirements: Applicants must meet the University of California, Berkeley Graduate Division minimum requirements, which include a bachelor's degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0.
