For the PhD in Public Health, applicants are generally expected to have completed a master's degree in a relevant field, though exceptional candidates with only a bachelor's degree may be considered. Required application materials include the online Graduate Application, Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Resume or Curriculum Vitae, three letters of recommendation, and unofficial transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. International applicants must also meet the English Language Proficiency requirement.
Concentration: Environmental Health Sciences, Epidemiology, Health Policy, and Infectious Diseases and Immunity
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Public Health is a research-oriented degree that provides students with the advanced knowledge and skills necessary to conduct independent research and to teach in public health and related fields. The program emphasizes the application of rigorous research methods to address complex public health problems. The program offers several areas of concentration, including Environmental Health Sciences, Epidemiology, Health Policy, and Infectious Diseases and Immunity.
Accredidation: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Research Assistantships, and Teaching Assistantships

ProgramName: Doctor of Public Health
Requirements: Applicants to the DrPH program must have a minimum of 2 years of post-degree, full-time professional experience at the time of application. In addition, an MPH or other health-related master’s or doctoral degree (e.g., MA, MS, MPP, PhD, MD, JD) is required. Completion of MPH core coursework is recommended prior to matriculation into the DrPH program.
Description: The UC Berkeley Doctor of Public Health (DrPH) is a school-wide interdisciplinary program that prepares graduates for high-level careers in public health leadership. The DrPH degree is the highest professional degree in the field of public health. This program provides students with the leadership, management, and advocacy skills to solve complex public health problems. Our students are diverse in their backgrounds and interests, and they are committed to making a difference in the world. The DrPH program is a small, highly selective, school-wide program. Students customize their curriculum based on their professional experience, professional interests, and career goals.
Accredidation: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based

ProgramName: Master of Public Policy
Requirements: The Goldman School of Public Policy (GSPP) requires all applicants to submit an online application, three letters of recommendation, a professional resume, two required essays, and official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended since high school. Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution.
Description: The Goldman School’s Master of Public Policy (MPP) program is a two-year, full-time program that emphasizes the application of analytical tools to a wide range of policy issues. The curriculum includes courses in microeconomics, quantitative analysis, political and organizational analysis, and legal analysis. Students also complete a policy internship and a Master’s thesis (Policy Analysis Exercise).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based fellowships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Public Policy
Requirements: Applicants to the doctoral program must have completed a Master's degree in public policy or a related field (e.g., economics, political science, sociology, etc.). Doctoral program applicants who do not have a Master's degree in public policy or a related field are occasionally admitted, but they are generally required to complete the first year of the GSPP MPP program before beginning the PhD program course requirements.
Description: The doctoral program is designed to prepare students for careers in university teaching and advanced policy research. It is a small, research-oriented program, with about two or three graduates per year. The program allows students to develop highly focused expertise in a particular policy area, while also becoming versatile in the multiple methodologies of public policy analysis. Our students work closely with the Goldman School faculty and are encouraged to collaborate with other faculty and doctoral students across the UC Berkeley campus.
AverageScholarshipAmount: $34,000 stipend plus full tuition and fees
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (multi-year funding package including fellowships, GSI, and GSR positions)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Range Management
Requirements: Minimum requirements for admission: A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; A satisfactory scholastic record, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. Additional Program Requirements: Letters of Recommendation (3), Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Resume/CV. The GRE General Test is not required.
Description: The Range Management Graduate Group offers a program of study leading to an MS degree in Range Management. This program is coordinated by the Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management. Range management is the specialized system of land management used to provide consumer goods and ecosystem services from non-arable lands. These lands, which include grasslands, shrublands, woodlands, and deserts, are managed by ecological rather than agronomic methods. The master’s program is designed to provide students with a) a solid foundation in the concepts and methods of range management and b) an opportunity to explore a specific problem in range management. It is particularly suited to students who have a bachelor’s degree in range management, forestry, or a related field and who wish to pursue a career in the management of rangeland resources.

ProgramName: Master of Real Estate Development + Design
Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution with a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0. Application requirements include an online application, official transcripts, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, three letters of recommendation, and a current resume. International applicants from countries where the official language is not English must submit evidence of English language proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS).
Description: The Master of Real Estate Development + Design (MRED+D) at UC Berkeley’s College of Environmental Design is an intensive, 11-month professional graduate degree program. Our curriculum centers on the four pillars of real estate development: finance, design, law, and construction. It also uniquely incorporates the principles of equity, sustainability, and resilience, preparing you to lead the creation of sustainable and vibrant urban environments. The program is designed to bridge the gap between design and real estate development, equipping students with the skills to address the complex challenges of urban development in the 21st century.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Rhetoric
Requirements: Application requirements for the Doctor of Philosophy in Rhetoric include: Official transcripts, Three letters of recommendation, Statement of purpose, Personal history statement, Writing sample (approximately 20–30 pages), and a Resume/CV. The Rhetoric department is a leading center for the study of the history and theory of rhetoric in its diverse forms: through legal and political arguments, in the literary and the visual arts, and as a philosophical and ethical practice.
Description: The Rhetoric Department is a leading center for interdisciplinary research in the humanities and social sciences. The program's strength is its multifaceted approach to the study of the history and theory of rhetorical discourse in its various forms: political, legal, scientific, and aesthetic. Rhetoric is also a primary site for the study of contemporary theory and for the development of new approaches to the study of images and visual culture. The department's faculty is known for its wide-ranging intellectual reach, and its graduate students often pursue research that crosses traditional disciplinary boundaries.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), and Graduate Student Researchers (GSR)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Romance Languages and Literatures
Requirements: The Romance Languages and Literatures (RLL) program at UC Berkeley is a joint program that allows students to specialize in two or more Romance languages (French, Italian, and Spanish) and their literatures. Minimum requirements for admission include a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution, and a grade point average of at least 3.0 (B). The RLL program requires its students to be proficient in at least two Romance languages. At least one of these should be at the level of a native speaker or a student with an undergraduate major in that language/literature. To be admitted, you should have at least some knowledge of the second language. Knowledge of a third Romance language is desirable, though not required for admission.
Description: The interdisciplinary PhD program in Romance Languages and Literatures (RLL) is offered by the departments of French, Italian Studies, and Spanish & Portuguese. Candidates work toward the PhD in Romance Languages and Literatures with an emphasis on a combination of two of the three Romance languages/literatures: French, Italian, and Spanish/Portuguese. The RLL program is designed for students whose interest in these languages and literatures and their corresponding cultures and linguistics requires a broader angle of vision than is found in a single-language department. Students specialize in two of the languages/literatures taught in the three departments (French, Italian, Spanish & Portuguese). One is designated as the student's major language, the other as the minor language. Students take courses in both languages and literatures, and they may be asked to teach in both. RLL students are also encouraged to make use of Berkeley’s many other departments and programs (e.g., Comparative Literature, Film Studies, Linguistics, Women’s Studies) to further their research and help form their dissertation committees.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Scandinavian Languages and Literatures
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0. Required application materials include three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, a writing sample (typically 15-20 pages), and a current CV/resume.
Description: The Department of Scandinavian offers a program of study leading to the MA and PhD in Scandinavian languages and literatures. The program is designed to provide students with a broad knowledge of Scandinavian literature, culture, and linguistics, and a high level of proficiency in at least one Scandinavian language. Students specialize in either the medieval or the modern period.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based fellowships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Slavic Languages and Literatures
Requirements: Prospective applicants must have an undergraduate degree from an accredited institution. At least two years of Russian or another Slavic language are required for admission to the program. Applicants must have a grade point average of at least 3.0 (B) or the equivalent in all work completed after the first two years of undergraduate study. The department requires three letters of recommendation and a writing sample of 15–20 pages. Applicants must also provide a Statement of Purpose and a Personal History Statement.
Concentration: Russian Literature, Czech Literature, Polish Literature, South Slavic Literature, or Slavic Linguistics
Description: The Department of Slavic Languages and Literatures offers programs of study leading to the MA and PhD degrees. Students are required to choose a major field (Russian, Czech, Polish, or South Slavic literatures or Slavic linguistics). To ensure that students receive a broad background, they must also choose two minor fields, one of which must be in a Slavic field (unless the major is Slavic linguistics, in which case both minors may be outside the field). This requirement may be satisfied by a minor in another Slavic literature or in Slavic linguistics, or by a minor in a related field such as another literature, history, or linguistics. All PhD students are required to take a pedagogy course in their second year and must complete at least two semesters of apprentice teaching. UC Berkeley Slavic graduates are distinguished by their preparation as both scholars and teachers. Members of the faculty represent a wide range of interests and approaches to the study of literature and linguistics.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, teaching assistantships, and research assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Social Welfare
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the MSW program, you must meet the following minimum requirements: A bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A grade point average (GPA) of B (3.0) or better. Evidence of sufficient preparation in the liberal arts and sciences. Social Work Experience: We strongly recommend that all applicants have the equivalent of at least one year (2,100 hours) of paid or volunteer social work experience.
Description: The School of Social Welfare and the School of Public Health offer a concurrent degree program for students who wish to pursue a career in the field of public health social work. This program is designed to provide students with the necessary knowledge and skills for effective practice at the intersection of these two fields. It offers a comprehensive and integrated approach to social welfare and public health, with a focus on addressing the social determinants of health and promoting health equity. The concurrent degree program is a three-year program. It is designed to be completed in six semesters of full-time study. At the end of three years, the student will have earned both the Master of Social Welfare (MSW) and the Master of Public Health (MPH) degrees.
Accredidation: The MSW program at UC Berkeley is fully accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE). The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Social Welfare
Requirements: Applicants to the PhD program in Social Welfare must meet the following minimum requirements: a bachelor's degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; a grade point average (GPA) of B (3.0) or better; evidence of capacity for doctoral-level scholarship and potential for making a significant contribution to the field of social welfare; and for most applicants, completion of a master's degree in social work or a related field. Required application materials include: Three letters of recommendation, Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Writing Sample, and a Current Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume.
Description: Berkeley Social Welfare’s PhD program prepares students for careers as scholars, researchers, and educators in the field of social welfare. Our program offers a rigorous, interdisciplinary curriculum designed to foster deep knowledge of social problems and the policies and practices designed to address them. Our PhD students learn to conduct independent research that contributes to the scientific knowledge base of the profession and informs social welfare policy and practice.
ScholarshipType: Multi-year fellowship support (stipend plus in-state tuition and fees), Graduate Student Instructor (GSI) or Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) positions

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Sociology
Requirements: The basic minimum requirement for admission to graduate study at Berkeley is a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution with a 3.0 grade-point average (GPA). Applicants are evaluated on the basis of their performance in previous academic work, the statement of purpose and personal history, the quality of the writing sample, and the strength of the letters of recommendation.
Description: The graduate program in sociology at Berkeley is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a Ph.D. It is primarily intended to prepare students for research and teaching in sociology, although some of our graduates also work in other fields. The department is a community of scholars including 30 faculty members and approximately 100 graduate students.
ScholarshipType: Multi-year funding package (Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships, and Research Assistantships)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in South and Southeast Asian Studies
Requirements: The minimum graduate admission requirements are: (1) A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; (2) A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and (3) Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. Applicants must also submit a Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, 3 Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts, and a Writing Sample.
Concentration: South Asian Studies, Southeast Asian Studies
Description: The Department of South & Southeast Asian Studies offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Arts (MA) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees in South and Southeast Asian Studies. The MA and PhD programs are intended for students who wish to pursue a career in research and teaching at the university level or to apply their knowledge of South or Southeast Asian languages and cultures in other professional contexts. Within the PhD program, there are two distinct tracks: South Asian Studies and Southeast Asian Studies. The South Asian Studies track is designed to provide students with a deep and wide-ranging knowledge of the languages and cultures of the South Asian subcontinent. Students choose a primary language of concentration (Sanskrit, Hindi, Urdu, Tamil, etc.) and a field of specialization (Literature, Religion, Philosophy, History, or Social Sciences). The Southeast Asian Studies track is designed to provide students with a deep and wide-ranging knowledge of the languages and cultures of the Southeast Asian region. Students choose a primary language of concentration (Indonesian, Khmer, Tagalog, Thai, Vietnamese, etc.) and a field of specialization (Literature, Religion, Philosophy, History, or Social Sciences).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based fellowships (e.g., Berkeley Fellowship, Chancellor's Fellowship), FLAS fellowships, and teaching/research assistantships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Spanish and Portuguese
Requirements: The Department of Spanish & Portuguese offers programs of study for the PhD in Spanish & Portuguese and the PhD in Hispanic Languages & Literatures. The department does not offer a terminal MA degree. Students are admitted to the PhD program. Students who have not yet earned an MA will earn the degree while working toward the PhD.
Concentration: Iberian and Latin American Literatures and Cultures; Luso-Brazilian Literatures and Cultures; Romance Languages and Literatures; Hispanic Languages and Literatures
Description: The graduate program in Spanish and Portuguese at Berkeley provides students with the most comprehensive education in the literatures, cultures, and languages of the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking worlds. The department offers the MA/PhD and PhD degrees in Spanish and Portuguese, with concentrations in Iberian and Latin American Literatures and Cultures and Luso-Brazilian Literatures and Cultures. We also participate in two interdisciplinary doctoral programs: Romance Languages and Literatures (offered in conjunction with the Departments of French and Italian) and Hispanic Languages and Literatures (offered in conjunction with the Department of Linguistics).
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), and Readers

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Statistics
Requirements: A bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale. For admission to the Master of Arts program, a bachelor's degree in any field is acceptable, but the applicant must have had some basic training in mathematics, including at least three semesters of calculus, a semester of linear algebra, and a semester of real analysis. In addition, some exposure to probability and statistics is desirable. International applicants from countries where the official language is not English must provide evidence of English language proficiency.
Department: Department of Statistics, College of Computing, Data Science, and Society
Description: The Department of Statistics offers three degree programs: the Ph.D., the M.A., and the Professional Master of Financial Engineering (MFE). Students in the Ph.D. program and M.A. program receive a solid foundation in statistical theory and practice. Faculty members are involved in a wide range of research projects in theoretical and applied statistics. Graduate students and faculty members benefit from the department's close ties with many researchers across the Berkeley campus and at the nearby Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. These groups offer a regular flow of visitors, many of whom give talks in the several departmental seminars. M.A. Degree: The M.A. in Statistics provides a solid foundation in statistical theory and practice and can be used as a springboard for a statistics or data science career in a variety of industries. This is a small, selective, and very fast-paced program that is usually completed in two semesters (one academic year).

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Statistics
Requirements: Prospective students should have a strong background in mathematics: at least three semesters of calculus, a course in linear algebra, and a course in real analysis. Some experience with probability and statistics is also desirable. Application Requirements: Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, 3 letters of recommendation, CV/Resume, Official Transcripts.
Description: The doctoral program in statistics is designed to give students a comprehensive knowledge of the theory and methods of statistics and probability. It is intended for students with a strong mathematical background and an interest in any area of statistics or probability. Research interests of faculty and students include many areas of statistical theory and methodology, probability theory, and the application of statistics and probability to many fields, including the biological and physical sciences, social sciences, and engineering.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), and Graduate Student Researcherships (GSR)

ProgramName: Master of Translational Medicine
Requirements: To apply for the Master of Translational Medicine, applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale. Required application materials include three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and a current resume or CV. International applicants must also demonstrate English Language Proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS). Additionally, the program requires prerequisite knowledge in Calculus (one year), Physics (one year), Chemistry (one year), and Biology (one year).
Department: Department of Bioengineering (UC Berkeley) and the Department of Bioengineering and Therapeutic Sciences (UCSF)
Description: The Master of Translational Medicine (MTM) program is a joint effort between the Department of Bioengineering at UC Berkeley and the Department of Bioengineering and Therapeutic Sciences at UCSF. The program is designed to provide students with the tools and network to take a medical innovation from the lab to the clinic. The curriculum combines engineering, clinical, and business training to prepare students for careers in the biotech and medical device industries, teaching essential skills to move innovations through the pipeline from the lab to the bedside.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (MTM Departmental Scholarships)

ProgramName: Master of Urban Design
Requirements: General application requirements include: official transcripts, evidence of English language proficiency (for international applicants), Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, three letters of recommendation, current resume/CV, and a portfolio. The GRE (Graduate Record Examination) is not required for this program.
Description: The Master of Urban Design (MUD) is a one-year (three semester) post-professional degree for those who already have a professional degree in architecture, landscape architecture, or city and regional planning. The program aims to train future leaders of urban design who can address the complex challenges of making and managing the urban environment in a rapidly urbanizing world. Urban design is an interdisciplinary field, and the program at Berkeley brings together faculty and students from the departments of Architecture, City & Regional Planning, and Landscape Architecture & Environmental Planning. The MUD program is centered on the urban design studio. Projects are based on real-world sites in the San Francisco Bay Area and elsewhere, and explore a wide range of urban scales, from the street and the block to the neighborhood and the region.
ScholarshipType: Departmental fellowships, Merit-based, Need-based

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Vision Science
Requirements: To apply for the Doctor of Philosophy in Vision Science, applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of B (3.0) or better. Required application materials include transcripts for all college-level work, three letters of recommendation, a Personal History Statement, a Statement of Purpose, and a current Resume or CV. International applicants from countries where the official language is not English must provide evidence of English Language Proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS scores). The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required.
Department: Herbert Wertheim School of Optometry & Vision Science
Description: The Vision Science Graduate Program provides comprehensive training in the many aspects of vision science, from the molecular biology of the eye to the psychology and neurophysiology of perception. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching. The Vision Science Program at UC Berkeley is an interdisciplinary program where students study the biology, physics, and psychology of sight and its impact on individuals and society. The program offers students a broad foundation in vision science while allowing them to specialize in a specific area of research, with access to state-of-the-art research facilities and world-renowned faculty.
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition and fees plus annual stipend
ScholarshipType: Merit-based fellowships, Graduate Student Research (GSR) appointments, and Graduate Student Instructor (GSI) positions

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Critical Theory
Requirements: To apply for the Designated Emphasis in Critical Theory, students must already be enrolled in a Ph.D. program at UC Berkeley. Applications are accepted twice annually. Required materials include: 1. A letter of intent (2-3 pages) describing the student’s interest in the DE, how their research relates to critical theory, and the courses they plan to take; 2. A curriculum vitae; 3. A writing sample (20-30 pages); 4. A letter of recommendation from the student’s faculty advisor supporting the application to the DE.
Description: The Designated Emphasis in Critical Theory (DE) provides graduate students already enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley with a curricular and research framework for studying the history and current developments of critical theory. The program is intended to offer students a systematic approach to the diverse traditions of critical thought that have informed modern scholarship across the humanities and social sciences. Students who complete the requirements of the DE receive a certificate of completion and the designation 'Critical Theory' on their official transcript and diploma.

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Folklore
Requirements: Admission to the designated emphasis is contingent on prior admission to a PhD program at UC Berkeley. To apply, students must provide: 1. A complete application form (available from the Folklore Program office); 2. A description of the student's research project and its relation to folklore; 3. A recommendation from the student's advisor.
Description: The Designated Emphasis in Folklore (DE) is a program for graduate students at UC Berkeley who are interested in the study of folklore and traditional culture. It is intended to provide a systematic and integrated curriculum of study for students who wish to pursue a concentration in folklore as part of their PhD program. The Designated Emphasis in Folklore is not a degree-granting program. Rather, it is an interdisciplinary program that offers a specialization in folklore to students who are already enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley.

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Women, Gender, and Sexuality
Requirements: Only currently enrolled UC Berkeley PhD students are eligible to apply for a Designated Emphasis. Applicants must submit: 1. A complete Application for Admission to the Designated Emphasis in Women, Gender, and Sexuality. 2. A brief statement of purpose (no more than 2 pages) describing the student's research interests and its relationship to Women, Gender, and Sexuality. 3. A letter of recommendation from a member of the Women, Gender, and Sexuality Graduate Group who has agreed to serve on the student's exam and/or dissertation committee. 4. A curriculum vitae.
Department: Department of Gender and Women’s Studies
Description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Women, Gender, and Sexuality provides graduate students with the opportunity to specialize in women, gender, and sexuality studies while completing their PhD degree. It is designed to provide a formal structure for interdisciplinary work and to recognize the importance of research and teaching in this area. The DE offers students a program of study that includes a core course, electives, and a dissertation with a significant focus on women, gender, and/or sexuality.

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in European Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for the Designated Emphasis in European Studies, students must be enrolled in an existing PhD program at UC Berkeley. Admission is by application to the DE Committee. Required documents for the application include a completed application form, a statement of purpose (no more than 2 pages) describing the student’s interest in European Studies and how it relates to their doctoral research, a letter of recommendation from the student’s faculty advisor in their home department, and a curriculum vitae.
Description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in European Studies is available to Berkeley Ph.D. students in any department or program. It provides an opportunity for students to engage in interdisciplinary research on Europe, and to have that expertise recognized with a formal credential. Students must satisfy requirements in three categories: course work, a required language, and a dissertation with a European focus. Students should apply as soon as they decide to pursue the DE. The latest a student can apply is one semester before the Ph.D. qualifying exam.

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Nanoscale Science and Engineering
Requirements: Admission to the DE is by application to the DE Graduate Group. To be eligible to apply, students must be in good standing in a participating PhD program. Ideally, students should apply for the DE after their first or second year of graduate study, but before taking the PhD Qualifying Exam. Application requirements include: 1. Completion of the application form including the signature of the student’s PhD advisor. 2. Preparation of a 1-2 page statement of interest that includes: a description of the student’s research interests and its relationship to Nanoscale Science and Engineering, and how the student intends to fulfill the DE requirements (including a proposed list of courses). 3. Letter of Recommendation from the PhD advisor.
Department: Nanoscale Science and Engineering Graduate Group
Description: The Nanoscale Science and Engineering Graduate Group (NSEGG) offers a Designated Emphasis (DE) in Nanoscale Science and Engineering (NSE). The DE in NSE is an interdisciplinary program that provides graduate students with a comprehensive education in the fundamental science and engineering of nanoscale structures. NSE is a rapidly growing field with profound implications for technology, medicine, and the environment. The program aims to train the next generation of researchers and leaders in this exciting field, fostering cross-disciplinary collaboration and providing students with the skills and knowledge needed to excel in this competitive landscape.

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Energy Sciences and Technology
Requirements: To apply for the Designated Emphasis in Energy Science and Technology (DEEST), students must: 1. Be a doctoral student in good standing at UC Berkeley. 2. Be enrolled in a PhD program in one of the participating departments (College of Engineering, College of Chemistry, College of Natural Resources, or Department of Physics). 3. Complete the DEEST Application Form. 4. Provide a one-page statement of interest. 5. Provide a letter of recommendation from the student’s faculty advisor. 6. Provide a transcript (unofficial is okay).
Description: The Designated Emphasis in Energy Science and Technology (DEEST) is an interdisciplinary program that provides a framework for doctoral students to specialize in energy science and technology. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the fundamental principles of energy science and technology, and to introduce them to the social, economic, and policy aspects of energy systems. The DEEST provides an opportunity for doctoral students from a variety of engineering and science departments to engage in a curriculum that includes energy-related coursework and research.

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Communication, Computation and Statistics
Requirements: To be admitted to the DE in Communication, Computation, and Statistics (CCS), a student must already be enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley. Students should apply to the DE as early as possible in their graduate career, but no later than the semester of their PhD Qualifying Examination. To apply, students must submit an application form, a letter of support from their PhD advisor, and a short statement of interest.
Description: The Designated Emphasis in Communication, Computation and Statistics (DECCS) provides students with a strong background in the methods of communication, computation, and statistics, as applied to the social sciences. The DECCS is intended for doctoral students in social science departments (e.g., Sociology, Political Science, Economics, etc.) who want to learn how to apply these methods to their research. The DECCS provides a curriculum that covers the fundamentals of communication, computation, and statistics, as well as more advanced topics in these areas. Students who complete the DECCS will be well-prepared for careers in academia, government, and the private sector. Upon successful completion of the dissertation and the DECCS requirements, the student’s transcript will include the notation ‘Designated Emphasis in Communication, Computation and Statistics’.

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Computational and Genomic Biology
Requirements: To be admitted to the DE, students must already be enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley. The student must have the support of his/her PhD advisor to join the DE, and the student’s PhD advisor must be a core or affiliate faculty member of the Center for Computational Biology. Application consists of an application form, a one-page statement of interest, and a letter of support from the student’s faculty advisor.
Description: Computational biology is a central field in modern biology. The Designated Emphasis in Computational and Genomic Biology (DE CGB) is intended to provide curriculum and training in the field to students in doctoral programs across the Berkeley campus. The DE CGB provides students with a solid foundation in the principles of biology, statistics, and computer science, as well as the ability to apply these principles to the analysis of genomic data.

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in New Media
Requirements: To be eligible for the Designated Emphasis in New Media, students must be enrolled in a Ph.D. program at UC Berkeley. Admission to the DE is by application to the Berkeley Center for New Media. Students are encouraged to apply for the DE as early as possible in their doctoral studies, and MUST apply prior to their qualifying examination.
Description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in New Media provides Berkeley doctoral students with a set of curricular and research resources for studying the impact of new media on traditional disciplines. It is an interdisciplinary program that involves more than two dozen faculty from across the campus. The DE provides students with a common set of theoretical and methodological tools for research on new media and brings them into a community of researchers who are exploring the field.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Global Urban Humanities
Requirements: To be admitted to the DE, students must already be enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley. Application requirements include a completed application form, a brief (1-2 page) letter of intent addressed to the GUH DE Admissions Committee describing the student’s research interest in the DE and their relevant background, an unofficial transcript of UC Berkeley coursework, and a letter of support from the student’s faculty advisor in their home department.
Description: The Graduate Designated Emphasis (DE) in Global Urban Humanities provides an interdisciplinary framework for the study of the city. Students investigate the histories and cultures of cities as they interact with the physical and social environments. The curriculum includes a core course, Global Urban Humanities: Theories and Methods, and two electives, as well as an interdisciplinary research studio. The DE allows students in the humanities, social sciences, and environmental design to engage in shared study and research, bridging the gap between descriptive and interpretive methods and the projective and diagnostic tools of the design and planning disciplines. Students in PhD programs across the campus are eligible to apply.

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Development Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible, students must be currently enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley. The application consists of a statement of interest (no more than 2 pages) describing the student’s research interests and how they relate to development engineering, a letter of recommendation from the student’s faculty advisor, and a list of courses that will be used to satisfy the Designated Emphasis requirements.
Description: Development Engineering (DE) is an interdisciplinary field that addresses the problems of people living in poverty. Building on the core strengths of UC Berkeley in engineering and the social sciences, the program focuses on creating technology-based solutions to solve global development problems. The DE provides students with a set of tools to create, pilot, and evaluate technology that could improve the lives of those in low-resource settings. Students learn how to measure the impact of their work and how to think about the economic and social context of their technical solutions.

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Science and Technology Studies
Requirements: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Science and Technology Studies is an interdisciplinary program of study open to students already enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley. Students are required to take a core course, three electives, and include an STS faculty member on their qualifying exam and dissertation committees. To apply for admission to the DE in STS, please submit: A 1–2 page Statement of Purpose describing your interest in STS and the relationship of the DE to your program of study. An application form. A letter of recommendation from a member of the STS affiliated faculty who is willing to serve as your DE advisor. A memo or email from your Head Graduate Advisor in your home department confirming that you are a student in good standing and that they have no objection to your participating in the DE.
Description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Science and Technology Studies (STS) provides a curated course of study for Berkeley PhD students who want to develop a rigorous, interdisciplinary approach to their work. The program is designed to provide students with a theoretical and methodological foundation in the social studies of science, technology and medicine. It is intended to help students from a wide range of disciplines to communicate with researchers from other fields, and to facilitate the development of a common set of questions and research methods. The DE will provide students with a formal credential in STS, and will help to create a community of scholars who are interested in the social and cultural dimensions of science and technology. Students who complete the DE will be better prepared to participate in the global conversation about the role of science and technology in society, and will be better positioned for academic and professional opportunities in this growing field.

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Dutch Studies
Requirements: Graduate students already admitted to a PhD program at UC Berkeley are eligible to apply. Designated Emphases (DE) are specialized concentrations available to doctoral students in certain programs. Students must already be admitted to a Berkeley PhD program to apply for a DE. To apply, students must have the support of a faculty member who is affiliated with the Designated Emphasis in Dutch Studies and who will serve on the student’s qualifying exam and dissertation committees. The application must be submitted before the qualifying examination.
Description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Dutch Studies is a program that provides a framework for regular and structured contact among graduate students and faculty in different disciplines who study Dutch history, culture, linguistics, and literature. The Dutch Studies program is unique in its breadth and its interdisciplinary nature. Its goals are: To provide a structure for graduate students who would like to study Dutch history, culture, linguistics, or literature in a more formal way. To foster an interdisciplinary approach to Dutch Studies and to create a community of scholars who work in these areas. For students who choose this DE, the PhD degree will be designated with the name of the home department and the program, for example: “PhD in History with a Designated Emphasis in Dutch Studies.”

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Indigenous Language Revitalization
Requirements: To apply, students should submit to the Chair of the Graduate Group in Indigenous Language Revitalization (ilr@berkeley.edu): A statement of purpose (maximum two pages), A letter of recommendation from the student’s faculty advisor, and A letter of recommendation from another faculty member who is part of the Indigenous Language Revitalization Graduate Group. Students should apply for admission to the Indigenous Language Revitalization Graduate Group at any time after their first semester and no later than the semester before their qualifying exam.
Description: The Designated Emphasis in Indigenous Language Revitalization (DEILR) is an interdisciplinary program that offers graduate students from any department at UC Berkeley the opportunity to gain expertise in the theory and practice of language revitalization. The program is designed to prepare students for academic and professional work in this field by providing them with a solid foundation in the linguistic, pedagogical, and social aspects of language revitalization.

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Renaissance and Early Modern Studies
Requirements: Admission to the DE is by application. Students should apply in their second or third year of study, but must be admitted to the DE before taking the qualifying examination. Requirements for admission: 1. Application form. 2. Statement of interest (no more than 2 pages) explaining the student’s interest in the DE and describing the student’s research and how it will involve interdisciplinary study in Renaissance and Early Modern Studies. 3. Letter of recommendation from the student’s PhD advisor. 4. Writing sample (e.g., a paper for a course, or a draft of a dissertation chapter). 5. Curriculum Vitae (CV).
Description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Renaissance and Early Modern Studies (REMS) provides a framework for regular exchange among faculty and graduate students in different departments at Berkeley and a way to coordinate and foster the interdisciplinary study of the early modern period (roughly 1350–1750). The Designated Emphasis is open to graduate students already enrolled in a Ph.D. program in any department or school at UC Berkeley. Since 2001, students from Architecture, Comparative Literature, English, French, German, History, History of Art, Italian Studies, Music, Near Eastern Studies, Philosophy, Rhetoric, South and Southeast Asian Studies, and Spanish and Portuguese have been part of the program.
ScholarshipType: Travel Grants, Summer Research Grants

ProgramName: Designated Emphasis in Southeast Asian Studies
Requirements: Only students already enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley are eligible for the Designated Emphasis. To be admitted to the DE, students must: 1. Be admitted to a PhD program at UC Berkeley. 2. Submit an application form signed by the student’s head graduate adviser in their home department. 3. Submit a statement of intent (approximately two pages) that explains how the student’s research interest and dissertation relate to Southeast Asian studies. 4. Have a member of the DE Graduate Group on their dissertation committee.
Description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Southeast Asian Studies (SEAS) provides a framework for regularized interdisciplinary collaboration and for the professional certification of graduate students who are currently enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley and whose work has a significant focus on Southeast Asia. There is a growing number of doctoral students at Berkeley in various departments and disciplines who work on some aspect of Southeast Asia. Often these students have few opportunities to interact with each other, and they frequently feel somewhat isolated within their own departments. The Designated Emphasis in Southeast Asian Studies aims to create a community of Southeast Asianists on the Berkeley campus. Its main goal is to promote a multi-disciplinary approach to Southeast Asian studies by providing students with a systematic way of identifying a core of faculty and other students with whom they can work as they proceed through their training.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Foreign Language and Area Studies Fellowships)

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Applied Data Science
Requirements: The Graduate Certificate in Applied Data Science is open to any current UC Berkeley graduate student. To be eligible, students must be currently enrolled in a UC Berkeley graduate degree program (Master’s or Ph.D.) and be in good academic standing. Applicants are required to submit a brief statement of interest and complete an online application.
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Applied Data Science is a program for UC Berkeley graduate students in any department. The certificate program allows students to gain the skills they need to navigate the world of data and big data. Students learn the latest techniques for collecting, cleaning, analyzing, and visualizing data, and gain experience with a wide range of data science tools and technologies.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Food Systems
Requirements: Only currently enrolled UC Berkeley graduate students in good standing are eligible to apply. To apply, please complete the Graduate Certificate in Food Systems Intent to Apply form. Certificate requirements include: one 3-unit core course (either PB HLTH 204 or ESPM 230), elective courses totaling at least 8 units from at least two of three categories (Social & Economic, Environmental, and Public Health), and one capstone/integrated project.
Department: College of Natural Resources, School of Public Health, and College of Environmental Design
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Food Systems is an interdisciplinary program that allows graduate students to gain a broad and comprehensive understanding of the complex factors that influence food systems. This certificate program is open to all graduate students at UC Berkeley and is designed to provide students with the necessary tools to address the multifaceted challenges of creating a more sustainable, equitable, and healthy food system. The certificate provides a framework for students to explore how different aspects of food systems—from production and processing to distribution and consumption—are interconnected and influence health, environment, and society. Students will develop the skills to analyze and address these complexities through interdisciplinary coursework and a capstone project.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Global Urban Humanities
Requirements: The Graduate Certificate in Global Urban Humanities is open to all UC Berkeley graduate students in good standing in any department. To apply, students must submit an Application Form, a Statement of Interest (max 500 words) describing research interests and how they relate to the certificate, and a short bio (max 100 words).
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Global Urban Humanities is a certificate program for UC Berkeley graduate students in any department who are interested in the study of cities and urban life through a combination of humanistic and design/social science methods. The program is part of the Global Urban Humanities Initiative, a joint project of the Arts & Humanities Division and the College of Environmental Design. The certificate provides a framework for students to engage in interdisciplinary research and pedagogy, offering a curriculum that includes an introductory core colloquium, elective courses from departments outside the student's home discipline, and a research-intensive capstone requirement such as an interdisciplinary studio or research seminar.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Real Estate
Requirements: The Interdisciplinary Graduate Certificate in Real Estate (IGCRE) is available to any student currently enrolled in a graduate program at the University of California, Berkeley. To apply, students should submit the Intent to Register form as soon as they decide to pursue the IGCRE. To receive the certificate, students must successfully complete three courses: one from the 'Core' category (ARCH 268, LD ARCH 268, CY PLAN 213, or MBA 280) and two additional courses from the approved list, one of which must be outside the student's home department. All courses must be taken for a letter grade and a grade of B or better must be achieved. In the final semester of study, students must submit the Completion Form and a current transcript.
Department: Haas School of Business, College of Environmental Design, Berkeley Law School, and Goldman School of Public Policy
Fees.1: $0 (The Graduate Certificate in Real Estate is an add-on to the degree program and does not have any additional tuition or fees)
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Real Estate (GCRE) is available to any student currently enrolled in a graduate degree program at UC Berkeley. The certificate is a way to gain further knowledge in real estate that may not be available in their home department, and to give students a competitive edge in the job market. It is an interdisciplinary program that includes the Haas School of Business, the College of Environmental Design, the Berkeley Law School, and the Goldman School of Public Policy. The certificate is administered by the Fisher Center for Real Estate and Urban Economics at the Haas School of Business.
MinGPA: 3.0 (Grade of B or better in all course requirements)

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Teaching and Learning in Higher Education
Requirements: The Certificate Program in Teaching and Learning in Higher Education is open to currently enrolled UC Berkeley doctoral students. To receive the Certificate, students must: 1. Successfully complete the 300-level pedagogy course in their department. 2. Teach as a GSI for at least two semesters at UC Berkeley. 3. Participate in at least six qualifying workshops sponsored by the GSI Teaching & Resource Center or other Graduate Division programs. 4. Be observed teaching by a faculty member who provides a written report to the student. 5. Develop a teaching portfolio that meets the criteria established by the GSI Teaching & Resource Center.
Department: GSI Teaching & Resource Center, Graduate Division
Description: The Certificate in Teaching and Learning in Higher Education provides a structure for GSIs to refine their teaching skills and to provide them with a credential for the academic job market. The program is sponsored by the GSI Teaching & Resource Center and the Graduate Council of the Academic Senate. To receive the certificate, participants must complete a sequence of activities: a pedagogy course, teaching experience, teaching observations, and a teaching portfolio. The certificate program aims to: (1) assist GSIs in enhancing their teaching while at UC Berkeley, (2) prepare GSIs for the teaching responsibilities they will assume as future faculty, (3) provide GSIs with a credential for the job market, and (4) identify GSIs on campus who have a significant commitment to teaching and learning.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African American Studies
Requirements: To declare the African American Studies major, students must have: Completed at least one of the lower division requirements (AAS 4A or 4B) with a grade of C or better. Completed one other African American Studies course (lower or upper division) with a grade of C or better. Have at least a 2.0 overall GPA. General undergraduate admission to the University of California, Berkeley requires the completion of 15 year-long high school 'a-g' subject courses with a grade of C or better, and a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents).
Concentration: Literature and the Arts, Social Sciences, History, Development and Urban Studies, and Gender and Sexuality
Description: The Department of African American Studies is an intellectual community committed to producing, refining and helping to expand the knowledge base about people of African descent in the United States, the Caribbean, Latin America, and Africa. In keeping with the University of California's mission of 'teaching, research and public service,' our department offers a rigorous and multi-disciplinary undergraduate and graduate curriculum that aims to help students: Examine and analyze the historical, cultural, and social complexities of the African American experience; Develop the critical and analytical skills needed to understand the nuances of the African Diaspora; and Prepare for leadership and service in a global society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Studies
Requirements: To declare the major, students must have a 2.0 GPA overall and in the major, and complete AS 10 (or equivalent). It is also required that students take AS 101 within two semesters of declaring.
Description: American Studies is a diverse, rigorous, and interdisciplinary program that encourages students to design an individual course of study that investigates the history, culture, and society of the United States. In the major, students choose an area of concentration to pursue based on their individual interests. Students often focus on themes such as: racial and ethnic identities; gender and sexuality; media and popular culture; law and politics; and the United States in a global context.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Ancient Greek and Roman Studies
Requirements: To be admitted to the University of California, Berkeley, applicants must satisfy the general University of California admission requirements. For freshman applicants, this includes the completion of 'a-g' subject requirements with a grade of C or better, a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents), and the submission of Personal Insight Questions. To declare the major in Ancient Greek and Roman Studies, students must have completed at least one course in the department with a grade of C or better.
Description: The Ancient Greek and Roman Studies (AGRS) major is designed for students who want to explore the literature and culture of the ancient Mediterranean world in all its depth and range, but who prefer to do so without the intensive language requirements of the Classics or Classical Languages majors. The AGRS major provides an expansive introduction to the history, literature, and culture of the ancient world. Students will engage with a broad range of topics from different regions and time periods, and they will study a variety of primary sources, including literature, inscriptions, material culture, and art. The program also emphasizes the development of critical thinking, research, and writing skills. Many AGRS majors choose to double-major in another field, such as History, Philosophy, Art History, or English.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, freshman applicants must meet the University of California's A-G subject requirements with a grade of C or better and maintain a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). All applicants must complete the UC application, which includes the Personal Insight Questions. For the Anthropology major specifically, the program requires the completion of three lower-division core courses: Anthropology 1 (Biological Anthropology), Anthropology 2 (Introduction to Archaeology), and Anthropology 3 (Introduction to Social and Cultural Anthropology). Transfer applicants must complete 60 semester (90 quarter) units of transferable college credit and are encouraged to complete major preparation coursework prior to admission.
Description: Anthropology is the study of human beings, past and present. To understand the full sweep and complexity of cultures across all of human history, anthropology draws and builds upon knowledge from the social and biological sciences as well as the humanities and physical sciences. A central concern of anthropologists is the application of knowledge to the solution of human problems. Historically, anthropologists in the United States have been trained in one of four areas: sociocultural anthropology, biological/physical anthropology, archaeology, and linguistics. Anthropologists often integrate the perspectives of several of these areas into their research, teaching, and professional lives.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Applied Mathematics
Requirements: To apply to the Bachelor of Arts in Applied Mathematics, students must first be admitted to the University of California, Berkeley. General freshman admission requires completion of the A-G subject requirements with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) and a high school diploma or equivalent. To declare the Applied Mathematics major specifically, students must complete the following lower-division prerequisites: Math 1A (Calculus), Math 1B (Calculus), Math 53 (Multivariable Calculus), Math 54 (Linear Algebra & Differential Equations) or Math 56, and Math 55 (Discrete Mathematics). A minimum GPA of 2.0 in the prerequisite courses taken at UC Berkeley is required for major declaration.
Concentration: Statistics, Numerical Analysis, Physics, Physical Sciences, Economics, Computer Science, Operations Research, Mathematical Biology
Description: The Department of Mathematics offers an undergraduate major in Applied Mathematics leading to the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree. The Applied Mathematics major has been designed for students who want to use mathematics to solve problems in other fields. This major is particularly suitable for students who intend to work in industry, or who want to study a field such as economics or physics at the graduate level.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Architecture
Requirements: Applicants must meet the University of California’s admission requirements, which include the Subject Requirement (completing 15 year-long 'a-g' courses with a grade of C or better), the Scholarship Requirement (minimum 3.0 GPA for California residents and 3.4 for non-residents), and the completion of the University of California application including Personal Insight Questions. For the Bachelor of Arts in Architecture, admission is based on a holistic review of the applicant's academic record and personal responses.
Description: The major in architecture leads to the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree. It combines required courses in environmental design and architecture with opportunities for highly varied individual programs. Through its core courses, the program offers a broad introduction to the field of architecture, and through studies in the various areas it provides opportunities to prepare for specialization in the field in graduate study, or for work in several architecture-related fields. In addition to the course work, students may also take advantage of the college's many resources, including the Architecture Library, the Environmental Design Archives, the CED shop, and the CED computer labs.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Arts with a major in architecture is a pre-professional degree. The National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB) only accredits professional degrees (Master of Architecture). Because the Bachelor of Arts in Architecture is a pre-professional degree, it is not accredited by the NAAB.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art
Requirements: Applicants must meet general University of California undergraduate admission requirements. For freshmen, this includes high school graduation, completion of the 15 'A-G' subject requirements with a grade of C or better, and a minimum 3.0 weighted GPA (3.4 for non-residents). For transfers, completion of lower-division general education and major prerequisites is required. Admission is based on a holistic review of the UC application, including Personal Insight Questions. Notably, the Department of Art Practice does not review portfolios for undergraduate admission.
Description: The Art Practice department provides rigorous training in the practice of visual art. Students are expected to develop a clear understanding of the history of art and the relationship of their work to contemporary art. The program focuses on several key areas of art practice: painting, sculpture, printmaking, digital media, photography, and performance. The program provides a rigorous education in the practice of visual art, within the context of a world-class public research university. Art Practice students learn to think critically and creatively, to analyze visual culture, and to communicate through a variety of media.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Asian American and Asian Diaspora Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California undergraduate admission requirements: completion of 15 year-long 'a-g' subject requirements with a grade of C or better, a minimum GPA of 3.0 for California residents (3.4 for non-residents) in these courses, and completion of the Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free, meaning SAT and ACT scores are not considered for admission. For the major specifically, students must complete at least one Asian American and Asian Diaspora Studies course with a grade of C or better and have a minimum 2.0 overall GPA to declare.
Description: The program in Asian American and Asian Diaspora Studies (AAADS) is an interdisciplinary program that offers a unique perspective on the history, culture, and experiences of people of Asian descent in the United States and the diaspora. The major provides a broad overview of the Asian American experience, including the history of immigration, the development of community organizations, and the cultural and artistic expressions of Asian American communities. The major also provides students with the opportunity to focus on specific themes and issues such as labor, gender, and the environment. Through their studies, students gain a deeper understanding of the complex forces that have shaped Asian American life and the contributions of Asian Americans to the social, political, and economic life of the United States.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Asian Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, freshman applicants must meet the following: complete a minimum of 15 college-preparatory courses (A-G courses) with at least 11 finished prior to the beginning of your senior year; earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.00 or better (3.40 or better for a non-resident of California) in these courses with no grade lower than a C; and answer the Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free, which means we will not use SAT/ACT test scores in our review process.
Concentration: East Asia, Southeast Asia, and South Asia
Description: The Asian Studies major offers three areas of concentration: East Asia, Southeast Asia, and South Asia. This interdisciplinary program is designed for students who want to study Asia through several different disciplines and/or more than one of the sub-regions of Asia. Students may also focus their study of Asia on a single sub-region and a single discipline. The major is designed to provide a broad understanding of the history, culture, and society of Asia, while also providing students with the language skills necessary to engage with the region.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Astrophysics
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, freshman applicants must: 1. Complete a minimum of 15 college-preparatory courses ('a-g' courses), with at least 11 finished prior to the beginning of your last year of high school. 2. Earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 if you're a nonresident) in these courses with no grade lower than a C. 3. Respond to four Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free, which means we will not use SAT/ACT test scores in our review process.
Description: The undergraduate major in astrophysics is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in both physics and astronomy. The major is intended to prepare students for graduate study in astrophysics or related fields, as well as for careers in industry or education. Astrophysics is the study of the physical nature of the universe. It uses the tools of physics to understand the properties of stars, galaxies, and the large-scale structure of the universe, as well as the physical processes that govern them. The major includes a comprehensive set of courses in mathematics and physics, as well as a thorough introduction to the concepts and techniques of modern astronomy and astrophysics. At UC Berkeley, we have a very active department, with approximately 30 faculty, 30-40 researchers and 100 undergraduate students. Our researchers and students have access to many world-class facilities, including the Keck and Lick Observatories, several space-based telescopes, and various supercomputing facilities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Bioengineering
Requirements: Applicants to the Bachelor of Science in Bioengineering must apply through the University of California undergraduate application system. For freshman applicants, requirements include the completion of 15 'a-g' high school subject requirements, a minimum GPA, and the submission of four Personal Insight Questions. For transfer applicants, the requirements include the completion of at least 60 semester units of UC-transferable college credit and specific lower-division major prerequisites including Math (Calculus, Linear Algebra, Differential Equations), Chemistry (General and Organic), Physics, and Biology. Admission to the College of Engineering is highly competitive and is based on a holistic review of academic performance and personal achievements.
Concentration: Biomedical Devices, Biomedical Imaging, Cell & Tissue Engineering, Synthetic & Systems Biology, Computational Bioengineering, Pre-Med
Description: Bioengineering is a field that applies engineering principles and design concepts to biology and medicine for healthcare purposes (e.g., diagnostic or therapeutic). Bioengineering is a multidisciplinary field, and its goal is to bridge the gap between engineering and medicine, combining the design and problem-solving skills of engineering with medical biological sciences to advance health care treatment, including diagnosis, monitoring, and therapy. Bioengineers can be found working in a wide range of industries and sectors, including medical device companies, biotechnology companies, pharmaceutical companies, hospitals, and research institutions.
Accredidation: The Bioengineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Bioengineering - Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: The joint major in Bioengineering and Materials Science and Engineering requires the completion of a minimum of 120-128 units. Lower division requirements include Mathematics (1A, 1B, 53, 54), Chemistry (1A/1AL or 4A, 1B or 4B), Physics (7A, 7B, 7C), and Engineering (BioE 10, BioE 26, Engin 7, MSE 45 and 45L). Upper division requirements consist of at least 31 units of BioE and MSE coursework, along with Humanities and Social Sciences (H/SS) breadth requirements.
Description: The joint major program in Bioengineering and Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) is designed for students who are interested in exploring the interface between these two fields. Bioengineering applies engineering principles to biological systems, while MSE focuses on the design and development of new materials with specific properties. Students in this joint major will learn how to apply materials science principles to biological systems, and how to develop new materials for medical and biological applications. Students should refer to the Bioengineering and MSE departments for more information about the specific research areas and opportunities available in each field.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Bioengineering and Business Administration
Requirements: Applicants must apply through the University of California (UC) application. General requirements include the completion of A-G subject requirements in high school with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Specifically for the Management, Entrepreneurship, & Technology (M.E.T.) program, applicants must choose the Bioengineering and Business Administration track. In addition to the standard UC Personal Insight Questions, applicants are required to complete a supplemental essay specific to the M.E.T. program. UC Berkeley is test-free, meaning SAT and ACT scores are not used in the admissions process.
Description: The Management, Entrepreneurship, & Technology (M.E.T.) program is a fully integrated, two-degree program that allows students to earn two Bachelor of Science degrees in one program—combining the best of the top-ranked College of Engineering and Haas School of Business. The Bioengineering & Business Administration track gives students the opportunity to learn how to apply engineering principles and design concepts to biology and medicine for healthcare purposes. Students develop a deep understanding of the biological world and how to engineer solutions to improve human health, while also gaining a solid foundation in business principles to bring these innovations to market. Students in the M.E.T. BioE + Biz track graduate with a B.S. in Bioengineering and a B.S. in Business Administration. The curriculum is designed to be completed in four years.
Accredidation: The Bioengineering B.S. program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET (http://www.abet.org). The Haas School of Business is accredited by AACSB International.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration
Requirements: The Haas School of Business offers the Spieker Undergraduate Business Program, a four-year Bachelor of Science in Business Administration. Applicants must submit the University of California Application and satisfy both UC Berkeley's general admission requirements and Haas-specific prerequisites. Key prerequisites include Calculus, Economics, Statistics, and English Composition. Freshmen apply directly to the four-year program, while transfer students must complete all lower-division requirements before enrollment. Evaluation is based on academic performance, Personal Insight Questions, and extracurricular activities/leadership.
Description: The Haas Undergraduate Program provides students with the knowledge and skills needed to understand the modern business world, to prepare them for specialized careers in areas such as accounting, finance, marketing, and management, and for graduate study. This program is highly competitive and provides a rigorous, broad-based education in business and the liberal arts, emphasizing core competencies such as accounting, finance, marketing, business communication, and organizational behavior.
Accredidation: The Haas School of Business is accredited by AACSB International.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and Need-based

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Celtic Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California’s minimum undergraduate admission requirements. For freshmen, this includes completing 15 year-long 'a-g' college-preparatory courses with a grade of C or better, and achieving a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) in these courses. Applicants must also complete the Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free for SAT and ACT scores. For transfer students, requirements include completing 60 semester (90 quarter) units of transferable college credit with a minimum GPA of 3.0.
Description: The Celtic Studies program is designed to give students a comprehensive overview of the history, literature, and culture of the Celtic-speaking peoples from the earliest times to the present. The program offers a multidisciplinary curriculum that includes courses in the languages and literatures of the Celtic world (modern and medieval Irish, Welsh, and Breton), as well as in the history, archaeology, and folklore of the Celtic-speaking peoples.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Biology
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, students must meet the University of California admission requirements: completion of a minimum of 15 college-preparatory 'a-g' courses with a grade of C or better, and a minimum GPA of 3.00 (3.40 for non-residents). Specifically for the College of Chemistry and the Chemical Biology major, the admissions process considers the applicant's academic record, including the strength of their preparation in mathematics and science, and their responses to the Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission.
Description: The chemical biology major provides a strong foundation in chemistry and the biological sciences. It is intended for students who want to study the interface of these two disciplines. The major is designed for students who are interested in pursuing careers in medicine, pharmacy, or the pharmaceutical industry, as well as those who want to pursue graduate study in chemical biology, biochemistry, or related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, you must meet the University of California’s minimum requirements: 15 year-long college-preparatory courses ('a-g' courses) with a grade of C or better — at least 11 of them prior to your last year of high school. You must earn a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) in all 'a-g' courses. Freshman applicants to the College of Chemistry are expected to have a strong background in mathematics and science.
Concentration: Biotechnology, Chemical Processing, Energy and Environment, Materials Science and Technology, Business and Management, and Applied Physical Science
Description: The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering (CBE) offers a Bachelor of Science (BS) in Chemical Engineering. Chemical engineering is a discipline that influences numerous areas of technology. In broad terms, chemical engineers conceive and design processes to produce, transform, and transport materials — beginning with experimentation in the laboratory and followed by implementation of the technology in full-scale production. Chemical engineers are in great demand because of the large number of industries that depend on the synthesis and processing of chemicals and materials. In addition to traditional careers in the chemical, energy, and oil industries, chemical engineers are finding increasing opportunities in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, electronic device fabrication, and environmental engineering. The unique training of the chemical engineer becomes essential in these areas when processes involve the chemical or physical transformation of matter.
Accredidation: The Chemical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering - Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, freshman applicants must meet the following requirements: Completion of a minimum of 15 year-long college-preparatory (A-G) courses with a letter grade of C or better (at least 11 of them prior to the start of the senior year). Applicants must earn a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) in these courses. The application process also requires the submission of the University of California Application and responses to the Personal Insight Questions.
Description: The College of Chemistry and the College of Engineering offer a joint major in Chemical Engineering and Materials Science and Engineering.
