This program is designed for students who are interested in the design and development of materials and their chemical processing. Materials science and engineering (MSE) and chemical engineering (ChE) are closely related. Modern chemical engineering is increasingly focused on the development of materials with specific properties, such as polymers, electronic materials, and catalysts. Materials science and engineering, on the other hand, is increasingly concerned with the chemical processing of materials. The joint major program is designed for students who are interested in the synergy between these two disciplines.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering - Nuclear Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, you must complete a minimum of 15 college-preparatory ('a-g') courses with a letter grade of C or better, with at least 11 completed prior to your last year of high school. You must earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 if you're a nonresident) in these courses. Applicants must also complete the personal insight questions.
Description: The joint major program in Chemical Engineering and Nuclear Engineering is designed for students who wish to prepare for careers in the nuclear power industry, nuclear research and development, or the chemical processing of nuclear materials. This joint major is one of several joint major programs offered in the College of Chemistry in conjunction with the College of Engineering. The program provides students with a strong background in both chemical engineering and nuclear engineering.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the following minimum requirements: completion of the A-G subject requirements (15 year-long college-preparatory courses) with a grade of C or better, and a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) in all A-G courses. Applicants must also submit the University of California undergraduate application, which includes four Personal Insight Questions. For the College of Chemistry, specifically the Bachelor of Science in Chemistry, strong preparation in mathematics and sciences is expected.
Concentration: Methods in Chemical Biology, Computational Chemistry, Materials Chemistry
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Chemistry is intended for students who are primarily interested in careers as professional chemists or in graduate study in chemistry. The curriculum is designed to provide a thorough foundation in the various areas of chemistry and related disciplines, and it is characterized by a wide range of rigorous laboratory and research experiences.
Accredidation: The Chemistry B.S. degree is accredited by the American Chemical Society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chicanx Latinx Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must complete a minimum of 15 college-preparatory 'a-g' courses with a letter grade of C or better, with at least 11 finished prior to the beginning of the last year of high school. Applicants must earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 if a nonresident) in these courses with no grade lower than a C. Applicants must also complete the Personal Insight Questions as part of the application. For the Chicano Studies major specifically, there are no official prerequisites, and students may declare the major at any time as long as they are in good academic standing (2.0 GPA).
Description: The Chicanx Latinx Studies (CLS) program offers an interdisciplinary curriculum that explores the experiences of people of Mexican and Latin American descent in the United States. The program focuses on themes such as immigration, labor, education, gender, and social movements. Through a combination of core courses and electives, students gain a deep understanding of the diverse history, culture, and socio-political dynamics of Chicanx and Latinx communities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chinese Language
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must complete a minimum of 15 college-preparatory (A-G) courses with a letter grade of C or better, with at least 11 courses finished prior to the beginning of their last year of high school. A minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) is required in these courses. Additionally, applicants must complete the Personal Insight Questions as part of the UC application. The Chinese major itself is an open major; students can declare at any time after having completed at least one course in the department and being in good academic standing.
Description: The Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures (EALC) provides students with the linguistic and analytical tools to understand the traditions and modern formations of East Asia. The Chinese Language and Culture major introduces students to the study of the literature, history, religion, and culture of China, through its language, in its historical and regional contexts. Students can focus on modern or pre-modern (classical) Chinese, or a combination of both. Graduates with a major in Chinese go on to careers in research, education, law, medicine, government, media, arts and culture, and more.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering
Requirements: To be considered for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California’s minimum requirements: completion of 15 year-long A-G subject courses with a grade of C or better, and a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 for non-residents) in these courses. Specifically for the College of Engineering, applicants are evaluated based on the rigor of their high school curriculum, particularly in mathematics and sciences, and their responses to the Personal Insight Questions.
Concentration: Engineering and Project Management, Environmental Engineering, GeoSystems Engineering, Structural Engineering, Transportation Engineering, and Water Resources Engineering
Description: Civil Engineering (CE) is a professional engineering discipline that deals with the design, construction, and maintenance of the physical and naturally built environment. This includes public works such as roads, bridges, canals, dams, airports, sewerage systems, pipelines, structural components of buildings, and railways. The Civil Engineering undergraduate program at UC Berkeley starts with a focus on basic principles of mathematics and natural sciences. From these, the curriculum develops into a focus on engineering sciences and the use of the modern tools of the engineering profession. Students can then choose to specialize in one or more of the following areas: Engineering and Project Management, Environmental Engineering, GeoSystems Engineering, Structural Engineering, Transportation Engineering, and Water Resources Engineering.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science program in Civil Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classical Civilizations
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must complete a minimum of 15 year-long A-G subject courses with a grade of C or better, with at least 11 courses finished before the final year of high school. A minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) is required in these courses. Applicants must submit the UC application, which includes answering Personal Insight Questions. For the Classical Civilizations major specifically, once admitted to the College of Letters and Science, students must complete lower-division requirements including two semesters of Greek or Latin and one semester of Classics 10A or 10B to declare the major.
Description: The Department of Classics offers two majors: Classics (Greek, Latin, or both) and Classical Civilizations. The former emphasizes the study of the ancient languages and the reading of the literature in the original; the latter offers a more general study of the history, literature, archaeology, and culture of the ancient world. Classical Civilizations majors develop a comprehensive and multifaceted understanding of the civilizations of ancient Greece and Rome. They take courses in many different areas—archaeology, art history, history, and literature—and also gain an introduction to one of the ancient languages (Greek or Latin).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classical Languages
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Classical Languages at UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the general University of California admission requirements. This includes the completion of 15 year-long 'a-g' subject courses with a grade of C or better, and a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Applicants must also submit the University of California application, which includes responding to Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not use SAT or ACT scores in the admission process.
Concentration: Greek, Latin, or both (Greek and Latin)
Description: The Major in Classical Languages: This major is designed for students who wish to emphasize the study of the ancient languages and to read the great works of Greek and Roman literature in the original. Students may focus on Greek, Latin, or both (Greek and Latin). The major is also suitable for students who wish to pursue a career in the teaching of Latin in secondary schools or who plan to do graduate work in Classics or a related field (e.g., Ancient History, Medieval Studies, Philosophy, or Religion).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Cognitive Science
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Cognitive Science, students must meet the general University of California freshman or transfer admission requirements. For freshman applicants, this includes the completion of 15 'A-G' subject requirements with a grade of C or better and a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-California residents). Applicants must also submit the University of California application, including the Personal Insight Questions. Once admitted to the College of Letters and Science, students must complete specific prerequisite courses to officially declare the Cognitive Science major: COG SCI 1, a Calculus or Discrete Math course, and introductory courses in Computer Science, Linguistics, Philosophy, and Psychology. All prerequisites must be taken for a letter grade and completed with a minimum grade of C or better.
Description: Cognitive science is the cross-disciplinary study of the human mind and its processes. It examines the nature, the tasks, and the functions of cognition (in a broad sense). Cognitive scientists study intelligence and behavior, with a focus on how nervous systems represent, process, and transform information. Mental faculties of concern to cognitive scientists include language, perception, memory, attention, reasoning, and emotion; to understand these faculties, cognitive scientists borrow from fields such as linguistics, psychology, artificial intelligence, philosophy, neuroscience, and anthropology. The interdisciplinary nature of cognitive science is such that it yields a variety of areas of study at the undergraduate level.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Literature
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, you must meet University of California’s minimum admissions requirements: complete 15 year-long college-preparatory courses (A-G courses) with a letter grade of C or better. At least 11 of these must be finished before the start of your senior year. You must earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 if you're a nonresident) in these courses with no grade lower than a C. Applicants must also submit the University of California application, which includes the Personal Insight Questions.
Description: The undergraduate major in Comparative Literature is designed to provide students with a broad and rigorous training in literary analysis and to foster an understanding of the cultural and historical contexts in which literature is produced and received. The major invites students to study literature across national and linguistic boundaries and to explore the relationships between different literary traditions, as well as the connections between literature and other media, such as film, music, and the visual arts. Students work in at least two different languages and investigate the ways in which literary and other cultural traditions interact and overlap.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, freshman applicants must complete a minimum of 15 college-preparatory (A-G) courses with a grade of C or better, including History, English, Mathematics, Science, a Language other than English, and Visual and Performing Arts. Applicants must earn a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Applicants must also complete the Personal Insight Questions as part of the application. For the Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science, students must select the major on their UC Berkeley application to be considered for admission to the major. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not use SAT or ACT scores in the application process.
Description: The Computer Science major is designed to provide students with a broad background in the theory and practice of computer science. Students will learn the fundamentals of computer science, including algorithms, data structures, and software engineering, as well as more advanced topics like artificial intelligence, computer graphics, and database systems. The program also emphasizes the importance of ethics and social responsibility in computer science.
Accredidation: The Computer Science Bachelor of Arts degree is not accredited by ABET.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Conservation and Resource Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, students must meet the University of California’s minimum admissions requirements: completion of A-G subject requirements with a C- or better and a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores in the admissions process. For the Bachelor of Science in Conservation and Resource Studies, students focus on an area of interest and are required to complete lower-division requirements including Biology (e.g., BIOLOGY 1A/1AL, 1B), General Chemistry (e.g., CHEM 1A/1AL), and Mathematics/Statistics (e.g., MATH 16A, 16B, or STAT 2). Applicants must also complete the UC application including Personal Insight Questions.
Description: The Conservation and Resource Studies (CRS) major is a self-designed interdisciplinary program for students interested in environmental issues and areas of interaction among natural resources, population, energy, technology, societal institutions, and cultural values. The major's focus is on the complex problems that have arisen from the way we use and interact with the environment. Students in the CRS major design their own area of concentration (track) using courses from across the campus. These tracks have included topics such as environmental justice, global environmental politics, human health and the environment, social justice and the environment, and education and the environment. CRS students have many opportunities to explore their specific interests, through an internship and a required senior thesis project.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Dance and Performance Studies
Requirements: To be eligible to declare the major in Dance and Performance Studies, students must have completed THEATER 25 (Performance: Looking at Culture) and DANCE 10 (Introduction to Dance Technique) with a grade of C or better. Students must also have a minimum overall GPA of 2.0.
Description: The Department of Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies (TDPS) teaches performance as a mode of critical inquiry, creative expression, and public engagement. Students learn to think through the body and to act through the mind. Through a diverse range of artistic traditions and theoretical frameworks, we investigate how performance shapes culture and society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Data Science
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Data Science, freshman applicants must complete the University of California's 'a-g' subject requirements with a grade of C or better, including history, English, mathematics, laboratory science, a language other than English, and visual and performing arts. A minimum 3.0 GPA (3.4 for non-residents) is required in these courses. Applicants must also complete the Personal Insight Questions as part of the UC Application. To declare the Data Science major, students must complete the following prerequisites: Foundations of Data Science (Data C8), Calculus I and II (Math 1A and 1B), and Linear Algebra (Math 54, Math 56, or Physics 89), as well as a course in Computational Structures (CS 61A, CS 88, or Engin 7). All major prerequisite courses must be completed with a minimum grade of C-.
Concentration: Domain Emphasis
Description: The Data Science major curriculum at UC Berkeley combines computational and inferential reasoning to draw conclusions based on data about some aspect of the real world. Data science comprises curriculum in computing, statistics, and a domain emphasis. The major is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in data science and the ability to apply those skills in a variety of fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Dutch Studies
Requirements: To declare the Dutch Studies major, students must have completed at least one course in the Dutch program with a grade of C or better. General requirements for the Bachelor of Arts include University Requirements (Entry Level Writing, American History and Institutions), Berkeley Campus Requirement (American Cultures), and College of Letters & Science Requirements (Reading and Composition, Quantitative Reasoning, and Foreign Language). The major itself requires 30 units of upper-division coursework.
Description: The Dutch Studies program is unique in its focus on the Netherlands and Dutch-speaking Belgium, their history and culture, and their place in the world. It provides students with a solid foundation in the Dutch language and a broad understanding of the literature, history, art, and culture of the Low Countries. Because Dutch is a Germanic language, many of the upper division courses are offered through the Department of German. However, because of its interdisciplinary nature, the Dutch Studies program also includes courses in History, Art History, and Geography.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Earth and Planetary Science
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must complete a minimum of 15 college-preparatory 'a-g' courses with a letter grade of C or better, with at least 11 finished prior to the beginning of the last year of high school. A minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) is required in these courses. Applicants must also submit Personal Insight Questions as part of the UC application. For the Earth and Planetary Science major, students are expected to complete foundational coursework in mathematics, physics, and chemistry.
Concentration: Atmospheric Science, Environmental Earth Science, Geology, Geophysics, Marine Science, and Planetary Science
Description: The Department of Earth and Planetary Science (EPS) offers six undergraduate majors: Atmospheric Science, Environmental Earth Science, Geology, Geophysics, Marine Science, and Planetary Science. In these majors, students learn to apply the fundamental principles of mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology to study the Earth as a system of interactively physical, chemical, and biological processes. EPS majors are designed to provide a strong foundation for students to pursue careers in research, teaching, government, and the private sector.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Religion, Culture and Languages
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, students must meet the University of California admission requirements: completion of 15 year-long 'a-g' college-preparatory courses with a grade of C or better (at least 11 completed before the final year of high school) and a minimum GPA of 3.0 for California residents or 3.4 for non-residents. Applicants must submit the UC Application, including Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission decisions.
Description: The major in East Asian Religion, Culture and Languages (EARCL) is designed for students who wish to focus on the study of East Asian religion and culture. This major is more flexible than either the Chinese or Japanese major and is intended to accommodate students who wish to take a more multi-faceted approach to East Asia, and to those who wish to focus on Buddhism or some other aspect of East Asian religion and culture. The major requires at least three years of study of one East Asian language (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, or Tibetan), but allows for more courses in the student’s area of interest (literature, history, thought, religion) and more of a multi-regional focus than do the Chinese and Japanese majors.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economics
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, freshman applicants must complete 15 year-long college-preparatory (a-g) courses with a grade of C or better, with at least 11 finished before the start of the 12th grade. A minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) is required in these courses. As of Fall 2023, Economics is a high-demand major in the College of Letters and Science; freshman applicants must select Economics as their primary major on the application to be considered for a guaranteed spot in the major.
Description: Economics is the study of how people and societies choose to use their limited resources. The Economics major provides students with a broad education in the field, including courses in economic theory, econometrics, and a variety of applied topics. Students learn to analyze economic issues using quantitative methods and to think critically about the role of government and markets in society. The department offers a wide range of courses in such areas as economic history, international trade and finance, labor economics, and public policy. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in economic theory and its application to a variety of real-world problems.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Ecosystem Management and Forestry
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Ecosystem Management and Forestry, applicants must fulfill the general University of California undergraduate admission requirements. These include the completion of at least 15 college-preparatory 'a-g' courses with a grade of C or better, achieving a minimum GPA of 3.0 for California residents (3.4 for non-residents), and completing the Personal Insight Questions as part of the University of California application. UC Berkeley is currently test-free, meaning SAT and ACT scores are not considered for admission decisions.
Concentration: Forestry, Natural Resource Management
Description: The Ecosystem Management and Forestry (EMF) major provides students with the multidisciplinary knowledge, skills, and tools to manage and bridge the conservation of complex ecosystems. Forests and other natural resources provide timber, water, habitat, and recreation. As the world’s population grows, we face new challenges: global climate change, wildfire, and an increasing need for sustainable natural resources. The EMF program provides students with the tools to solve these problems by integrating knowledge of forest ecology and biology with management of wildland resources and an understanding of the social, economic, and policy aspects of resource management. Students in the EMF major will select one of two specializations: 1. Forestry or 2. Natural Resource Management. The Forestry specialization is accredited by the Society of American Foresters (SAF) and provides a pathway to a professional career in forestry. It is the only program in the San Francisco Bay Area that provides the necessary training to become a Registered Professional Forester (RPF) in California. The Natural Resource Management specialization is designed for students who want a broad education in the management of natural resources. It provides flexibility for students to focus on areas such as conservation, restoration, or environmental policy.
Accredidation: The Forestry specialization is accredited by the Society of American Foresters (SAF).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering & Computer Sciences
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, students must meet the University of California admission requirements: the Subject Requirement (completion of 15 year-long 'a-g' courses with a grade of C or better), the Scholarship Requirement (minimum GPA of 3.0 for California residents or 3.4 for non-residents), and the completion of Personal Insight Questions. For the College of Engineering, applicants are strongly encouraged to complete the following: 4 years of mathematics (including calculus), and 3 years of laboratory science (including physics and chemistry). Admission to the EECS major is highly competitive and considers both academic and non-academic factors.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences (EECS) program is designed for students who want to study both electrical engineering and computer science. The program offers a vibrant and innovative environment where students engage with world-class faculty and cutting-edge research. The EECS curriculum provides a well-rounded education in the fundamentals of electrical engineering and computer science, while also allowing students to specialize in areas of interest through technical electives. The EECS major is a rigorous program that prepares students for careers in industry or for further study in graduate school. It includes foundational coursework in mathematics, physics, and engineering, as well as advanced coursework in specialized areas of EECS.
Accredidation: The Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences (B.S.) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Energy Engineering
Requirements: Students in the Energy Engineering program must complete 120 units. All students must complete the Humanities and Social Sciences Requirement of the College of Engineering. Specific degree requirements include lower division courses in Mathematics (1A, 1B, 53, 54), Chemistry (1A, 1AL, 1B), Physics (7A, 7B, 7C), and Engineering (7, 26, 45, 45L). Upper division requirements include courses in Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and technical electives chosen in consultation with an advisor.
Description: Energy engineering is a multidisciplinary field that includes the study of energy production, conversion, storage, and consumption. The Energy Engineering program is one of several majors within the Engineering Science program in the College of Engineering. The program provides students with a strong foundation in physical sciences and engineering, with a focus on energy systems, including renewable energy, energy efficiency, and energy policy. Students learn to analyze and design complex energy systems, considering technical, economic, and environmental factors.
Accredidation: The Engineering Science program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Engineering Mathematics and Statistics
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Engineering Mathematics and Statistics, freshman applicants must meet the University of California’s minimum admission requirements: completion of 15 'a-g' college-preparatory courses with a grade of C or better, and a minimum 3.0 GPA (3.4 for non-California residents). Applicants must submit the University of California application, which includes four Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission decisions.
Description: The Engineering Mathematics and Statistics major provides students with the opportunity to study a core curriculum in mathematics and statistics along with a choice of a concentration in an engineering or science field. This interdisciplinary program provides a study in mathematics and statistics and their applications to engineering and the physical sciences. This major is intended for students who have a strong interest in mathematics and/or statistics and their application in engineering and the sciences. Students may choose from a wide variety of concentrations.
Accredidation: The Engineering Mathematics and Statistics program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Engineering Physics
Requirements: Admission to the Engineering Physics major is closed to students already on campus. Students must be admitted directly into the major at the time of application to UC Berkeley. Information on the application process can be found on the UC Berkeley Admissions website. For more information, please see the College of Engineering website.
Description:
The Engineering Physics major is interdisciplinary and offers students the opportunity to study a variety of fields, including:
The program is designed for students who have a strong interest in physics and wish to prepare for careers in research or development in the high-technology industry. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in physics and mathematics, while also offering students the chance to explore a range of engineering disciplines. Students choose an area of concentration in one of several engineering departments (bioengineering, civil and environmental engineering, electrical engineering and computer sciences, industrial engineering and operations research, materials science and engineering, mechanical engineering, or nuclear engineering). Graduates are well-prepared for graduate study in physics or engineering, as well as for careers in industry.
Accredidation: The Engineering Physics program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, you must meet University of California’s minimum admissions requirements: Complete a minimum of 15 year-long college-preparatory courses (A-G courses) with a letter grade of C or better — at least 11 of them prior to your last year of high school. Earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.00 or better (3.40 if you're a nonresident) in these courses with no grade lower than a C. Applicants must also answer 4 out of 8 Personal Insight Questions.
Description: The English major is designed to introduce students to the history of literature written in English and to the variety of methods by which such literature can be analyzed. It offers students an opportunity to study many different kinds of writing in English, from medieval poetry and early modern drama to contemporary novels and digital media. In the English major, students are invited to learn about the various traditions of poetry, drama, and prose; they are also invited to learn about the ways in which these traditions have been shaped by and have helped to shape the history of the world in which they were written. The department offers courses in all periods of English and American literature, from the earliest to the most recent, as well as courses in the history of the English language and in creative writing.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Economics and Policy
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Environmental Economics and Policy, applicants must complete the University of California application. Evaluation is based on a combination of academic achievement, personal insight questions, and extracurricular activities. Transfer applicants must complete a minimum of 60 transferable semester units, including specific major prerequisites: two semesters of Calculus (Math 1A/16A and Math 1B/16B) and one semester of Introduction to Economics (Economics 1 or 2). All students must meet the University of California's 'A-G' subject requirements for freshman admission.
Description: The Environmental Economics and Policy (EEP) major provides a foundation in microeconomic theory and its application to environmental, natural resource, and international development issues. EEP students explore how the tools of economic analysis can be used to solve some of the world’s most pressing problems, from climate change and biodiversity loss to poverty and food insecurity. The curriculum includes courses in economic theory, quantitative methods, and environmental and resource economics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering Science
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, you must meet the following: 1. Subject Requirement: Complete 15 year-long courses (the 'a-g' courses) with a grade of C or better. 2. GPA Requirement: Earn a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) in all 'a-g' courses. 3. Personal Insight Questions: Applicants must answer 4 out of 8 personal insight questions. For the College of Engineering specifically, applicants are evaluated on the strength of their math and science preparation.
Description: The Environmental Engineering Science (EES) major is an interdisciplinary program in the College of Engineering. It is intended for students who are interested in the scientific and engineering aspects of environmental problems and their solutions. The program provides a foundation in mathematics, physics, and chemistry, and it also includes coursework in the biological and geosciences. The curriculum emphasizes the application of engineering principles to the study of the environment and is designed to provide students with a broad and flexible background. It also prepares students for graduate study in environmental engineering and related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Sciences
Requirements: Applicants must complete the University of California application, which includes providing academic history and answering Personal Insight Questions. For the Environmental Sciences major within the Rausser College of Natural Resources, recommended lower-division preparation includes coursework in General Chemistry, Biology, Physics, and Calculus. UC Berkeley is test-free, meaning SAT and ACT scores are not considered for admission decisions.
Concentration: Biological Science, Physical Science, and Social Science
Description: The Environmental Sciences (ES) major is designed to provide students with the necessary biological, physical, and social science backgrounds to analyze and solve environmental problems. The ES major is highly interdisciplinary, reflecting the nature of the environmental problems that it addresses. The curriculum provides students with a broad and rigorous foundation in the natural sciences (biology, chemistry, physics, and calculus) while also introducing students to the social sciences (economics, policy, and human behavior). Each student chooses one of three concentrations: Biological Science, Physical Science, or Social Science. Students also complete a senior research project (the ES Senior Seminar), which involves a year-long independent research project on an environmental problem of their choosing.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Ethnic Studies
Requirements: To declare a major in Ethnic Studies, students must have completed ETH STD 10A and ETH STD 10B with a grade of C or better. Prospective students must also meet the general University of California admission requirements, which include the completion of 15 year-long college-preparatory (a-g) courses with a letter grade of C or better and a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) in these courses.
Description: The Ethnic Studies major provides a core curriculum designed to develop a comparative and multidisciplinary understanding of the experiences and communities of people of color in the United States and abroad. Students may also take more specialized courses on the history, culture, politics, and sociology of particular groups (e.g., African Americans, Asian Americans, Chicanx/Latinxs, and Native Americans).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film and Media
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Film & Media at UC Berkeley, applicants must complete the University of California Undergraduate Application. Freshman applicants must meet the 'a-g' subject requirements (15 year-long courses with a grade of C or better) and maintain a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). All applicants must respond to Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores in the admissions process. For the Film & Media major specifically, students are typically admitted to the College of Letters and Science as 'undeclared' and must complete prerequisite courses FILM 10 and FILM 20 with a grade of C or better to officially declare the major.
Description: The Department of Film & Media offers an undergraduate major leading to the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree. The program provides students with a deep understanding of the history, theory, and aesthetics of moving-image media. The curriculum explores the development of cinema from its beginnings to the present day, covering a wide range of national cinemas and genres. Students develop critical tools to analyze film as an art form and a social practice, while also exploring the theoretical and cultural implications of various media forms. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, research, and writing, and provides students with the analytical tools necessary to understand the role of media in modern society. The program prepares students for a variety of careers in film and media-related fields, as well as for graduate study in the humanities and social sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in French
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must: Complete a minimum of 15 college-preparatory (A-G) courses with a letter grade of C or better, with at least 11 finished prior to the start of the 12th grade. Earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 for non-residents) in these courses. Additionally, applicants must submit the University of California application, which includes responding to four Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free, meaning SAT or ACT test scores are not used in the application process.
Concentration: Plan A (Literature and Culture), Plan B (French and a Related Field)
Description: The Department of French at Berkeley is one of the top-ranked in the country, and its distinguished faculty offers a wide range of courses in French and Francophone literature and culture, from the Middle Ages to the present day. Language instruction at all levels is provided by a talented group of professional lecturers. The department's undergraduate program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the French language and in the literatures and cultures of the French-speaking world. In addition to gaining proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing, students develop skills in literary and cultural analysis, critical thinking, and research. The major also prepares students for graduate study in French or related fields, as well as for careers in education, international business, law, diplomacy, and more.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Gender and Women's Studies
Requirements: Applicants must complete secondary school with a minimum GPA of 3.4 in the required 'a-g' academic subjects. Required application components include secondary school records, English language proficiency exam scores for international students (TOEFL iBT 80 or higher, IELTS 6.5 or higher, or Duolingo English Test 115 or higher), and the completion of 4 out of 8 personal insight questions. UC Berkeley is test-free, meaning SAT and ACT scores are not required or considered for admissions decisions.
Description: Gender and Women's Studies (GWS) is an interdisciplinary field that investigates how gender and sexuality are shaped by and within social, cultural, historical, political, and economic contexts. The GWS curriculum at UC Berkeley offers students the opportunity to study gender and sexuality through a wide range of disciplines, including history, sociology, anthropology, literature, art, film, and media studies. In GWS courses, students learn to analyze power and inequality, and to understand how categories of difference—such as race, class, ability, and nation—interact with gender and sexuality. Students also develop critical thinking, research, and writing skills that are valuable in a wide range of careers.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Genetics and Plant Biology
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, you must meet the following: Complete a minimum of 15 college-preparatory (A-G) courses with a grade of C or better. 11 of these courses must be finished prior to your last year of high school. Earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 for non-residents) in these courses. Applicants must also provide responses to the Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free, which means we will not use SAT/ACT test scores in our review process.
Concentration: Biotechnology and Bioenergy; Plant Genetics, Breeding, and Genomics; Plant Biology
Description: The Genetics and Plant Biology (GPB) major, offered by the Department of Plant and Microbial Biology, provides an undergraduate program that examines the fundamental aspects of how plants function. Students in the GPB major study the molecular and cellular biology of plants, as well as their interactions with other organisms and the environment. The program provides a broad foundation in the biological sciences, with an emphasis on plant biology and genetics. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for careers in research, education, and biotechnology, as well as for further study in graduate or professional schools.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Geography
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must complete the University of California (UC) application, fulfill the A-G subject requirements with a grade of C or better, and achieve a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) in all A-G courses. Applicants must also complete the Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission. For the Geography major specifically, students may declare the major after completing at least one geography course at Berkeley with a grade of C or better.
Concentration: Earth System Science, Economy, Culture and Society, Global Environmental Change, Urban Studies and Development
Description: Geography is a diverse and active community of scholars engaged in research and teaching about the surface of the earth and the people who live on it. Geographers study the distribution of physical and social phenomena, the ways people interact with and modify their environment, and the nature of places and regions. The undergraduate major is designed to provide students with a broad knowledge of the field and its core themes: earth’s physical environment, human-environment relations, and the spatial and social logic of human society. At the same time, the major is flexible enough to allow students to focus their studies in areas of particular interest, such as global environmental change, earth system science, urban studies, or economy, culture, and society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Geology
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, students must meet the University of California's general admission requirements. For freshmen, this includes completing 15 'a-g' subject courses (including history, English, mathematics, science, and a foreign language) with a grade of C or better, and achieving a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Applicants must also complete the Personal Insight Questions. For the Geology major specifically, students should complete lower-division prerequisites including: EPS 50 (The Planet Earth), Mathematics 1A and 1B (Calculus), Chemistry 1A and 1AL (General Chemistry), and Physics 7A (Physics for Scientists and Engineers).
Description: The geology major is designed for students with a primary interest in the history and evolution of the Earth, including the causes of the current shape and structure of the Earth’s surface, the materials that make up the Earth, and the processes that control its long-term development. Geology is an interdisciplinary science that uses principles of physics, chemistry, and biology to explore the Earth system. Undergraduate research is highly encouraged. Graduates of this program may go into the private sector, work for government agencies, or pursue graduate school.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in German
Requirements: To declare a major in German, students must have a grade-point average (GPA) of at least 2.0 (C) for all work undertaken at the University of California. In addition, students must have completed all lower division requirements for the major with a GPA of 2.0 or better. For students who have taken their lower division German language courses at Berkeley, the department requires a grade of at least C- in German 4 or its equivalent. Students who have completed German 4 with a grade of P (Pass) are also eligible to declare.
Concentration: Plan 1: German Literature and Culture, Plan 2: Interdisciplinary
Description: The German Department at the University of California, Berkeley, is one of the oldest and most prominent German departments in the United States. Its graduate program is consistently ranked among the top programs in the country. At the undergraduate level, the department offers a major and a minor in German. Students may focus their studies on various aspects of German language, literature, and culture, or pursue a more interdisciplinary track. The department also offers several courses in English that are popular with students from across the university. With its distinguished faculty and diverse course offerings, the UC Berkeley German Department provides students with a rich and stimulating environment for the study of German-speaking cultures.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Global Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Global Studies at UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California’s minimum admission requirements, which include the Subject Requirement (completion of 15 A-G year-long high school courses) and the Scholarship Requirement (minimum 3.0 GPA for California residents or 3.4 for non-residents). UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores. To declare the Global Studies major, students must complete Global 10A and Global 10B with a grade of C or better and satisfy the foreign language requirement through the second semester (intermediate) level.
Concentration: Global Development, Global Health and Environment, and Global Peace and Conflict
Description: The Global Studies program provides students with the tools to understand the complex issues that define our world. Students choose a specific geographic region or a global theme to focus their studies. The major offers three tracks: Global Development, Global Health and Environment, and Global Peace and Conflict. Regional specializations include Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, Middle East, and Russia/Eastern Europe/Central Asia. This interdisciplinary program allows students to study how the globalization of markets, cultures, and politics affects the lives of people in different parts of the world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in History at UC Berkeley, applicants must complete the University of California (UC) application. General requirements include the completion of A-G subject requirements with a minimum GPA, and the submission of Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free, meaning SAT and ACT scores are not considered for admission. For the History major specifically, students typically enter the College of Letters and Science as undeclared and must complete lower-division prerequisites—including a two-course sequence in United States history and other history breadth requirements—with a minimum GPA of 2.0 to declare the major.
Description: The History Department at Berkeley is one of the top-ranked programs in the world. It provides its students with a strong foundation in the history of several different parts of the world and in several different periods. Students learn how to read and think critically, how to evaluate evidence, and how to write clearly and persuasively. The major is designed to be flexible, allowing students to pursue their own interests within the field.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History of Art
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California admission requirements: completion of a minimum of 15 college-preparatory ('a-g') courses with a letter grade of C or better, and a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) in these courses. Applicants must also submit the University of California application, including the Personal Insight Questions. The History of Art major is located within the College of Letters and Science; students typically declare the major after completing at least one History of Art course at Berkeley with a grade of C or better.
Description: The Department of History of Art at Berkeley provides an excellent program for the student who wants a strong liberal arts education and a thorough knowledge of the history of art. Training in the department leads to an understanding of the relationship between art and the cultures that produced it. It also develops the student’s ability to think, to look, and to write in a clear and critical way.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research, applicants must meet the University of California’s basic admission requirements. This includes the completion of 15 college-preparatory 'a-g' courses with a grade of C or better, including 11 courses finished prior to the senior year. A minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) is required. Applicants must also complete the Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission. For the College of Engineering, it is highly recommended that students complete the most rigorous math and science courses available, such as calculus, physics, and chemistry.
Description: Industrial Engineering and Operations Research (IEOR) is the discipline of finding and applying the most efficient and effective way to design, organize, and operate complex systems. These systems can be found in a variety of industries, including manufacturing, healthcare, finance, transportation, and energy. IEOR professionals use mathematical modeling, data analysis, and optimization techniques to improve the performance of these systems and solve complex problems. The Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the core principles of IEOR, including probability and statistics, optimization, and system design. Students also have the opportunity to take a variety of elective courses in areas such as financial engineering, supply chain management, and health care systems.
Accredidation: The Industrial Engineering and Operations Research (B.S.) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Industrial and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Integrative Biology
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, freshman applicants must complete a minimum of 15 year-long A-G courses with a grade of C or better, with at least 11 finished prior to the beginning of the last year of high school. A minimum 3.0 GPA (3.4 for non-residents) is required. For the Bachelor of Arts in Integrative Biology, students are typically admitted to the College of Letters and Science as undeclared. To declare the major, students must complete the following lower-division prerequisites with a grade of C or better: Biology 1A and 1AL, Biology 1B, Chemistry 1A and 1AL, and Chemistry 3A and 3AL. Additionally, students must have a minimum 2.0 GPA in all courses for the major.
Concentration: Plan A: Ecological, Evolutionary, and Organismal Biology; Plan B: Human Biology, Health, and Society
Description: The Department of Integrative Biology (IB) offers an undergraduate major leading to the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree. The IB major is designed to provide students with a broad and fundamental education in biology, while also allowing for specialization in areas of particular interest. The department's focus is on the integration of biological knowledge across all levels of organization, from molecules to ecosystems, with an emphasis on the evolution and function of organisms in their natural environments.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies
Requirements: To be eligible to declare the Interdisciplinary Studies Field (ISF) major, a student must have a minimum 2.0 UC GPA and have completed either ISF 100A or ISF 100B with a grade of C or better. Additionally, students must have at least two semesters remaining at UC Berkeley and must submit a well-developed research proposal to an ISF Faculty Adviser for approval as part of the application process.
Description: The Interdisciplinary Studies Field Major (ISF) is a research-oriented program that allows students to develop an individualized major program of study around a research problem of their own design. The major is designed for students who have a specific research interest that cannot be pursued within a single department. ISF students work with a faculty advisor to create a program that includes courses from at least three different departments. The program culminates in a senior thesis. In the thesis, students are expected to engage in a rigorous and systematic study of their research problem and to demonstrate their mastery of the multidisciplinary approach they have developed.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Italian Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California’s undergraduate admission requirements, which include the Subject Requirement (completion of 15 year-long 'a-g' courses with a grade of C or better) and the Scholarship Requirement (minimum 3.0 GPA for California residents or 3.4 for non-residents). For the Bachelor of Arts in Italian Studies, students typically enter the College of Letters and Science as undeclared and must complete the lower-division prerequisites, which include Italian 1, 2, 3, and 4 (or their equivalents), before declaring the major.
Description: The Department of Italian Studies at Berkeley is widely recognized as one of the best in the country. It is dedicated to the study of the literature, culture, and history of Italy, from the Middle Ages to the present. The undergraduate program in Italian Studies provides students with a solid foundation in the Italian language and a broad understanding of Italian literature and culture. It is a multidisciplinary major that combines language study with courses in literature, film, history, and the arts, allowing students to explore the richness and diversity of Italian contributions to world culture.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Japanese Language
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California's minimum requirements. Freshman applicants must complete the 15 year-long 'a-g' subject requirements with a grade of C or better and maintain a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Transfer applicants must complete 60 semester (90 quarter) units of UC-transferable college credit with a minimum GPA of 2.4 (2.8 for non-residents). For the Bachelor of Arts in Japanese, lower-division major requirements include JAPAN 1, JAPAN 10, JAPAN 20, and JAPAN 7A or 7B.
Description: The major program in Japanese is intended to provide a solid foundation in Japanese language and to introduce students to the breadth of Japanese culture and its contribution to the human experience. While students may focus on either classical or modern Japanese literature, they will also have the opportunity to study a range of other topics in the humanities, including linguistics, film and media, thought and religion, and history.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Korean Language
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California admission requirements: completion of 15 year-long 'a-g' subject area courses with a grade of C or better (11 must be completed prior to the start of the 12th grade year), a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) in 'a-g' courses, and completion of the UC application including the Personal Insight Questions. For the Bachelor of Arts in Korean, students typically apply to the College of Letters and Science as 'undeclared' and must satisfy lower-division prerequisites (KOREAN 1A-1B and 10A-10B) before declaring the major.
Concentration: Korean
Description: The Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures (EALC) at UC Berkeley is one of the premier centers for the study of China, Japan, and Korea in the world. Its renowned faculty and excellent students engage in the study of East Asian civilizations from the beginning of writing to the present day, across multiple disciplines. The department offers an undergraduate major with three tracks—Chinese, Japanese, and Korean—and a minor. The undergraduate program in the Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the languages, literatures, and cultures of East Asia. The major program requires language study and a distribution of courses in the history, literature, and culture of the region.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Landscape Architecture
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general University of California undergraduate admission requirements. Freshman applicants are required to complete the 'a-g' subject requirements with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-California residents). Transfer applicants must complete at least 60 transferable semester (90 quarter) units, including lower-division major requirements such as environmental design courses. Admission is based on the University of California application, which includes Personal Insight Questions. The College of Environmental Design (CED) does not require a portfolio, resume, or supplemental application for undergraduate admission.
Description: Landscape architecture is the design, planning and management of the land. Its objectives are to create and preserve beauty, to maintain a healthy environment, and to promote social well-being. The undergraduate curriculum in landscape architecture centers on creative and ecologically based design, and the inventory, analysis, and design of the land. It provides students with a sound general education in the arts and sciences as well as a specific orientation to the concepts and skills of landscape architecture. Through the Bachelor of Arts in Landscape Architecture, the College of Environmental Design (CED) seeks to foster an understanding of the relationship between the built and natural environments; provide students with the skills to design and manage sustainable landscapes; focus on design and planning at the site, neighborhood, and regional scales; and emphasize the importance of community engagement and social justice in landscape architecture and environmental planning. This program is a four-year non-professional degree that provides a pre-professional education, but does not qualify a student for professional licensure.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Landscape Architecture is a non-professional degree. It is not accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Latin American Studies
Requirements: To declare the Latin American Studies major, students must have: Completed at least one semester at UC Berkeley; A minimum 2.0 cumulative GPA; Completed the language requirement (completion of SPANISH 4 or PORTUG 4 or the equivalent proficiency); and completed one semester of Latin American History (HISTORY 8A or 8B or a pre-approved substitute). To declare, students must submit the Major Application and an Area of Concentration form to the Latin American Studies advisor.
Description: The Latin American Studies (LAS) major provides students with a broad knowledge of Latin American history, culture, and society, as well as a specialized knowledge of a particular region or topic within Latin America. Students develop linguistic proficiency in Spanish or Portuguese and are encouraged to spend time studying or conducting research in Latin America. The LAS major is an interdisciplinary program, and its requirements include courses in several different departments.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and Need-based

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Legal Studies
Requirements: To declare the Bachelor of Arts in Legal Studies, students must first be admitted to UC Berkeley. Major declaration requirements include: 1. Completion of LEGALST 10 (Introduction to Legal Studies) with a grade of C or better. 2. Completion of one additional Legal Studies 'Area' course (LEGALST 100 through LEGALST 149) with a grade of C or better. 3. A cumulative UC Berkeley GPA of 2.0 or higher. For general undergraduate admission, UC Berkeley is test-free and evaluates applicants based on high school coursework (A-G requirements), GPA, and Personal Insight Questions.
Description: Legal Studies is an interdisciplinary major in the College of Letters and Science that focuses on the study of law and justice. The program is designed to provide students with an understanding of the nature of law, the ways in which law is created and applied, and the relationship between law and society. The major is not a pre-law program in the professional sense, but rather a liberal arts program that emphasizes critical thinking, research, and writing skills. The Legal Studies major is based on the assumption that law is a fundamental social institution and that its study is essential to a liberal education. The curriculum is designed to introduce students to the various ways in which law can be studied, including historical, philosophical, sociological, and economic perspectives. Students are encouraged to develop their own interests within the major and to choose courses that reflect those interests.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California’s minimum undergraduate admission requirements: completion of 15 year-long college-preparatory courses (A-G requirements) with a letter grade of C or better, and a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) in these courses. Additionally, applicants must submit the University of California application, which includes responding to four out of eight Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not use SAT or ACT scores in its review process.
Description: Linguistics is the study of language as a human faculty. Its goals are to understand the structure of human languages, how they are learned, how they are used, how they change over time, and how they are represented in the brain. The undergraduate major in linguistics provides students with a solid foundation in the core areas of the field—phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics—and introduces them to the diversity of the world's languages and the methods used to study them.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the following: 1. Complete a minimum of 15 college-preparatory (A-G) courses with a grade of C or better, including History/social science, English, Mathematics, Laboratory science, Language other than English, Visual and performing arts, and College-preparatory electives. 2. Earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 if you're a nonresident) in these courses. 3. Complete the UC application including the Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free, meaning SAT or ACT scores are not used in the application process.
Description: The Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) department offers a comprehensive program of education and research. The undergraduate curriculum provides a strong foundation in the physical and chemical sciences, as well as the engineering principles required to design and develop new materials for a wide range of applications. Students learn about the various classes of materials, including metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites, and explore the cutting-edge fields of nanotechnology, biomaterials, and energy materials. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on laboratory experiences and provides opportunities for research and internships. Graduates of our program are well-prepared for careers in industry, government, and academia, and are poised to become leaders in the field of materials science and engineering.
Accredidation: The Materials Science and Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Materials, Metallurgical, Ceramics and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the University of California, Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California's minimum undergraduate admission requirements: completion of 15 year-long college-preparatory (A-G) courses with a grade of C or better, a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) in A-G courses, and completion of the Personal Insight Questions. For the Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics specifically, students typically enter the College of Letters and Science as undeclared and must complete lower-division prerequisites (Math 1A, 1B, 53, 54 or 56, and 55) with a minimum GPA to officially declare the major.
Description: The Department of Mathematics offers two majors: Mathematics and Applied Mathematics. The Mathematics major is intended for students who are interested in the theory of mathematics. It is suitable for those who wish to pursue a career in teaching, in government or industry, or who wish to pursue graduate study in mathematics or a related field. Mathematics is a highly developed and yet still very active subject. It has many applications in the sciences, and in many other areas as well. The undergraduate program in mathematics provides a solid foundation in the core areas of the subject and allows students to explore various advanced topics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering at UC Berkeley, freshman applicants must meet the University of California's 'a-g' subject requirements, which include 15 year-long high school courses with a grade of C or better. Applicants must have a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). For the College of Engineering, it is strongly recommended that applicants complete four years of mathematics, including calculus, and three years of laboratory science (including physics and chemistry). Admission is based on a holistic review of academic performance, extracurricular activities, and responses to four Personal Insight Questions.
Concentration: Aerospace Engineering, Biomechanical Engineering, Control, Design, Energy and Environment, Manufacturing, Materials Processing, Mechanics, Mechatronics, Micro and Nanoscale Engineering, Nuclear Engineering
Description: Mechanical Engineering is the most diverse of the engineering professions, as its application ranges from the design of small parts to large-scale systems. Mechanical engineers apply their knowledge of mathematics and the sciences to solve technical problems, while also considering the effects of their work on the environment and society. Students in the Mechanical Engineering (ME) program begin with a foundation of engineering sciences (mainly physics and mathematics) and then move on to study the ME core: design, manufacturing, controls, and thermo-fluids. Students can also choose technical electives in several different areas to tailor their education to their specific interests.
Accredidation: The Mechanical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Media Studies
Requirements: To apply to the Media Studies major, students must first be admitted to UC Berkeley. Media Studies is a high-demand major. Freshman applicants must select Media Studies as their primary major on their UC application to be guaranteed a spot in the major if admitted to Berkeley. Transfer students must complete four prerequisite courses with a letter grade: Media Studies 10 and three introductory courses from three different social science departments (Anthropology, Economics, History, Political Science, Psychology, or Sociology). A minimum GPA of 2.0 in the prerequisite courses is required for declaration.
Description: The Media Studies Major is an interdisciplinary program in the College of Letters and Science. It is designed to provide students with a foundational understanding of the role of media in society. The program provides a broad liberal arts education, focusing on the history, values, and structure of media systems and their impact on culture, politics, and the individual. Media Studies students learn to think critically about the media and to communicate effectively in a variety of forms.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Microbial Biology
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Microbial Biology, students must meet general University of California undergraduate admission requirements, which include completing 15 college-preparatory (A-G) courses with a letter grade of C or better and achieving a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Specific lower-division major requirements include Biology 1A, 1AL, and 1B; Chemistry 1A, 1AL, 3A, 3AL, 3B, and 3BL; Mathematics 10A and 10B (or 1A and 1B); and Physics 8A and 8B (or 7A and 7B). Transfer students must complete these lower-division requirements with a letter grade of C- or higher to be competitive for admission.
Concentration: Microbial Ecology and Evolution, Host-Pathogen Interactions, and Microbial Biotechnology
Description: Microbes—bacteria, fungi, and viruses—are the most abundant and diverse life forms on Earth. They are essential to every ecosystem on the planet and play an integral role in human health and disease. Microbial biology is a major for students interested in studying the fundamental processes of microbial life and their applications in biotechnology, medicine, and environmental science. The program provides a strong foundation in chemistry, biology, physics, and math, while offering specialized coursework in microbiology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Middle Eastern Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, freshman applicants must complete 15 year-long college-preparatory (a-g) courses with a grade of C or better, including 2 years of history, 4 years of English, 3 years of mathematics, 2 years of science, 2 years of a language other than English, 1 year of visual and performing arts, and 1 year of a college-preparatory elective. A minimum non-weighted GPA of 3.0 for California residents (3.4 for non-residents) is required. Applicants must also complete the Personal Insight Questions. To declare the major in Middle Eastern Studies, students must complete lower-division prerequisites, including MELC 10 (Introduction to the Middle East) and two semesters of a Middle Eastern language (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, or Turkish), with a minimum GPA of 2.0. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores in the admissions process.
Description: The undergraduate major in Middle Eastern Studies (MES) is a multidisciplinary program designed to provide students with a multifaceted understanding of the history, politics, cultures, and languages of the Middle East. The major is intended to provide students with a comprehensive and multidisciplinary understanding of the Middle East as a region and the diverse cultures that inhabit it. The program includes study of a Middle Eastern language (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, or Turkish) and coursework in history, social sciences, and humanities. Students are encouraged to develop a specific interest within the major, such as a focus on a particular period, country, or theme (e.g., gender, religion, or conflict).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Molecular and Cell Biology
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, you must meet the following: Complete a minimum of 15 college-preparatory (A-G) courses with a letter grade of C or better. At least 11 of these courses must be completed prior to your last year of high school. Earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.00 or better (3.40 if you're a nonresident) in these courses with no grade lower than a C. UC Berkeley is test-free, which means we will not use SAT/ACT test scores in our review process. Applicants must also submit answers to the Personal Insight Questions.
Concentration: Biochemistry, Molecular, and Structural Biology; Cell and Developmental Biology; Genetics, Genomics, and Development; Immunology and Pathogenesis; Neurobiology
Description: The Molecular and Cell Biology (MCB) major focuses on the study of the fundamental structures and processes of life at the molecular, cellular, and organismal levels. It is one of the largest undergraduate majors at UC Berkeley. The department is organized into five divisions: Biochemistry, Biophysics and Structural Biology; Cell Biology, Development and Physiology; Genetics, Genomics, and Development; Immunology and Molecular Medicine; and Neurobiology. The MCB major provides a strong foundation in modern biology and prepares students for a wide range of careers in research, medicine, biotechnology, and beyond.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Molecular Environmental Biology
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Molecular Environmental Biology, applicants must meet the general University of California undergraduate admission requirements. Freshman applicants must complete the 15 required 'A-G' subject courses with a grade of C or better, including history, English, mathematics, science, and a foreign language, and have a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Transfer applicants must complete 60 semester (90 quarter) units of transferable college credit with a minimum GPA of 3.0. Specific major prerequisites for MEB include General Biology, General Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, and Calculus.
Concentration: Animal Health and Behavior, Biodiversity, Ecology, and Environmental and Human Health
Description: Molecular Environmental Biology (MEB) focuses on the organization and function of biological organisms and their relationship to each other and their environment. This major focuses on how organisms adapt to different environments and explores the environmental and human health impacts of biology. MEB is particularly suitable for students who wish to emphasize the biological and health aspects of environmental science. The program provides students with a broad foundation in the biological sciences, with a focus on the study of organisms, their molecular and cellular biology, and their relationship to the environment.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, you must meet the University of California’s undergraduate admission requirements. These include the completion of 15 year-long 'a-g' subject pattern courses with a grade of C or better, a minimum GPA of 3.0 for California residents (3.4 for non-residents), and completion of the UC Application which includes Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not use SAT or ACT scores in the admissions process. For the Bachelor of Arts in Music, prospective students apply to the College of Letters and Science; there is no audition or supplemental application required for admission to the major as a freshman.
Description: The Department of Music offers a program of study leading to the degree of Bachelor of Arts. The major provides a base for many different careers and is particularly appropriate for students who wish to emphasize music in a liberal arts education. It also serves as preparation for graduate study in music history and literature, theory, composition, performance, or ethnomusicology. The Department of Music is an active participant in the campus’s rich cultural life. Its concerts, lectures, and other events are widely known for their number and quality. The department presents approximately 100 concerts each year and sponsors numerous seminars, workshops, and colloquia.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Native American Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California’s subject and scholarship requirements: 1. Complete a minimum of 15 college-preparatory 'a-g' courses with a letter grade of C or better. 2. Earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 if you're a nonresident) in these courses. 3. Submit responses to the Personal Insight Questions. To declare a major in Native American Studies, students must have completed at least one Native American Studies course with a grade of C or better and have at least a 2.0 overall GPA at UC Berkeley.
Description: Native American Studies (NAS) is an interdisciplinary program that offers a major and a minor. The NAS program provides an opportunity for students to study the history, culture, politics, and contemporary situation of the Indigenous peoples of the Americas. The curriculum is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of the unique political, legal, and social status of Native American nations and communities. The program focuses on themes of sovereignty, self-determination, and decolonization, drawing on disciplines such as history, law, literature, sociology, and environmental studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Near Eastern Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, students must meet the following requirements: 1.
