Subject Requirement: Complete 15 year-long 'a-g' college-preparatory courses with a grade of C or better. 2. GPA Requirement: Earn a minimum GPA of 3.0 in all 'a-g' courses (3.4 for non-California residents). 3. Personal Insight Questions: Applicants must respond to four of the eight Personal Insight Questions as part of the application process.
Concentration: Ancient Near Eastern Civilizations; Middle Eastern Civilizations; Near Eastern Art and Archaeology
Description: The Department of Middle Eastern Languages and Cultures offers a major and a minor in Middle Eastern Languages and Cultures (formerly Near Eastern Studies). The major provides a comprehensive study of the languages, literatures, and civilizations of the Near/Middle East from antiquity to the present. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the history, culture, and languages of the region, while also allowing for specialization in a particular area of interest.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nuclear Engineering
Requirements: Applicants must meet the University of California admission requirements, which include high school graduation, the completion of 15 year-long academic courses (A-G subject requirements) with a grade of C or better, and a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). For the College of Engineering, it is strongly recommended that students complete four years of mathematics (including calculus), and sciences including physics and chemistry. All applicants must complete the UC Application and answer the Personal Insight Questions.
Description: The Department of Nuclear Engineering offers a program of undergraduate study leading to the Bachelor of Science degree in Nuclear Engineering. The program is designed to provide a solid foundation in the fundamental principles of nuclear science and engineering. This foundation includes nuclear physics, reactor physics, thermal hydraulics, radiation detection and measurement, and nuclear materials. Students also gain experience in the design and operation of nuclear systems through laboratory courses and a senior design project. The curriculum is intended to prepare students for careers in the nuclear industry, national laboratories, or government agencies, and for graduate study in nuclear engineering or related fields.
Accredidation: The Nuclear Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutritional Sciences
Requirements: All applicants to Berkeley must apply through the University's central undergraduate admissions office. Admission to Berkeley is a two-step process: First, applicants must meet the University of California's basic admission requirements. Second, these applicants are then evaluated through Berkeley's holistic review process. Students can apply to the Nutritional Sciences - Physiology & Metabolism major when they apply to UC Berkeley, or they can apply to the Rausser College of Natural Resources as an undeclared student and declare the major later.
Concentration: Physiology & Metabolism
Description: Nutritional Sciences (NS) is an undergraduate major offered by the Department of Nutritional Sciences and Toxicology (NST). This major provides a strong foundation in the biological and chemical sciences. In the Physiology & Metabolism (PM) track, students learn about the biology and chemistry of how our bodies utilize nutrients from the food we eat. The PM track covers topics ranging from the molecular and cellular level to the organ system level. This track is ideal for students who are interested in pursuing careers in medicine, research, or other health-related fields. In order to graduate, students must complete at least 120 units, including the university's requirements, the college's requirements, and the major's requirements.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Peace and Conflict Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, students must meet the University of California’s basic admission requirements. This includes the Subject Requirement (completing 15 year-long college-preparatory 'A-G' courses with a grade of C or better), the GPA Requirement (minimum 3.0 GPA for California residents or 3.4 for non-residents), and the completion of the UC Application including the Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is a test-free campus and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission decisions.
Concentration: Global Peace and Conflict
Description: Global Peace and Conflict provides students with the tools to understand the origins and nature of conflict, as well as the conditions for peace. This track is inherently interdisciplinary, drawing on scholarship from across the social sciences and humanities. Students explore topics such as the causes of war, the role of international law and organizations, the dynamics of social movements, and the challenges of peacebuilding in the aftermath of conflict. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical frameworks and practical case studies, encouraging students to think critically about how individuals, communities, and nations can work toward a more just and peaceful world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy, applicants must complete the University of California application, which includes the Personal Insight Questions. General admission requirements include completion of the A-G subject requirements (15 year-long courses) with a minimum GPA of 3.0 for California residents or 3.4 for non-residents. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission. Once enrolled in the College of Letters and Science, students must complete at least two lower-division philosophy courses at UC Berkeley with a grade of C or higher in each to declare the Philosophy major.
Description: The department offers an undergraduate major in philosophy leading to the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad background in the history of philosophy and a basic understanding of the major subfields of philosophy. The department's faculty members represent a wide range of interests and approaches to the subject. The undergraduate major is intended to provide a solid foundation for further study in philosophy, as well as a good general education for students who plan to enter other fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Physics
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Physics at UC Berkeley, applicants must submit the University of California (UC) application. Freshman requirements include the completion of 15 year-long 'a-g' college-preparatory courses with a grade of C or better, with at least 11 of these completed before the senior year. A minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) is required in these courses. Applicants must also complete the Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores in the admissions process. For students already enrolled at Berkeley, declaring the major requires completion of lower-division prerequisites (Physics 7A, 7B, 7C or 5A, 5B, 5C; and Math 1A, 1B, 53, 54) with a minimum 2.0 GPA.
Description: The Physics major is designed to give students a solid foundation in the concepts and principles of physics. It is intended to prepare students for graduate study in physics or a related field, or for a career in industry or government.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Economy
Requirements: To declare the major in Political Economy, students must have: Completed GLOBAL 45 with a grade of C or better; Completed or be currently enrolled in ECON 1 or 2; Have a cumulative UC GPA of 2.0 or higher. For students currently taking Global 45 and/or Econ, the department will process the declaration petition after the current semester's grades are posted and it is verified that all requirements are met. Students must also complete lower division requirements including: a principles of economics course (ECON 1 or 2), a calculus course, a statistics course, and a foreign language requirement (completion of the fourth semester of a language other than English).
Concentration: Geographic or thematic area (e.g., Development and Globalization; International Trade and Finance; Science, Technology, and the Environment; or a specific region)
Description: Political Economy is an interdisciplinary program that studies the intersection of politics and economics. It provides students with a sophisticated understanding of how the state and the economy interact and shape each other. The curriculum focuses on three main areas: the role of the state in the economy, the impact of economic processes on political systems, and the historical development of economic and political institutions. Students in the major explore the relationship between the individual, the state, and the market, and the ways in which these entities interact to create public policy and economic outcomes. The major is designed to provide students with a broad-based education in the social sciences, while also allowing them to focus on a particular area of interest through their concentration.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, freshman applicants must complete a minimum of 15 year-long college-preparatory (A-G) courses with a grade of C or better, including history, English, mathematics, science, a language other than English, and visual and performing arts. A minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) is required. To declare the Bachelor of Arts in Political Science, students must complete five lower-division requirements (Political Science 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5) and maintain at least a 2.0 GPA in all courses taken for the major.
Description: Political science is the study of politics, government, and public policy, both in the US and around the world. Political scientists seek to both describe and explain political phenomena. This includes study of the processes by which government decisions are made, the role of citizen engagement, the nature of political institutions, the causes of international conflict and cooperation, and the comparative performance of different government systems. Political Science is one of the largest majors on the UC Berkeley campus. Our faculty members’ research and teaching cover all of the major subfields of political science: American politics, comparative politics, international relations, political theory, models and politics, and formal theory and quantitative methods.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology
Requirements: The Psychology major requires the completion of 8 prerequisite courses and 8 upper division courses. To declare the major, students must have completed all 8 prerequisite courses: one (1) general psychology course, one (1) statistical methods course, three (3) biological science courses, and three (3) social science courses. All prerequisites must be taken for a letter grade and students must have a minimum 2.0 grade point average in the prerequisites. New students (freshmen and transfers) must follow the admissions process through the University of California and UC Berkeley Admissions.
Description: The Psychology Department at UC Berkeley provides a program of study that is both broad and deep, including courses in the six key areas: Behavioral and Systems Neuroscience; Clinical Science; Cognitive Neuroscience; Cognitive Psychology; Developmental Psychology; and Social-Personality Psychology. Our undergraduate program is intended to provide students with a broad exposure to the different areas within the field. Psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behavior. It is a multifaceted discipline and includes many sub-fields of study such areas as human development, sports, health, clinical, social behavior and cognitive processes.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Public Health
Requirements: To be eligible to apply for the Public Health major, students must first be admitted to UC Berkeley. The Public Health major is a high-demand, capped program, and admission is by application only. Students typically apply during their sophomore or junior year after completing specific prerequisite courses. Prerequisites include: Biology (BIOLOGY 1A & 1AL, BIOLOGY 1B), General Chemistry (CHEM 1A & 1AL), Organic Chemistry (CHEM 3A & 3AL), Mathematics (MATH 1A or 16A, MATH 1B or 16B), Statistics (STATS 2, 20, or W21), and one approved Social Science course. A minimum GPA of 2.0 is required for eligibility, and the application includes a personal statement.
Description: Public health is a multi-disciplinary field that focuses on health and disease at the population level. The curriculum for the public health major is designed to provide students with a broad introduction to the field of public health, as well as to the social and behavioral sciences, the biological sciences, and the quantitative sciences (e.g., biostatistics and epidemiology). The program also provides students with the opportunity to explore more specific areas of public health through elective coursework.
Accredidation: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies, applicants must follow the general University of California undergraduate admission requirements. This includes completing the UC application with Personal Insight Questions and meeting the A-G course requirements. Specifically for the Religious Studies major, students must complete three lower-division prerequisite courses (Religious Studies 90A, 90B, and one additional lower-division course) with a minimum GPA of 2.0 to declare the major. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission.
Description: The Religious Studies major is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide students with a broad and deep understanding of the diverse religious traditions of the world and the various ways in which religion has shaped human history, culture, and society. The curriculum is flexible, allowing students to focus on a particular religious tradition, geographical area, or thematic interest. Religious Studies students develop skills in critical thinking, cross-cultural analysis, and research that prepare them for a variety of careers and further academic study. The program provides an interdisciplinary and cross-cultural approach to the study of religion, drawing on a wide variety of academic disciplines—including history, philosophy, literature, anthropology, sociology, and art history—to provide a comprehensive understanding of religion as a human phenomenon.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Rhetoric
Requirements: To declare the Rhetoric major, students must have: Completed the L&S Reading and Composition requirement (Part A and Part B); Completed Rhetoric 10 or Rhetoric 20 with a grade of C or better; A minimum GPA of 2.0. For general admission to the University of California, Berkeley, freshman applicants must complete the A-G course requirements with a grade of C or better and meet minimum GPA requirements (3.0 for California residents and 3.4 for non-residents).
Concentration: History and Theory of Rhetoric, Public Discourse, Narrative and Image
Description: The rhetoric major offers a course of study that is at once highly focused and broadly inclusive. It is focused on the analysis and practice of discourse in its varied forms: persuasive, polemical, instructive, and aesthetic. It is inclusive because rhetorical study concerns the relation of discourse to all the conditions of human experience: the historical and the contemporary; the material and the intellectual; the social and the political; the legal and the literary. The study of rhetoric provides the student with the critical and analytical tools for understanding the ways in which various kinds of discourse—public and private, historical and contemporary—are generated, how they work, and what they do. Rhetoric as a mode of inquiry is interested in the ways in which meanings are produced and products are given meaning.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based prizes and awards

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Scandinavian
Requirements: To declare the Scandinavian major, students must have completed at least one semester of Scandinavian 1, 2, 3, or 4 (or equivalent) with a grade of C or better. Students must also meet with the Undergraduate Adviser to review requirements and fill out a Major Declaration form. Undergraduate applicants must also satisfy the University of California admission requirements, which include the completion of 15 year-long A-G courses with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) and the submission of Personal Insight Questions.
Concentration: Concentration 1: Literature/Culture/History, Concentration 2: Language/Linguistics, Concentration 3: Old Norse
Description: The undergraduate major in Scandinavian is designed to give students a high degree of proficiency in the modern languages (Danish, Norwegian, or Swedish), and a solid background in the literature, culture, and history of Scandinavia from the medieval period to the present. In addition, the department offers a major concentration in Old Norse studies. The department’s offerings also include a range of courses in English translation on such topics as Scandinavian folklore, Viking-age culture, Northern European mythology, film, and the works of Hans Christian Andersen, Søren Kierkegaard, Henrik Ibsen, August Strindberg, and Ingmar Bergman.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Slavic Languages and Literatures
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California’s basic admission requirements: completion of 15 year-long 'a-g' subject courses with a grade of C or better (including history, English, mathematics, science, a language other than English, and visual and performing arts), and a minimum GPA of 3.00 (3.40 for non-residents) in 'a-g' courses. The application process includes the UC application and answering Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores in the admissions process.
Concentration: Russian, East European/Eurasian, West Slavic
Description: The Department of Slavic Languages and Literatures offers a major in Slavic Languages and Literatures with concentrations in: Russian, East European/Eurasian, or West Slavic. The department's faculty specialize in several areas, including Russian literature and culture of all periods; Polish, Czech, and South Slavic literatures and cultures; Slavic and East European linguistics; and Armenian studies. The major is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the language, literature, and culture of their chosen area of concentration, while also offering opportunities for broader study across the Slavic world and beyond.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Social Welfare
Requirements: Prospective applicants must complete all lower-division prerequisites with a letter grade of C or higher, and have a minimum overall UC GPA of 2.0. Admission to the Social Welfare major is based on completion of all prerequisite courses and a review of the student's personal statement and overall academic record. Prerequisites include: Introductory Social Work (SOCWEL 10), Introductory Psychology (PSYCH 1 or PSYCH W1), Introductory Sociology (SOCIOL 1, SOCIOL 3 or SOCIOL 3AC), and Introductory Statistics (STAT 2, STAT 20, STAT W21, or STAT C8/DATA C8).
Description: Social Welfare is a liberal arts major designed for students who want to study the history, structure, and functions of social welfare as a social institution and who want to study the profession of social work as it is practiced in a variety of settings. The major is designed for students with three different types of goals: those who wish to prepare for graduate study in social work; those who wish to enter the labor market in a social service position after graduation; and those who want to use their study of social welfare to help them become more informed citizens and to provide a basis for future graduate study in another field. The curriculum focuses on social welfare as an institution, social work as a profession, and on the perspectives of social science as they apply to the study of social welfare. Courses are selected from several social science departments.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Society and Environment
Requirements: To be considered for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California's minimum requirements: completion of 15 year-long 'a-g' courses with a grade of C or better, and a minimum 3.00 GPA (3.40 for non-residents) in those courses. Berkeley is test-free, meaning it does not use SAT or ACT test scores in the application process. Applicants must complete the UC Application, which includes Personal Insight Questions.
Concentration: U.S. Environmental Policy and Management; Global Environmental Politics; Justice and Sustainability
Description: The Society and Environment (S&E) major introduces students to the main approaches and theory for understanding the relationship between society and the environment. Environmental problems are the result of many factors: political, economic, social, and cultural, as well as biological and physical. Developing solutions requires an understanding of the intersection of all these areas. Students in S&E choose one of three concentrations: 1. U.S. Environmental Policy and Management, 2. Global Environmental Politics, 3. Justice and Sustainability.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Sociology
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, students must meet the University of California's general admission requirements. For freshman applicants, this includes completing the 15 required 'a-g' subject courses with a grade of C or better and earning a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Transfer applicants must complete 60 semester (90 quarter) units of transferable college credit with a minimum GPA of 2.4 (2.8 for non-residents). Specifically for the Sociology major, which is housed in the College of Letters and Science, students apply to the college first. Sociology is currently designated as a high-demand major, meaning students should indicate Sociology as their primary major on their UC application to be considered for guaranteed placement in the major.
Description: Sociology is the study of social life, social change, and the social causes and consequences of human behavior. Sociologists investigate the structure of groups, organizations, and societies, and how people interact within these contexts. Since all human behavior is social, the subject matter of sociology ranges from the intimate family to the hostile mob; from organized crime to religious cults; from the divisions of race, gender and social class to the shared beliefs of a common culture; and from the sociology of work to the sociology of sports. In fact, few fields have such broad scope and relevance for research, theory, and application of knowledge. Sociology provides many distinctive perspectives on the world, generating new ideas and critiquing the old. The field also offers a range of research techniques that can be applied to virtually any aspect of social life: street-corner interviewing, focused case studies, clinical analysis of census data, survey research, historical analysis, and computer simulation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in South & Southeast Asian Studies
Requirements: Applicants must meet the University of California's general undergraduate admission requirements. For freshman applicants, this includes the completion of 15 'A-G' subject requirements with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Transfer applicants must complete 60 semester (90 quarter) units of UC-transferable college credit with a minimum GPA of 2.4 (2.8 for non-residents). To declare the South & Southeast Asian Studies major, students must complete lower-division prerequisites including language proficiency and core culture courses, and maintain a minimum GPA of 2.0.
Concentration: South Asian Studies, Southeast Asian Studies
Description: The Department of South & Southeast Asian Studies offers a program of instruction in the languages and civilizations of South and Southeast Asia. South Asia includes the nations of India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, and Bhutan. Southeast Asia includes the nations of Brunei, Burma (Myanmar), Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, and Vietnam. South and Southeast Asian Studies as a field involves the study of the history, society, culture, religion, and literature of these two regions.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Spanish & Portuguese
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, students must meet the University of California’s admission requirements: complete 15 year-long 'a-g' subject courses with a grade of C or better (11 of which must be completed prior to the senior year), and earn a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.00 (3.40 for non-residents) in these courses. Applicants must also submit the UC application and answer the Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores in the selection process.
Concentration: Spanish, Portuguese, Spanish & Portuguese, or Hispanic Languages, Linguistics, and Literatures
Description: The Department of Spanish & Portuguese offers a diverse curriculum that includes the language, literature, and cultures of the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking worlds. Our programs emphasize linguistic proficiency, critical thinking, and a deep understanding of the historical and cultural contexts of these regions. Students who major in Spanish and Portuguese can choose from four different tracks: Spanish, Portuguese, Spanish & Portuguese, or Hispanic Languages, Linguistics, and Literatures.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Statistics
Requirements: To declare the Statistics major, students must complete the following 5 prerequisite courses: Math 1A (Calculus), Math 1B (Calculus), Math 53 (Multivariable Calculus), Math 54, 56, or 110 (Linear Algebra), and Stat 20, Stat W21, or Stat 28 (Introductory Statistics). To declare the Statistics major, you must have a minimum grade of C in each prerequisite course and a minimum overall GPA of 2.0 in the prerequisites. For freshman admission to the University of California, Berkeley, applicants must meet the University of California minimum requirements: completion of 15 college-preparatory (A-G) courses with a C or better, a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents), and completion of the Personal Insight Questions.
Description: Statistics is the science of learning from data. It is a discipline that is concerned with the collection, analysis, and interpretation of data, as well as the effective communication and presentation of results relying on data. Statistics is a field that is vital to many other disciplines, including the biological and social sciences, medicine, engineering, business, and public policy. The Statistics major at UC Berkeley is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the theory and practice of statistics. The program includes coursework in calculus, linear algebra, probability, and statistical theory, as well as courses in statistical methods and data analysis. Students also have the opportunity to take advanced courses in areas such as machine learning, stochastic processes, and high-dimensional data analysis. The Statistics major prepares students for graduate study in statistics or related fields, as well as for careers in a wide range of industries, including finance, technology, healthcare, and government.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Sustainable Environmental Design
Requirements: Prospective students must complete the University of California’s online application. UC Berkeley is test-free, meaning it will not use SAT or ACT test scores in its review process. Applicants must fulfill the University of California's basic admission requirements, including the completion of 'a-g' course requirements with a minimum GPA, and must respond to four Personal Insight Questions (PIQs). For transfer students, completion of specific lower-division prerequisites and the IGETC or UC Seven-Course Pattern is required.
Description: The Sustainable Environmental Design (SED) major is the College of Environmental Design’s newest undergraduate program. It is designed for students who are passionate about the sustainable design of the built environment at all scales: from the building and the neighborhood to the city and the region. The major offers a holistic, critical approach to urban sustainability, integrating perspectives from the environmental sciences, the social sciences, and the design disciplines. Through a combination of design studios, lecture courses, and seminars, students learn to analyze and design urban environments that are more resource-efficient, resilient, and equitable. The curriculum combines studio-based design courses with courses in urban theory, environmental science, and technology. As a result, SED students are prepared to address some of the most pressing environmental and social challenges facing our cities and regions today.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Theater and Performance Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UC Berkeley, applicants must meet the following minimum requirements: Completion of 15 year-long college-preparatory courses (A-G subjects) with a grade of C or better, including 2 years of History, 4 years of English, 3 years of Mathematics, 2 years of Science, 2 years of a Language other than English, 1 year of Visual and Performing Arts, and 1 year of a College-preparatory elective. Applicants must earn a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) in these courses. Additionally, students must submit the UC application including Personal Insight Questions.
Description: The Department of Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies (TDPS) teaches performance as a mode of critical inquiry, creative expression, and public engagement. In TDPS, performance is an interdisciplinary field that includes theater, dance, and performance studies. We offer a wide range of courses in acting, directing, choreography, design, technical theater, performance theory, history, and literature. Our goal is to provide students with a rigorous and diverse education that prepares them for a variety of careers in the arts and beyond. The curriculum is designed to foster creativity, critical thinking, and collaboration, and to encourage students to explore the intersections of performance, culture, and society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Urban Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Urban Studies, applicants must meet the University of California’s general freshman or transfer admission requirements. For freshman, this includes completion of 15 year-long 'a-g' subject pattern courses with a grade of C or better (including history, English, mathematics, science, and foreign language) and a minimum GPA of 3.0 for California residents or 3.4 for non-residents. Applicants must complete the UC application, including the Personal Insight Questions. UC Berkeley is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission. Once admitted to the College of Environmental Design, students must complete lower-division requirements including ENV DES 1, ENV DES 4, and CY PLAN 110.
Description: The Urban Studies major at the University of California, Berkeley, seeks to provide students with a broad understanding of the social, political, economic, and physical aspects of cities and urban life. The major is designed to prepare students for careers in public service, urban planning, law, and business, as well as for graduate study in these and related fields. Urban Studies is an interdisciplinary program that draws from a variety of disciplines to understand the complex nature of cities. Students take courses in city planning, architecture, landscape architecture, and environmental design, as well as in the social sciences and humanities. The major emphasizes the study of urban issues from a variety of perspectives, including historical, theoretical, and practical. The major seeks to introduce students to the following bodies of knowledge: historical and contemporary analysis of American and international urbanization, urbanism, and urban design and planning; the social, economic, and political factors that shape cities and metropolitan areas; the physical form of cities and its relationship to the environment; methods for analyzing and understanding urban processes and issues; and the various ways that planners, designers, and others have intervened in cities to address social and environmental problems.
